speaker: Basim
en: A request for help from Murjana, the daughter of Ali Baba. A trader, rich beyond measure. What could the daughter of a famed merchant want? It says to meet her outside the gates of Baghdad.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Murjana? I hear she is formidable with a sword. Some say she dances with them in battle.

speaker: Murjana
en: Do you take me for a dog's ass? These apples were selling at half the price yesterday!

speaker: Civilian
en: Yesterday is yesterday, no? Do you think coin rains freely from the skies? I have people to feed!

speaker: Murjana
en: There needs to be balance in the market, any respectable merchant knows that. If my father sees this...

speaker: Basim
en: Murjana, daughter of Ali Baba?

speaker: Murjana
en: Who asks?

speaker: Basim
en: Call me Basim. We received your letter back the bureau.

speaker: Murjana
en: Ah, the Hidden Ones, yes! Well if I waited any longer, camels would have sprouted wings on their humps. We can skip the prattle. Come, time is running and so shall we.

speaker: Basim
en: Wait. Where are we going?

speaker: Murjana
en: To find my father.

speaker: Basim
en: Wait, I have something to take care of.

speaker: Murjana
en: I do not have long to wait, Hidden One.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum (Peace be upon you), Murjana.

speaker: Murjana
en: Yalla! (Let's go)! Time is running quick, we have to hurry. Are you ready?

speaker: Basim
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Murjana
en: I prepared the horses.

speaker: Basim
en: How did you find us?

speaker: Murjana
en: One hears many things in Baghdad, especially when your father knows every trader in the city.

speaker: Basim
en: Ali Baba. In your letter you mentioned he was in danger.

speaker: Murjana
en: Without a doubt. Have you heard of the Forty Thieves?

speaker: Basim
en: The notorious bandits, led by the King of Thieves. Legend says he wields a flaming sword. The boys I grew up with would not stop talking about him. I thought it a legend, a tale told to children.

speaker: Murjana
en: My father has been involved with them. For thieves, they are surprisingly skilled at trading.

speaker: Basim
en: Your father was meeting them on their territory?

speaker: Murjana
en: A terrible idea. I have told him a thousand times not to deal with the likes of thieves, but my words are the wind. Now look where we are. Me, working with Hidden Ones to make sure he is safe.

speaker: Basim
en: You must love your father if you hired a Hidden One to play guard.

speaker: Murjana
en: We travel together, and I am the protector of his caravans. I have responsibility for his well-being... and a daughter worries. These thieves are not to be taken lightly. You are my reserve should I need aid. The plan is simple. We keep watch from afar, and should anything happen... follow my lead.

speaker: Murjana
en: We're near.

speaker: Murjana
en: Oh, no! Tuffaha! (Apple!) My father's horse! La'anakum Allah! (May God curse you all!) I'm going to tear their limbs for rats!

speaker: Basim
en: Wait, Murjana. We do not know what transpired yet.

speaker: Murjana
en: There! We need to get down there, now!

speaker: Basim
en: What happened to watching from afar?

speaker: Murjana
en: The time for watching is over! My father's life is at stake. I'm going

speaker: Basim
en: No, wait, I will take them, quietly. We are on their grounds now, it pays to practice caution.

speaker: Murjana
en: Fine! Show me how you do it, but hurry.

speaker: Thief
en: Ha-ha! You hear what he said? "We had a deal! You gave me your word!" Ha-ha!

speaker: Thief
en: Does he not know to never deal with thieves?

speaker: Basim
en: No fuss.

speaker: Basim
en: Murjana...

speaker: Murjana
en: Yes, I'm here...

speaker: Murjana
en: No!

speaker: Basim
en: Ad'u Allah an yudkhilah al-. (I pray to God that he may enter Heaven.)

speaker: Murjana
en: Thank you.

speaker: Basim
en: I do not believe that this is the last of the thieves. There must be more. We must go.

speaker: Murjana
en: Yes.

speaker: Murjana
en: My father is to be buried and remembered, the way it should be. Meet me at my home near the bazaar. I will make payment for your services there.

speaker: Basim
en: The guards remain on high alert. Until I change that, I should not regroup with Ali. The risk is too great.

speaker: Basim
en: Ali has gone and regrouped with the rebels. Roshan should be there by now as well.

speaker: Basim
en: This looks like the place. Now, where is Ali?

speaker: Ali
en: It was through the might of Allah that I was destined to escape from the depths of that ghastly prison and return to you all, a roaring fire in my belly and a strength renewed.

speaker: Ali
en: All credit where it is due. For this man came to my aid at my darkest hour. And from what I have heard I am not the only one.

speaker: Ali
en: I will pay a great tribute to you in a chronicle of our exploits. But we must first write the end of it. Come.

speaker: Basim
en: I see you two have met.

speaker: Ali
en: Only briefly. But the night is young and there is much to discuss. About what you can procure for me.

speaker: Roshan
en: Our means are limited, but rest assured I will listen to your needs, Ali. Later.

speaker: Roshan
en: Share what you know about Al-Ghul so that Basim may do what he's come here to do.

speaker: Ali
en: Yes, yes, yes... Your affairs before mine. But just this once.

speaker: Ali
en: Al-Ghul sends orders to the prison guards detailing where to dig around Baghdad. But it's not just prisoners he's using.

speaker: Basim
en: There is a promissory note for workers here. It looks like Al-Ghul arranges to purchase migrant laborers as well.

speaker: Roshan
en: Who in Baghdad could make those sorts of arrangements without raising suspicion?

speaker: Ali
en: There is but one man. Mas'ood Al-Ya'qoob. He runs Baghdad's soap mills. Finds paying work for foreign settlers. Most of them Persian.

speaker: Roshan
en: So he forces these laborers into working his dig sites, all under the guise of providing them with a livelihood.

speaker: Ali
en: Beshi!

speaker: Basim
en: He tracked down one of Al-Ghul's dig sites. Posed as a prisoner. What happened?

speaker: Beshi
en: The search turned up nothing. But that did not stop the guards from trying to silence us. I cracked one's skull and fled. I doubt the others were as lucky.

speaker: Ali
en: A foolish thing to do with nothing to show for it.

speaker: Beshi
en: Not nothing. Al-Ghul will be at the caravanserai. I overheard the guards talking.

speaker: Basim
en: Of course... Merchants from all over stop there to rest. If Mas'ood is buying migrant workers, it is likely the caravanserai is where he conducts his affairs. What does he look like?

speaker: Ali
en: He is a large man. Favors adornments like jewels and silks from the East.

speaker: Roshan
en: Then he will be hard to miss. It is time, Basim.

speaker: Ali
en: What is your plan?

speaker: Roshan
en: That will be for Basim to decide.

speaker: Ali
en: Basim? Alone? No, let me gather some men

speaker: Roshan
en: And allow for foolish spectacle? Your day to display your prowess will come. But this day belongs to Basim.

speaker: Roshan
en: Consider it part of our agreement. Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: I need a moment to reflect.

speaker: Roshan
en: Understood, but be quick. This is not an opportunity we can squander.

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim. Have you gathered yourself?

speaker: Basim
en: I am ready.

speaker: Roshan
en: Then walk with me.

speaker: Roshan
en: Our prodigal Hidden One returns.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Finally, you found the path back. What do you have for us?

speaker: Basim
en: The one we are looking for is a (foreigner), someone out of Baghdad.

speaker: Rebekah
en: You are certain?

speaker: Basim
en: I found proof. They were working with the Tax Collector and the Harbormaster. One used the guards to harass and extort coin from the dhimmiyun (foreigners), the other seized goods at the docks.

speaker: Roshan
en: Extortion, I understand... but seizing goods? More objects from these ancient beings they worship?

speaker: Basim
en: They are looking for a rare hairpin, imported from the East Road. It will be up for auction at the Da'irat Al-mal.

speaker: Rebekah
en: An official invitation into the auction. Now, we have a way in. Well done.

speaker: Roshan
en: Our target has to be someone connected to both Al-Anqa and Al-Kullulu. Someone working closely with the officials.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Informers heard whispers of the Caliph's Treasurer. In recent times they have been quite involved in the businesses of Karkh.

speaker: Basim
en: Someone like that will no doubt make an appearance at the Da'irat Al-mal.

speaker: Roshan
en: We should prepare, so I will scout ahead. Meet me near the souq when you're ready.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Not a lot is known about this person. Underestimating your opponent is a fool's folly.

speaker: Basim
en: Worried? I will tread carefully.

speaker: Roshan
en: The plan is simple. Enter the auction as a merchant, wishing to bid on exotic artifacts. We know they want the hairpin, and we know they will be at the auction. They already let it slip through their fingers once.

speaker: Basim
en: When the hairpin appears, I will watch the crowd and make sure to obtain it. That will secure a meeting with this Treasurer.

speaker: Roshan
en: I am fully confident they will bid on it, whatever the cost.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes. I will gather as much information as I can about this Treasurer before the auction starts.

speaker: Roshan
en: For someone in their position, there will be no lack of whispers.

speaker: Roshan
en: The first feather without a head. It is your duty to find the right one. Do not let yourself get distracted. Focus on the mission at hand. It does no one good to linger on things that do not exist. This is real.

speaker: Basim
en: I understand.

speaker: Roshan
en: Silence is better for the wise, and how much more so for fools. Hazzan muwaffaqan. (Good luck).

speaker: Basim
en: Do you think we need luck?

speaker: Basim
en: There is a rot in Karkh, Treasurer. Property stolen. Merchants extorted. Foreigners tormented. Corruption is rank, and everywhere... but you are at its heart. Even now, your poison spreads along the East Road to lands untouched by the Order's venom. I hear you hunger for a hairpin, one up for auction at the Da'irat Al-mal. I will play the rival for your heart's desire and draw you from the shadows.

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim! How did you fare?

speaker: Rebekah
en: The streets are alive with talk about the auction.

speaker: Basim
en: Rumors spread quickly... It was this woman. Ning.

speaker: Roshan
en: A woman holding the reins. She must have angered many.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Angered and enthralled, in equal parts. It is no wonder she kept her identity hushed.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Now the upper echelons of affluent louts are soiling their silk robes, wondering if they are next.

speaker: Roshan
en: The Order will not stop here. If they have reached the East then there is no telling how far they will spread.

speaker: Roshan
en: Did you see it? The jinni...?

speaker: Basim
en: It... it is gone now. It is gone.

speaker: Roshan
en: Rest while you can. Our work is not done yet.

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim ibn Is'haq.

speaker: Basim
en: How did you find this place?

speaker: Nehal
en: Easy. I just followed the trails of blood.

speaker: Basim
en: You should not be here.

speaker: Nehal
en: Do you talk to him?

speaker: Basim
en: Sometimes. Yes.

speaker: Nehal
en: But he does not answer. I do. We have drifted apart since... since that day. But what we have seen, back at the palace... This light. These sounds. You cannot have possibly forgotten.

speaker: Basim
en: Unlike you, Nehal, I keep the past in the past.

speaker: Nehal
en: You call yesterday the past? And this jinni of yours, this repulsive shadow that crushes your chest... has it crawled back into the past too?

speaker: Basim
en: No, it is still here. Sometimes, even in the day, I feel its breath on my neck. The nightmare invades the real world. Or has always been part of it.

speaker: Nehal
en: This is part of your reality, Basim. I am a part of your reality too. I'm your past. Tell me... will you leave me there? In the dark corners of your memory?

speaker: Basim
en: I will not.

speaker: Tabid
en: Now if you could invent a mechanical rug-sweeper... Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: It is done.

speaker: Tabid
en: And how did it all play out?

speaker: Basim
en: I am afraid this is a tale for another day. We will save it for one of our campfires.

speaker: Tabid
en: You have done well, my friend.

speaker: Ahmad
en: Better get back to my work. You know how easily I get bored. Thank you for what you did, Basim.

speaker: Tabid
en: It is the truth, you have done well. One last thing. Arib? Was she... involved?

speaker: Basim
en: Not that I know, but we must remain vigilant.

speaker: Al-Mahani
en: Oh please, not yet, not yet! The pain is unbearable!

speaker: Al-Mahani
en: My heart, ya sadeeqi, it fails me.

speaker: Basim
en: Let me find you some help. Perhaps there is a doctor I can take you to?

speaker: Al-Mahani
en: Too late ... yet there are still many things I must do. My life's work, a treatise upon the heavenly stars... I must get it to the House of Wisdom before my rivals claim it and steal my glory!

speaker: Basim
en: If you wish, I can deliver the treatise for you?

speaker: Al-Mahani
en: And then ... there is my beloved son. Today, he and I argued. Most bitterly... Without his forgiveness, I cannot...

speaker: Basim
en: I will fetch him so that you can make your peace.

speaker: Al-Mahani
en: No, the treatise first! Help me retrieve it. Please!

speaker: Basim
en: I shall do so. My father was an architect. He too had his glory stolen by a rival.

speaker: Al-Mahani
en: Ah! My heart!

speaker: Basim
en: Sit. I will find the treatise.

speaker: Al-Mahani
en: It has ... three pages, each separate from the others... Please find them for me.

speaker: Basim
en: The wind is picking up.

speaker: Basim
en: Its profundity weights heavily on my hands.

speaker: Basim
en: There you are.

speaker: Basim
en: These numbers are beyond my understanding. That is all of them. I must return to the astronomer.

speaker: Basim
en: Ahsan Allahu 'aza'akum. (May God console you.)

speaker: Basim
en: A momentary friend. I retrieved your father's treatise and now I offer it to you. He said it was his life's work.

speaker: Basim
en: Those were his words, yes.

speaker: Basim
en: He love you. Truly he did ... but it was the treatise that mattered most to him.

speaker: Basim
en: He begged me to seek you out ... but I ignored him, and chose to secure the treatise for the sake of posterity.

speaker: Basim
en: A new day. Another test. I should get back.

speaker: Basim
en: Alamut Fortress takes my breath away... as if it leaped out of the hikayat (stories) I heard when I was a child.

speaker: Roshan
en: If you do not have faith in yourself, then who will?

speaker: Roshan
en: There you are. Are you ready?

speaker: Basim
en: I... I think so.

speaker: Roshan
en: Put yesterday out of your mind. It has no bearing on today.

speaker: Roshan
en: Get dressed and we can begin.

speaker: Roshan
en: Go on, Basim. Like we practiced.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes, master.

speaker: Novice 1
en: You look strong today, Basim! Keep training!

speaker: Basim
en: Steady, Basim. Steady.

speaker: Roshan
en: Leap! Now!

speaker: Basim
en: Yes, master!

speaker: Roshan
en: I've seen enough. We will try again tomorrow.

speaker: Basim
en: I felt fine.

speaker: Roshan
en: I can see it in your body. You lose focus too easy. The Leap of Faith is a crucial step on your path to initiation. It is one of the Brotherhood's first and most sacred rites. To perform it successfully, you must first center your mind, body and spirit. Embrace the fear. Quiet it. Find the stillness. And let go.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes, Master.

speaker: Roshan
en: Let's return to the camp.

speaker: Basim
en: May I ask you something?

speaker: Roshan
en: You may.

speaker: Basim
en: Back in Anbar, at the palace, I witnessed a meeting between the Caliph and five masked men. Order members. The Caliph was meant to protect the object they discovered, but he knew nothing of their plans for it. He did not even know them by name. How does the most powerful man in Baghdad bend such a fearful knee to the faceless?

speaker: Roshan
en: The Order has held dominion over such men and their empires for centuries. By convincing them of their truth, that they are the natural arbiters of the world. The Caliph was but their puppet, and the same will be true of whomever succeeds him. The entire Caliphate is under their influence.

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim, speak with Fuladh and see if he needs help. We will continue your training later.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes, master.

speaker: Roshan
en: Have you seen Mentor Rayhan in camp?

speaker: Hidden One 1
en: He is preparing to receive the Tahirid emissary, master.

speaker: Roshan
en: Thank you.

speaker: Basim
en: Good day, Tabid!

speaker: Tabid
en: Hello, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: What troubles you?

speaker: Tabid
en: Truthfully, I am frustrated. The Order has only grown stronger in Baghdad since the death of the Caliph. And we are stuck on this mountain.

speaker: Basim
en: Mentor Rayhan surely knows what he is doing...

speaker: Tabid
en: Maybe I should trust more.

speaker: Basim
en: Have you seen Fuladh?

speaker: Tabid
en: Probably at his office, as usual? Anyways, I must get back to work.

speaker: Basim
en: Araka Lahiqan! (See you later!)

speaker: Basim
en: How is Nur, the brave eagle?

speaker: Nur
en: Will he fall or will he soar?

speaker: Basim
en: You will soar, ya sadeeqi (my friend)! Insha' Allah! (If God wills it!)

speaker: Nur
en: Thank you. We have a similar spirit, you know?

speaker: Basim
en: What gave you that idea?

speaker: Nur
en: One of the Banu Musa was angry at you and you were unfazed. Remember?

speaker: Basim
en: I did not touch his hammer.

speaker: Nur
en: You refused to apologize for something you did not do. I respect that. Stubborn like me!

speaker: Basim
en: I have been called worse.

speaker: Basim
en: Have you seen Fuladh in camp?

speaker: Nur
en: I have seen him speaking to Ahmad near his office.

speaker: Basim
en: Araka Lahiqan! (See you later!)

speaker: Basim
en: How are these fine animals, ya khaiyal (horse-keeper)?

speaker: Horseman
en: Hale and healthy!

speaker: Basim
en: Are they native to this area?

speaker: Horseman
en: They came with us ten years ago, when we set up our camp. Zul-Janah was born here.

speaker: Basim
en: She is a beautiful horse. Thank you for introducing us.

speaker: Horseman
en: Take care, ya sadeeqi (my friend)!

speaker: Fuladh
en: I may get back to you on this.

speaker: Ahmad
en: Of course!

speaker: Fuladh
en: Ah, what is this in the corner ... here? A small design?

speaker: Ahmad
en: It is my signature. So you know that I created this and not Al-Hasan or worse, Abu Jafar!

speaker: Ahmad
en: I jest, you understand? Wada'an! (Farewell!)

speaker: Fuladh
en: Ah, Basim. How are you?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Yes, Enkidu! Food is coming! He is intelligent. And intelligence is supposed to rhyme with patience!

speaker: Fuladh
en: Reminds me of someone...

speaker: Basim
en: Have you been speaking to Master Roshan?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Have patience... Be kind to your progress.

speaker: Basim
en: I will take this to heart. Roshan asked me to come see you?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Ah, yes! Rebekah needs leather strips. Can you fetch those from the store-room?

speaker: Basim
en: I shall, Fuladh.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Araka Lahiqan! (See you later!)

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum. (Peace be upon you.) What is this thing you work on?

speaker: Ahmad
en: Huh? Oh, um... it is a type of grab-dredge.

speaker: Basim
en: How does it work, Abu Jafar?

speaker: Ahmad
en: Ahmad.

speaker: Basim
en: Ahmad. Of course.

speaker: Ahmad
en: Hmm, maybe I am thinking about this backwards and I can... hmm...

speaker: Basim
en: I will let you continue your work.

speaker: Ahmad
en: Yes, yes. Fine.

speaker: Basim
en: Rebekah needs leather strips from the camp's store-house. I must find those for her.

speaker: Novice 2
en: As-salamu 'alaikum (Peace be upon you), Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: That is not it.

speaker: Basim
en: It is hard to find anything in here.

speaker: Basim
en: No, that is not a strip of leather.

speaker: Tahirid emissary
en: These forces within the Caliphate are beginning to put pressure on us.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Forces? You mean the Order, Aban.

speaker: Tahirid emissary
en: I... can only speak of what I know, ya sadeeqi (my friend).

speaker: Tahirid emissary
en: The Caliph wishes to nullify the rebels and if you persist in giving them support... we cannot assure you protection from any... Caliphate response.

speaker: Rayhan
en: The rebels supply us with information in Baghdad. Without them, we are blind.

speaker: Tahirid emissary
en: Be that as it may, Governor Muhammad is very committed to showing that he can end this rebellion swiftly.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Huh, I do not doubt that.

speaker: Tahirid emissary
en: I came to warn you. Things are moving fast in Baghdad. You may have to act sooner than expected.

speaker: Rayhan
en: I hear you, Aban.

speaker: Basim
en: So the Tahirids who govern these lands are the only thing standing between Alamut and a full scale attack. A fragile peace. How long will it last?

speaker: Basim
en: How does construction go?

speaker: Worker 1
en: Ah, it is taking longer than we expected, ya sayyidi (sir).

speaker: Basim.
en: That must be frustrating.

speaker: Worker 1
en: Uh, Mentor Rayhan is a wise man but he speaks of this as if it was destined that we build here. We have patience and follow his guidance.

speaker: Basim
en: Master Roshan tells me I must not be in a hurry to rush back to Madinat as-Salam (The City of Peace).

speaker: Worker 1
en: I would not hurry at all. Baghdad is... different now. It is very dangerous.

speaker: Basim
en: Rebekah?

speaker: Rebekah
en: Basim, Basim... are you just wandering the camp aimlessly now?

speaker: Basim
en: No, I have this leather for you. Will it do?

speaker: Rebekah
en: Apparently, you've moved past the wooden swords. I protested, but Roshan insisted.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Here is your dagger.

speaker: Rebekah
en: And your sword. I am proud to have worked on them.

speaker: Basim
en: This blade has character!

speaker: Rebekah
en: Why would I make anything less than unique?

speaker: Basim
en: I am in your debt. I was not expecting new weapons today!

speaker: Rebekah
en: Repay me by using them on the Order. Make them feel the sharpness of its character!

speaker: Rebekah
en: Roshan said you had further training today? Show her that new sword of yours!

speaker: Basim
en: I look forward to it!

speaker: Novice 3
en: Blessings upon you, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: How does training go, ya sadeeqi (my friend)?

speaker: Novice 3
en: Nur showed me a new way to grip my knife and it has improved my accuracy greatly! If you throw it just so, it sails through the air swift and true!

speaker: Basim
en: Shall I remind you how to use a knife?

speaker: Novice 3
en: Ya ilahi! (My God!) Well done!

speaker: Novice 3
en: You have inspired me to train harder!

speaker: Basim
en: This is the way, ya sadeeqi (my friend)!

speaker: Hidden One 2
en: You cannot enter. It is forbidden.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum, ya sadeeqi. (Peace be upon you, my friend.)

speaker: Worker 2
en: 'Wa 'alaikum as-salam! (And peace be upon you!) Did Fuladh send you?

speaker: Basim
en: No, he did not.

speaker: Worker 2
en: Then you're not here to help move these rocks?

speaker: Basim
en: I am quite sure that was not me.

speaker: Worker 2
en: I do not mean to be rude but I have no time to talk. I must figure this out.

speaker: Basim
en: I will leave you to it, then.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum, ya sayyidi. (Peace be upon you, sir.)

speaker: Worker 3
en: Wa 'alaikum as-salam! (And peace be upon you!)

speaker: Basim
en: I was out in the mountains earlier and the sight of Fortress Alamut filled me with awe.

speaker: Worker 3
en: Mentor Rayhan told us to take inspiration from nests the eagles construct in the Alamut peaks.

speaker: Basim
en: I can see the influence. Wada'an. (Farewell.)

speaker: Worker 3
en: Rafaqaka Allah! (May God accompany you!)

speaker: Roshan
en: Good work. Until tomorrow.

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim. Time for combat training.

speaker: Basim
en: I was surprised when Rebekah handed me this. Is a sword not a coarse weapon for a Hidden One?

speaker: Roshan
en: As Hidden Ones, we must become proficient with a number of weapons. You never know how a fight will escalate. Anyone can wield a sword. But how will you use it?

speaker: Basim
en: I am here to learn that, master.

speaker: Roshan
en: Are you truly here?

speaker: Basim
en: Well... yes. I believe so.

speaker: Roshan
en: You are here in body but are you here in mind and soul?

speaker: Basim
en: Is this... a riddle?

speaker: Roshan
en: No. It is the difference between life and death.

speaker: Roshan
en: Make sure you target and circle around me. Never turn your back on your opponent.

speaker: Roshan
en: What are you doing? Are you trying to get stabbed in the back?

speaker: Roshan
en: Yes, better! Show me your quick stabs first.

speaker: Roshan
en: Good. Yes. Excelent!

speaker: Roshan
en: There are times when we must put more force into our attacks to cause more damage. It will leave you exposed, so time it properly! Now go!

speaker: Roshan
en: I'm waiting for you.

speaker: Roshan
en: That's it! Come in strong! Excellent!

speaker: Roshan
en: Now, for defense. You can parry the attacks of your opponent. After a few sucessful parries your opponent will be stunned. Try to parry my attacks.

speaker: Roshan
en: Yes. That's good. Excellent!

speaker: Roshan
en: Some attacks cannot be parried, and must be dodged instead. Prepare yourself!

speaker: Roshan
en: Good work. That's the way. Well done.

speaker: Roshan
en: Now, let us try a free fight together. Use what you've learned.

speaker: Roshan
en: That took me by surprise. Well done.

speaker: Roshan
en: Hey, wake up! Bring your head back to right now.

speaker: Basim
en: Agh! Take that!

speaker: Roshan
en: Where did that come from?

speaker: Roshan
en: We are done for today, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: Why must we stop? I learn nothing from failing.

speaker: Roshan
en: True learning requires action and stillness in equal parts. You have made the action. Now, seek the stillness. Do not rush your training. Be patient. Failure is a part of progress. Think on these words and come back better.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes, master, I will.

speaker: Roshan
en: Good. See you later.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: Ahmad will soon go back to the House of Wisdom. I fear he may end in a middle of a snakes' nest.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I know how close you are to your brother. We shall learn more soon. Then we can act.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum (Peace be upon you), Abu Jafar.

speaker: Ahmad
en: It is Ahmad.

speaker: Basim
en: Ahmad. My apologies.

speaker: Ahmad
en: Do not worry. Come and warm yourself by the fire.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Our brother Ahmad is leaving us tomorrow.

speaker: Ahmad
en: To Baghdad. The House of Wisdom.

speaker: Basim
en: The House of Wisdom?

speaker: Ahmad
en: We have been working there, my brothers and I, for years. I still have some things to work on. Science waits for no one. And I will fulfill my duty as a Hidden One by becoming your eyes and ears among the scholars.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Fuladh, tell Basim the story of the feather...

speaker: Fuladh
en: Our tradition of the feather comes from Egypt. They represent the feathers of Ma'at. The feathers of the heron were dipped in the blood of the targets. These would be left for the Lord of the Duat to judge. It is important we remain humble and know our place in the process. We are messengers of justice and not the final judges.

speaker: Nur
en: Will anyone help me on patrol tonight?

speaker: Basim
en: I will come with you, Nur. I must get my body moving if I am to warm up tonight.

speaker: Nur
en: I am grateful. Let us go.

speaker: Nur
en: Are you coming, Basim? Leave the stories for later!

speaker: Rebekah
en: We have not had a messenger from Samarra in quite a while.

speaker: Tabid
en: You are from there, yes?

speaker: Rebekah
en: From a small village on the outskirts. My father owns a sandals workshop. I grew up watching him at work. (missing dialogue)

speaker: Nur
en: Get on!

speaker: Basim
en: May I speak to you in confidence?

speaker: Nur
en: You know you can.

speaker: Basim
en: I overheard Mentor Rayhan speaking to an emissary earlier... Mentor Rayhan asked if we may come under attack for dealing with rebels in Baghdad. Are we safe here in Alamut?

speaker: Nur
en: I do not know... but I pity the people who attack this nest of eagles!

speaker: Nur
en: How goes the watch?

speaker: Sentinel
en: Nothing happened at all on Alamut and I am so hungry. We did not make it to the main canyon.

speaker: Nur
en: Excellent. We will start there. Thank you.

speaker: Basim
en: Come, Nur. Follow me!

speaker: Nur
en: Are you looking forward to your initiation?

speaker: Basim
en: Yes. It feels like I have been preparing my whole life for this.

speaker: Nur
en: I could not sleep the night before my ceremony. From excitement and a small bit of fear, if I am to be honest.

speaker: Basim
en: We all fear the unknown, but a greater unknown awaits on the other side of initiation.

speaker: Nur
en: You speak of the Order?

speaker: Basim
en: I see them as monsters from a tale: hiding in dark corners, down dark alleys.

speaker: Nur
en: The difference is that the Order is real.

speaker: Basim
en: What do they want?

speaker: Nur
en: They want to control Baghdad. They want power.

speaker: Nur
en: This is Muhja.

speaker: Basim
en: Magnificent.

speaker: Nur
en: Soon, you shall have one of your own!

speaker: Basim
en: Fuladh introduced me to an eagle named Enkidu. He said we have much in common. And... not in a complimentary way.

speaker: Nur
en: She sees something. Follow me!

speaker: Nur
en: Shh. Quietly, Basim.

speaker: Nur
en: Find a place to hide...

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: What is this place?

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: We must be nearing their camp. We have the element of surprise.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: Be ready.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Stop making so much noise!

speaker: Nur
en: Quickly.

speaker: Basim
en: I am behind you!

speaker: Nur
en: We must strike fast!

speaker: Basim
en: Agreed!

speaker: Nur
en: We must wait for the right moment...

speaker: Nur
en: Do not make a noise...

speaker: Mercenary 3
en: You are done for! Prepare for hell!

speaker: Nur
en: Yes! Show no mercy!

speaker: Nur
en: Do not give up! Keep fighting! Remember your training!

speaker: Nur
en: Not like the wooden targets, is it?

speaker: Basim
en: It is not that.

speaker: Basim
en: This sword...

speaker: Nur
en: What of it?

speaker: Basim
en: Mercenaries from Baghdad use these weapons.

speaker: Nur
en: We must warn the others.

speaker: Nur
en: Mercenaries from Baghdad.

speaker: Roshan
en: How do you know?

speaker: Nur
en: Basim recognized the make of the sword. I believe him.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Bring him in.

speaker: Rayhan
en: How do you know these men were from Baghdad?

speaker: Basim
en: Growing up on its streets, I have seen their weapons many times... and closely.

speaker: Roshan
en: Behind every mercenary is a man who gave them their orders.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Yes, and we must act if we are to learn who that is. We will return to Baghdad, seek Ali ibn Muhammad's help.

speaker: Roshan
en: Ah, of course. Sahib az-Zanj? (Chief of the Zanj?) He is a dangerous and delusional fool.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Maybe so... but he is one of our only allies in Baghdad. We need him and we need his men.

speaker: Nur
en: I will go back to Baghdad.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Go to Ali. Find out if the Order sent those men.

speaker: Nur
en: I will.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Waffaqaka Allah. (May God grant you success.)

speaker: Basim
en: Waffaqaka Allah. (May God grant you success.)

speaker: Nur
en: Wada'an. Araka Lahiqan! (Goodbye. See you later!)

speaker: Basim
en: That is a lot of books.

speaker: Al-Jahiz
en: Do not think I am a librarian. I am a writer! Many of these are my own works. Though I do collect, it is true. This city hides ... other rare and ancient tomes. If you should find one, bring it here. I'll make it worth your time.

speaker: Al-Jahiz
en: Do you have something for me?

speaker: Basim
en: Not as yet.

speaker: Al-Jahiz
en: Perhaps next time we will both find more than idle words and disturbance!

speaker: Al-Jahiz
en: Wonderful! No need to tell anyone about all this. We wouldn't want any unfortunate accusations of plagiarism ... again.

speaker: Basim
en: I found this stange book. Does it interest you?

speaker: Al-Jahiz
en: Oh, do you know what that is? It has many names. I know it as Kitab Al-Azif, the Book of the Dead. It is death to all who read it! ...if you believe the stories. I myself do not. But it will remain on my shelves where it can do no harm ... just in case.

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim, we should keep moving.

speaker: Basim
en: I would like to look around first, if I may? Baghdad and its surroundings call to me.

speaker: Roshan
en: Very well. But do not be long. There will be much to do once we reach Harbiyah.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Look for a lattice-covered courtyard near Shari's mosque. That is where Nur was gathering his information. That is where we will be.

speaker: Basim
en: Now, where does my heart take me?

speaker: Basim
en: Such familiar sights. Greetings once again, Baghdad. Show me what I have missed.

speaker: Basim
en: I have idled long enough. Roshan and Fuladh are surely awaiting me at the Bureau.

speaker: Basim
en: So this is a Hidden Ones Bureau. I expected some sort of hovel.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Some Bureaus are. Others can be fitted with gold trim. Wherever space we settle, all that's important is that our occupancy remains a secret.

speaker: Basim
en: We certainly have that here. Have you found anything helpful?

speaker: Roshan
en: Nothing hinting at Ali's whereabouts. However, Nur was in contact with someone named Beshi. A name I recognize as one of Ali's closest allies within the rebel collective. He's a dock worker at the upper harbor. See if he's in the area. He may have something to tell us about Ali's disappearance.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I have found something!

speaker: Fuladh
en: It seems Nur mapped out this very district. Marked the factories area to the north.

speaker: Basim
en: What is there?

speaker: Roshan
en: The rebels sympathizers. If Nur visited this area for any reason, it is worth following up on.

speaker: Basim
en: Understood.

speaker: Roshan
en: These are not strong leads, but they are a start nonetheless. Fuladh and I will see what more we can uncover.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Be careful.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: What is happening? Why are the soldiers patrolling?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: There was an attack in Sharqiyah. Everyone's on edge.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Sounds like trouble. Let's go home.

speaker: Basim
en: The whole area is on high alert. I am expected.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: What's wrong with the General? He's in a panic, screaming for reinforcements we don't have.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Something that happened in Sharqiyah has him worried... More than usual, I mean.

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: Stay alert! They broke into the Officer's room. If they break in here, it is all your heads!

speaker: Basim
en: The General's balcony might be open. That is a brave move for a coward. And foolish.

speaker: Soldier
en: If you asked me, that key is trouble.

speaker: Basim
en: A key. There must be a door it opens.

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: It will be fine. I am worried for nothing. Hah, yes, I am certain. All will be well.

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: You will regret this. I am feared in battle. Have you not heard of me?

speaker: Basim
en: I heard you are a coward who steals credit for other man's bravery.

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: Guards! Double wages for the one who brings me his head! Triple!

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, there's the coward now!

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: You are nothing! Guards! Guards! A year's pay to the one who saves me!

speaker: Basim
en: Who is Al-Mardikhwar? Where is he?

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: Guards! Guards!

speaker: Basim
en: There is a note. Al-Mardikhwar had questions about our friend's past. Smart. He was ordered to a meeting at the Great Garrison.

speaker: Basim
en: One down. Now to deal with Al-A'eshma.

speaker: Basim
en: That is two down. I should return to Fuladh.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: Is that you, Basim?

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: It is all right, I know you.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: I cannot place your face, but you bear our mark.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: I am Naaji, one of Mentor Rayhan's informers. I asked for a more difficult assignment but maybe I should not have.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: Tell me the problem.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: I tracked a pair of corrupt guards to the place where they take their bribes, but I do not think I can handle both.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: Well done so far. Between us, we can finish the job. Follow my lead.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Soldier
en: Look out! We're being attacked!

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: Argh! That bastard cut me! He cut me!

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: Oh... This job has just gotten a whole lot harder.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: Oh, Basim, you... you have done it?

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: Congratulations! Your first official assignment as a Hidden One is complete!

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: I could not have done it without your help.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: Nonsense! With a little more training, you will do fine. You simply need more confidence.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: You...really think so?

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: I do. Only a rare few succeed perfectly on their first attempt. Do not give up.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: You do not have the steady nerves to follow through on your targets, but you did show intelligence in tracking them. Maybe you could still serve the Hidden Ones. Not with your blade, but with your mind.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: You mean by helping to identify and locate targets? That sort of thing?

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: Exactly! Our actions must be guided by knowledge, and some are simply better at gathering it.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: I did not think I was capable!

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: You only thought you needed my help. Maybe you do have the makings of a Hidden One.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: Thank you, Basim. I shall report back to Mentor Rahan and see what he says.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: I almost had him... I think.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: So, Naaji, it looks like everything worked out in the end.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: The Bureau agreed my talents were better suited to preparing the hunt than making the kill.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: You have a keen mind, Naaji, and the more you hone those skills, the sharper they will be.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: The Bureau was not easy to convince, but I persisted. With training, my hands will grow steady and deadly.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Basim
en: If you pursue your goal with such passion, you will surely succeed.

scene: Blade In The Crowd, Tool In The Shed
speaker: Naaji
en: Thank you for setting me on the right path, Basim. Take this as a token of my appreciation.

speaker: Ali
en: They took them in broad daylight and executed them! They will die for this, every one of them! It is time we fight!

speaker: Fuladh
en: Your anger is just, but you will not win a war, Ali.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Basim! Good, you are needed. Mercenaries have taken some rebels and executed them in the square.

speaker: Ali
en: And your Rafiq would have me hide like a rat while they hunt my men openly.

speaker: Beshi
en: We must at least return the dead to their families.

speaker: Ali
en: Do you still fear to fight these devils, Beshi?

speaker: Beshi
en: My only fear is that we become like them.

speaker: Fuladh
en: There is more to this than it seems. The Caliph would not risk war. This is the work of the Order.

speaker: Ali
en: Then I will find those responsible, and slaugther them like dogs.

speaker: Fuladh
en: The Order will find you first. It's likely they are looking for you and Beshi already. You are well known to them. Basim, however...

speaker: Basim
en: Ali, I will find who did this, and I will kill them all. You have my word.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Basim is right. Let him do this. When those responsible lie dead, you will receive the credit.

speaker: Ali
en: All right. Everyone must know it was me. I will return to Jarjaraya, but I will not wait long. I will meet you at the gate, Basim.

speaker: Beshi
en: And I will make sure the bodies are returned to their families for burial.

speaker: Fuladh
en: That might have gone badly.

speaker: Basim
en: You think this is the work of the Order?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Yes. As you know, Sharqiyah is run by Turkic mercenaries paid by the Caliph, who himself is only a puppet for the Order. Spies tell me at least one of the mercenary commanders in Sharqiyah is with them.

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me who, and I will find him.

speaker: Fuladh
en: We must tread carefully. Sharqiyah stands on a razor's edge. The rebels are armed and growing in number. They could attack at any time. A misstep here could start a war that threatens even Alamut.

speaker: Basim
en: What do you advise, Fuladh?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Go with Ali to Jarjaraya and look around. Someone there must know something.

speaker: Fuladh
en: And Basim ... work quickly. You see what is at stake.

speaker: Basim
en: I have some questions, Fuladh.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I hope I have answers for you.

speaker: Basim
en: What do the rebels want?

speaker: Fuladh
en: You yourself know well the divide between rich and poor. Many have grown tired of the injustice, and want change. In the beginning it was mostly slaves, but now tradesmen, the wealthy, and even some nobles support Ali's cause.

speaker: Basim
en: And Ali inteds to lead them in overthrowing the Abbasid Caliphate?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Ali believes the most qualified should rule, not just the wealthy or highborn. Ironically, he considers himself the most qualified, and claims descent from the Prophet's own family to support it.

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me of the Zanj.

speaker: Fuladh
en: It is a bitter story. The Zanj are peoples stolen from their homelands in the Horn of Africa, and brought here to work the fields for the wealthy.

speaker: Basim
en: So they are slaves?

speaker: Fuladh
en: They are paid, but they are not free. Like all men, they desire to be masters of their own lives.

speaker: Basim
en: What do you know about Jarjaraya?

speaker: Fuladh
en: It is a small village to the south, home to a divided population of rich and poor. Most of the Zanj are there. It has also become a refuge for those who came to Baghdad looking for work, and failed.

speaker: Basim
en: No wonder Ali has gained support there.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Yes. In few other places is the divide between those who have everything and those who have nothing so sharp.

speaker: Basim
en: What of yourself, Fuladh? How did you come to the Hidden Ones?

speaker: Fuladh
en: That is a story that should be shared around a good fire after a long meal.

speaker: Basim
en: Will you tell me nothing?

speaker: Fuladh
en: I was the child of my father's concubine. His favored wife, worried I could claim inheritance, threw us both out. I grew up in the desert alone. My friends were the animals, particularly birds. We understood each other.

speaker: Basim
en: That explains your love of eagles.

speaker: Fuladh
en: After I grew to manhood, a Hidden One saw me hunting with my birds. He brought me to the Brotherhood, and I stayed.

speaker: Basim
en: Shukran, Fuladh. That is all for now.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Alhamdulillah. (Praise be to God.)

speaker: Basim
en: Alhamdulillah. (Praise be to God.)

speaker: Fuladh
en: I am glad you are safe.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: Alhamdulillah. (Praise be to God.) A first of many achievements to come, Basim.

speaker: Roshan
en: We should only hope. There is still much work to do.

speaker: Roshan
en: While our focus was on Al-Ghul, Fuladh quietly scouted the city for where we could erect more Bureaus.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I have found dwellings in three districts that are most unassuming. Tabid and Rebekah have arrived from Alamut and set off to Al-Abbasiyah and Karkh. I will make my way to Sharqiyah shortly.

speaker: Roshan
en: And I will join Rebekah in Karkh, where corruption is as common as the arid air.

speaker: Roshan
en: See Abu Jafar about some things he's been working on, then come find us.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: Have a look, Basim. I may have something that is of interest to you.

speaker: Basim
en: Resourceful as always. My thanks, Ahmad.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: It's Abu Jaf— Ah, you jest.

speaker: Basim
en: Every now and again. Araka Lahiqan (See you later), Abu Jafar. Keep well.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: And you, Basim.

speaker: Kong
en: Lies! You reported my crate of beautiful leaves, I know it!.

speaker: Luca
en: Go away, Kong. You are old and full of fear and piss. It is sad.

speaker: Kong
en: You...!

speaker: Basim
en: What fresh brew do you have for me today, Kong?

speaker: Kong
en: No brew until Luca returns my crate! But if you have come to buy tea, I have many recommendations...

speaker: Basim
en: Kong! It is me, Basim.

speaker: Kong
en: Ni shì shuí ā? (Who are you?) Who?

speaker: Basim
en: Uh... Basim... ?

speaker: Kong
en: I am not an idiot! Everyone claims to be someone I know. Answer me this. What tea did my Basim like?

speaker: Basim
en: Ginger, with some turmeric.

speaker: Kong
en: Wrong! Basim does not like tea!

speaker: Kong
en: Wah, Basim! Little finch, look at you all dressed up! Come, come. Follow me to my stall, away from this terrible man.

speaker: Kong
en: So, little finch! What have you been up to, ah? So many years...

speaker: Basim
en: Just here and there. I... had to leave Baghdad for a while.

speaker: Kong
en: Ah, youth!

speaker: Basim
en: What about yourself, Kong? What have you been doing these years?

speaker: Kong
en: Doing what I do best. Making coin! Although with some difficulty of late. The guards are on high alert, and that Greek merchant has taken it in his stride to report me at every chance. I know it in my ripe old bones that he waits for me to die of starvation. Or worse, go out of business. Ah! But here you are, little finch. Remember the dazzling duo we used to be? How about helping a friend out, for old times!

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, just like old times. But I need to speak with you after this. There is something I need as well.

speaker: Kong
en: Of course! After you fetch my confiscated crate of beautiful leaves. It must be over there, where the guards are. Go forth!

speaker: Basim
en: Fine. But I have something to ask of you, after this.

speaker: Kong
en: Yes, yes, of course!.

speaker: Basim
en: This must be Kong's crate of tea leaves.

speaker: Basim
en: Looks like this crate is still intact. Kong will be pleased.

speaker: Kong
en: My leaves! Praise be to you, little finch!

speaker: Basim
en: Where shall I put it?

speaker: Kong
en: Come, come! Put it here.

speaker: Kong
en: Basim delivers once again! Many thanks, little finch!

speaker: Basim
en: Where are these from? India?

speaker: Kong
en: No, this is all the way from China! , my hometown, produces the best leaves! I also import leaves from India, and even Persia.

speaker: Basim
en: Moving up in the world, Kong.

speaker: Kong
en: Karkh first, then the world. I am now selling my goods at the Grand Auction. Have you heard of it?

speaker: Basim
en: The Da'irat Al-mal. Yes, I am trying to get in.

speaker: Kong
en: Why? What kind of business are you doing, little finch? Why not share it with me? We worked so well together!

speaker: Basim
en: The kind of business that could get you into big trouble. Do you think you can help me get into the auction?

speaker: Kong
en: Ah, that is my Basim, always with the secrets. But do not play around, huh? Karkh is much more dangerous now than before. The auction is very exclusive. It is not easy to get in. I can help you, little finch. But first, I have a request.

speaker: Kong
en: See, there? Blocked. The guards are stopping everything that comes in from the road and river. It is as if they are taking orders from someone higher up. These days, they do not even accept my bribes.

speaker: Basim
en: They must be looking for something. An object, or...

speaker: Kong
en: Some stupid nonsense, I do not know! But they spoil my business, that I do know! Now I just sell dumb leaf water. I hear that they keep the items in the Harbormaster's guarded warehouse, somewhere east of here...

speaker: Basim
en: Let me guess. You want me to help you free your wares in exchange for entry into the auction.

speaker: Kong
en: The warehouse is decorated with banners, around some cranes. My items for entry into the auction. Sound like a good deal?

speaker: Basim
en: Sounds like a deal.

speaker: Luca
en: Hey, you! Kong's friend. I may have something you would be interested in. Come closer.

speaker: Basim
en: What can I do for you?

speaker: Luca
en: This is about what I can do for you. Did Kong ask you to enter a warehouse?

speaker: Basim
en: Just say what you have to say.

speaker: Luca
en: That Kong is always trying his luck. Well, it's his lucky day because I happen to know where it is. All I need is something in return...

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me what you know.

speaker: Luca
en: Follow the road, cross the bridge on the right. You'll see the warehouse on your left, past the river.

speaker: Basim
en: That narrows it down. Thank you.

speaker: Basim
en: I will think about it.

speaker: Luca
en: I am here if you change your mind.

speaker: Basim
en: The warehouse. Do you know where it is?

speaker: Luca
en: Hm! Of course. My mind is as sharp as cheese. You know what I require in return...

speaker: Basim
en: The warehouse Kong mentioned. I need to find out more about this Harbormaster.

speaker: Soldier
en: Greece... India... anything out of Baghdad. If I want to keep my head, I better be sure to check them all.

speaker: Basim
en: Instruction to search any and all foreign goods... for an artifact. An ancient Chinese hairpin, specifically. This all starts at the harbor.

speaker: Soldier
en: Did you hear that Javed is in trouble? Maybe I can be the next Harbormaster.

speaker: Soldier
en: Rather you than me. Whose head do you think will roll next?

speaker: Basim
en: The Da'irat Al-mal. Ceramics, exotic wares, and rare goods. All on display.

speaker: Soldier
en: Marha! These tea leaves from the East are worth more coin than my night of work. Hmm. What if I...?

speaker: Basim
en: A list of exotic foreign goods seized. Most from out of Baghdad. There are Kong's things. Vases and some expensive tea leaves. This should be what Kong needs.

speaker: Basim
en: A strongly worded letter to the Harbormaster. He let a hairpin slip through their fingers and someone is not happy. There is a scent on this letter ... and a familiar symbol. Al-Kullulu. Looks like the Harbormaster is part of the Order. The Harbormaster has set up this blockade for foreign wares, especially for ancient artifacts from the East.

speaker: Basim
en: There is nothing more here. The Harbormaster is waiting.

speaker: Basim
en: Another wall between the people and power at play. I hope the Harbormaster is not expecting me.

speaker: Al-Kullulû
en: La'anakum Allah! (May God curse you!) One artifact, and no one can find it.

speaker: Basim
en: Kong! I have good

speaker: Kong
en: Shuí ā! (Who!) Who goes there! I have a weapon!

speaker: Basim
en: Just me.

speaker: Kong
en: Ah, the little finch returns to the nest! Empty-handed!

speaker: Basim
en: It is here. This can help you get your wares out from the harbor.

speaker: Kong
en: Hah, I never doubted you for a second! Come, let us enjoy a cup, for the memories. I will even make your favorite.

speaker: Kong
en: What did you find there? Who was behind it?

speaker: Basim
en: A man, by the name of Javed. He was working for someone, looking for an artifact. An exotic hairpin. It is important, somehow... I need to find out why. I must.

speaker: Kong
en: You have changed, little finch. Or should I just say, finch? When we last met, you were a street thief. Now... I hope you know what you are searching for. Sometimes it is best to leave the thorn in, lest you bleed dry.

speaker: Basim
en: Now, for what was promised to me?

speaker: Kong
en: An invitation to the auction. It is only given to esteemed guests. Do not ask me where I got it from, unless you want lies.

speaker: Kong
en: With that scroll you can get in without having to fit yourself in one of my boxes!

speaker: Basim
en: That was your plan?

speaker: Kong
en: Men have endured worse to reach their goals.

speaker: Basim
en: Someone influential is looking for the hairpin, but let it slip. Now the only chance they have is at the Grand Auction. Hmm...

speaker: Basim
en: Now to look into the other lead.

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim! Over here.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Hmm. You seem shorter than I remembered, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: And you still have not grown a single digit, Rebekah.

speaker: Roshan
en: Now, we're not here as enemies.

speaker: Basim
en: No, but we never held back on the training ground.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Roshan tells me you are a local here.

speaker: Basim
en: In a manner of speaking. I lived here a time before I left for Anbar.

speaker: Rebekah
en: This place is no different from the places I'm used to. The rich wipe their shit with the clothes of the poor.

speaker: Basim
en: That is the Karkh I remember.

speaker: Roshan
en: It is your Karkh no longer. Rebekah has uncovered a district tainted by corruption... stronger than usual.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Rumors of harassment from officials, and goods being controlled and seized. We think someone here has a hold over the district.

speaker: Basim
en: Let me guess. The Order.

speaker: Rebekah
en: A grand auction is happening, the Da'irat Al-mal. An annual show of silk robes comparing their golden spoons. No surprise, but this event is invite only. There is a high chance one of our targets will attend.

speaker: Basim
en: So, gain entry into the auction and find the one behind this.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Mumtaz! (How delightful!) You catch on quick.

speaker: Basim
en: Finding it hard to keep up?

speaker: Roshan
en: There might be clues if we trace trouble to the root. I can show you where they are brewing. Join me outside when you're ready.

speaker: Basim
en: What else do you know about the Da'irat Al-mal?

speaker: Rebekah
en: A specially curated place, one for the rich to display their bounty.

speaker: Basim
en: Does an event like that happen frequently here?

speaker: Rebekah
en: If the local merchants are to be believed, it happens once a year. But I'm sure there are no shortages of parties for the wealthy. What else?

speaker: Basim
en: What have you learnt about Karkh? I want to see it from fresh eyes.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Nothing that I'm not used to. Corruption, poverty... But the souq is vibrant. The spices, the materials... and oh, the tools! So many things I could experiment with.

speaker: Basim
en: Already thinking about taking a break?

speaker: Rebekah
en: Oh, calm down. I know where my focus lies. What else?

speaker: Basim
en: You know a little bit about me and where I am from. What about you, Rebekah?

speaker: Rebekah
en: Since when do you want to know more about me?

speaker: Basim
en: Come now, we are on the same side. Does not hurt to get to know who you are working with.

speaker: Rebekah
en: Hmph. Well, I'm not from here but let's just say my parents would not be out of place at an event like the Grand Auction.

speaker: Basim
en: You came from riches?

speaker: Rebekah
en: Shamefully so. As a child I never enjoyed the glamor, the dress up, and the manners. It was all so suffocating. It all changed when I stepped outside of our gates one day and saw the world for what it really is. I've never turned back since. What else?

speaker: Basim
en: No more questions. Shukran (Thank you), Rebekah.

speaker: Basim
en: Master.

speaker: Roshan
en: Are you ready, Basim? Karkh awaits.

speaker: Basim
en: Ready. Let us move.

speaker: Roshan
en: Follow me.

speaker: Roshan
en: Ever thought you would return here, to Karkh?

speaker: Basim
en: No. Much of my childhood was spent along these streets, finding friendship with rats and roaches. Some memories are good, most are bitter.

speaker: Roshan
en: Memories only serve to distract us. The Order has spread their influence into every crack in the city, turning Baghdad into their farm.

speaker: Basim
en: That will change.

speaker: Roshan
en: Responsibility lies heavy on our shoulders. The Order's blight falls over Karkh, and we are the only ones who can cure it.

speaker: Basim
en: How has Rebekah been adjusting to Karkh?

speaker: Roshan
en: She does not like the politics, but she has to fulfill her duty. Karkh is an acquired taste. Businesses at each other's throats, the obsession over money, perfume...

speaker: Basim
en: People here are happy to be lost in their own paradise.

speaker: Roshan
en: A paradise that can only be afforded by the wealthy, and often, corrupted.

speaker: Roshan
en: Come, we're nearly there.

speaker: Roshan
en: Welcome back to Karkh.

speaker: Basim
en: Spice still clings to the air.

speaker: Basim
en: What was it like, the first time you took a life?

speaker: Roshan
en: I barely recall. It was a man I used to know well. Before all this. Before the Hidden Ones.

speaker: Basim
en: You do not remember...?

speaker: Roshan
en: My memories are buried next to him. I refused to let his death haunt me, the way his breath haunted me when he was alive. I won't let the past define me. This is why I now consider myself the daughter of no one. If we do not quell the storm within us while awake, it takes us in our dreams. Like with you... and your jinni.

speaker: Roshan
en: Now. The souq. Like Rebekah said, some guards came through recently. Breaking bottles, smashing crates.

speaker: Basim
en: What caused this aggression?

speaker: Roshan
en: Let's find out. I've also heard they're seizing foreign goods, mostly from the East Road.

speaker: Basim
en: The East Road? I believe I know someone who can help. It has been an age, hopefully he's still around. I would be happy to see him again.

speaker: Roshan
en: Do not let nostalgia cloud reality, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: I will not. I know nothing stays the same.

speaker: Basim
en: It has been some time... I wonder what has changed around here. Maybe I could first pay an old friend a visit.

speaker: Beshi
en: We are brothers, all. Side by side we stand. And should one man fall, it is the one beside him who picks him up. We have been cut down. Divided. But here we remain. And so long as we draw breath, this fight will continue. So whet your blades. Pray to Allah for his guiding hand. For today, I see a great victory on the horizon.

speaker: Basim
en: That may be Beshi rallying those men.

speaker: Basim
en: Are you Beshi?

speaker: Basim
en: I am with Nur. You knew him, yes?

speaker: Beshi
en: I knew him... Last I saw he was being chased from the city. Does he live?

speaker: Basim
en: Barely. But he is safe.

speaker: Beshi
en: Stubborn bastard. What do I call you?

speaker: Basim
en: Basim.

speaker: Beshi
en: Very well, Basim. Have you a blade other than that butter knife you carry? You may fancy yourself something bigger just now.

speaker: Basim
en: For what? Are you setting off to find Ali?

speaker: Beshi
en: Not quite yet. These are only half my men. The rest are being held at the harbor further up the road.

speaker: Basim
en: There may be too few of us to wage an attack. If you want to save your men, our approach should be a cautious one. I will go, quietly. Have these men lie in wait and escort those we free.

speaker: Beshi
en: Your kind all think the same way. But it is a sound plan.

speaker: Basim
en: Get to the docks. Find Beshi.

speaker: Basim
en: That is the last. I must regroup with them.

speaker: Beshi
en: You are a hound, Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: I am only doing my part. Together we will see the end of what ails this city.

speaker: Beshi
en: Look no further than Al-Ghul. The man only spoken of and never seen.

speaker: Basim
en: What can you tell me about him?

speaker: Beshi
en: He takes enemies of the Caliphate and makes them dig in the desert. Prisoners. Rebels. Laborers. In search of what, I do not know. These men were captured with Ali weeks ago and were destined to perish beneath the sands.

speaker: Rebel
en: Not Ali. He's been taken elsewhere. They marked and separated us. Ali was in another group. They wanted to question him about ...

speaker: Rebel
en: You. And your friends.

speaker: Basim
en: Can you show me this marking?

speaker: Beshi
en: What are you thinking?

speaker: Basim
en: Ali and Nur got close enough to Al-Ghul that he took notice. If we find Ali, he can lead us to Al-Ghul.

speaker: Beshi
en: It is but one path. There may be another. I will go where these men were being sent to dig and pose as a captive.

speaker: Rebel
en: Are you mad?

speaker: Beshi
en: Only stubborn. Here, take this.

speaker: Basim
en: What do I do with it?

speaker: Beshi
en: It is a Khidmah Token. Those who understand its value will do what is in their power to help. I will send these men to regroup at the watermill on the northern outskirts. A rebel stronghold. You are welcome there.

speaker: Basim
en: Waffaqaka Allah.

speaker: Beshi
en: Baraka Allah feek. (May God bless you.)

speaker: Historian
en: Friend! Friend! Please. A moment, please.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes? How can I help you, old man?

speaker: Historian
en: Thank you for stopping, friend. I am a historian and teacher here from Baghdad on a mission of academic research.

speaker: Basim
en: I imagine there is much to study and explore here in AlUla.

speaker: Historian
en: Oh yes. The carvings in the rocks here at Jabal Ikmah date back many centuries. My students are examining them now.

speaker: Basim
en: Students? Where are they?

speaker: Historian
en: That is the very reason I called to you. Three of them have been gone a very long time. I begin to worry.

speaker: Basim
en: I am sure they are in no danger.

speaker: Historian
en: Safe? Yes, of course. But doing their work? This is what concerns me. Would you mind checking on them? My legs do not do the work of a younger man any longer.

speaker: Basim
en: Of course.

speaker: Basim
en: Let us see what these students are up to.

speaker: Basim
en: Your interest in these carvings suggest you are a student of such artifacts. Is that correct?

speaker: Student
en: Hello friend. Yes, I am considering their meaning. May I ask what you think of this one?

speaker: Basim
en: I am no scholar, but this looks to me like a hunting party of some sort. Though what they are after, I cannot say.

speaker: Student
en: To a layman's eye perhaps, but if I pointed out that what you see are frogs celebrating the harvest, what do you see now?

speaker: Basim
en: Frogs?

speaker: Student
en: A folk tale, my friend. Surely not true frogs. However, I enjoyed your dismay at my words. You see it now, of course.

speaker: Basim
en: Oh, yes.

speaker: Basim
en: A student of old carvings, are you?

speaker: Student 2
en: You have a keen eye. May I ask what you see in this relic of the past?

speaker: Basim
en: To my reckoning, it resembles a field, one arrayed with a type of crop. But please, tell me what you see.

speaker: Student 2
en: I see your confusion. However, it is really a carving of a traditional flatbread covered with .

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, thank you for opening my eyes to these insights.

speaker: Student 2
en: It is my duty and pleasure.

speaker: Basim
en: Pardon my interruption, but are you a student of these works?

speaker: Student 3
en: Yes, that is right! In fact, if I may trouble you momentarily, I would ask your view on this artifact.

speaker: Basim
en: I could only guess that it depicts an ancient deity of some sort. A creature invented in a legend.

speaker: Student 3
en: Your attempt shows thoughtfulness. But we need not read so much into such things. Artists represent daily life too.

speaker: Basim
en: So they do. And what daily occurrence does this artwork represent to you?

speaker: Student 3
en: It merely record the birth of a five-legged cow to a village. Nothing more.

speaker: Basim
en: Oh, yes of course. Thank you. I will be on my way now.

speaker: Historian
en: Ah, by the look on your face I can see that at the very least my students have not been devoured by leopards.

speaker: Basim
en: I can tell you that their bodies do not appear damaged. Their eyes however...

speaker: Historian
en: I take it they shared with you some of their findings. Tell me, what have they surmised from the stone carvings?

speaker: Basim
en: One described a large frog that could have been dancing. Perhaps celebrating a bountiful harvest.

speaker: Historian
en: A frog? And dancing no less! I already know the inattentive one who said this.

speaker: Basim
en: A student said that one of the carvings looked like a piece of (bread) with some muhammara on it.

speaker: Historian
en: They said this? What nonsense! Good for nothing rascal will never become a true historian if he keeps this up.

speaker: Basim
en: Your student said the etching was of an animal giving birth. A cow, to a five-legged calf.

speaker: Historian
en: Who said this? Which one? It was Yusuf, wasn't it? That son of a donkey! Back to being a stable boy for him!

speaker: Basim
en: I am certain his appreciation for the subtle beauty of those paintings will improve with your sage counsel.

speaker: Historian
en: You are most kind and generous with your words. Many thanks for your assistance. Be well in your journeys.

speaker: Basim
en: You are doing good work here. Teaching young people about the region's heritage is a noble calling. Goodbye.-->

speaker: Basim
en: What troubles you?

speaker: Basim
en: Evil spirit?

speaker: Basim
en: You saw her? Are you certain?

speaker: Basim
en: With your true eye or your mind's eye? The latter cannot always be trusted.

speaker: Basim
en: It would not be the first demon I have met. Nor will it be the last.

speaker: Basim
en: Flesh blistered, almost melted in places... A most unnatural death.

speaker: Basim
en: The emblem of the Caliph's palace...

speaker: Basim
en: Chinese markings.

speaker: Basim
en: The air ... its burning touch gnaws at my skin. Is this the breath of the Si'la'?

speaker: Basim
en: The crystals within this jar... My guess, sal ammoniac. Or something like it. I should not linger. The poisoned vapor from the crystals has grown weak, but could still prove deadly.

speaker: Basim
en: Something heavy was dragged along here...

speaker: Basim
en: Men with wagons came from that direction.

speaker: Basim
en: Merchants stopped here. Watered their animals at the river.

speaker: Basim
en: Something was offloaded. The tracks suggest it was the villagers' doing... Was the wagon's owner even aware?

speaker: Basim
en: I must share my findings with the survivor.

speaker: Basim
en: Not at all. Which is usually the case when the opponent does not exist.

speaker: Basim
en: There is no demon! Not here! It was the desperation of your friends that led to this tragedy.

speaker: Basim
en: Chinese merchant passed through, pausing to water their animals ... correct?

speaker: Basim
en: At this point, your friends decided to steal a chest of jars... ...not knowing they held a harmful vapor. Most likely something the Caliph's alchemists requested for their studies. When your friends opened the jars, the poison killed them within a few heartbeats.

speaker: Basim
en: I know that look. Shame. Guilt...

speaker: Basim
en: I am sorry, truly I am ... but now you must live with the consequences of your actions.

speaker: Basim
en: Ali. Are you ready?

speaker: Wasif
en: And who are you to tell me what I can and cannot do?

speaker: Muhammad
en: There is more at stake here than your pride, Wasif. We walk a narrow path.

speaker: Wasif
en: Enough! Take care what you say when we next meet, Governor. I will not suffer such insult twice.

speaker: Ali
en: That's Wasif and Baghdad's governor, Muhammad ibn Abdallah ibn Tahir. He gave Wasif an order. The warlord did not like it.

speaker: Basim
en: The Governor of Baghdad has no authority over the Warlord, unless... Could he also be with the Order?

speaker: Ali
en: Muhammad? I don't believe it. He is not just Governor, he is a poet, and a scholar. The man has spirit. I hoped to make him an ally.

speaker: Basim
en: Well, I hope you are right. Wasif is enough to deal with. I just have to find a way inside the Garrison.

speaker: Ali
en: One of the stewards inside is loyal to me. You will find him near the cookhouse. When he sees the red sash, he will help you.

speaker: Basim
en: What will you do?

speaker: Ali
en: I will find Beshi, and then free other rebels being held in the prison. Wasif I leave to you.

speaker: Basim
en: Warlord. You cloak yourself in the Caliph's colors so you can kidnap and kill at will. You are a plague upon the land. Its soil is red with the blood of those you have butchered. All because they sought their freedom... or because you feared they would. You think yourself untouchable, surrounded by your soldiers. But we will storm the Garrison, free Beshi, and see your reign of terror end.

speaker: Basim
en: Those walls do not look climbable. I will have to find another way in.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Those garrison walls are useless as they are. Have you seen the holes in the Garrison walls? What's the point of having walls if they have holes in them?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: You mean the construction? There are guards everywhere. No one's getting in or out of that place without being caught.

speaker: Basim
en: There might be a way in along the northern wall. I should take a look.

speaker: Garrison Cook
en: Bring the Narbaj (pomegranate juice stew) and the meal when it's ready. And forget your knives! We've got a lot more to take to the barracks. You're going to need both hands for carrying.

speaker: Basim
en: There is a steward here loyal to Ali. He will be somewhere near the cookhouse.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I'll bet he's left the key in that mess of a room.

speaker: Basim
en: Where there is a key, there is a lock... or a gate.

speaker: Steward
en: Over here!

speaker: Basim
en: You are Ali's man?'

speaker: Steward
en: I saw your red sash. We must be quick. Wasif is in the inner garrison. I can get you through a side entrance, but we cannot be seen together. Follow me at a distance, and stay out of sight.

speaker: Basim
en: I understand.

speaker: Steward
en: Tell me when you're ready to go.

speaker: Basim
en: All right, let us go.

speaker: Steward
en: I will walk in the open to avoid suspicion. Follow me at a distance, and stay in cover.

speaker: Steward
en: Try to stay in the shadows.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Have you heard those screams? It's like ghosts or something. I heard the prison is haunted.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Something's happening down there that isn't... right. I heard the same thing at Damascus Gate. You don't want to know.

speaker: Steward
en: I hope they fix the walls soon.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: You and me both. My patrols will be shorter, for one thing.

speaker: Soldier 5
en: Warlord Wasif is back, so no shirking on your patrols. Do the full round, all the way to the construction. If I catch any of you shortcutting, you'll lose a week's pay and be on latrine duty for a month.

speaker: Steward
en: Everything seems quiet enough, my friend.

speaker: Soldier 6
en: I'm not your friend. Be about your business, and be quick.

speaker: Steward
en: So far, so good. We're half-way. Remember, stay hidden. If you fail, I will not be able to help and you must find your way.

speaker: Basim
en: This is the barracks. Wasif's room is probably further inside.

speaker: Steward
en: Finally. This door will lead you to Wasif. Now, I must get back.

speaker: Basim
en: Wasif's room. It is surprisingly bare for a man of his rank.

speaker: Basim
en: This is an elaborate shrine. Wasif must have loved his mother.

speaker: Soldier 7
en: Stand straight and eyes front! The Warlord is arriving and will tolerate no disorder!

speaker: Wasif
en: Better. The heft is good, the balance too. The hilt is still a bit tight. Let us see if the edge is better.

speaker: Wasif
en: "Whoever bears arms against us is not one of us." You chose the wrong side, my friend.

speaker: Beshi
en: belongs to Allah! Not you!

speaker: Wasif
en: It's still sticking. Make the deeper.

speaker: Soldier 8
en: Time to put the dog down!

speaker: Basim
en: We should free the others. Then you can lead your men outside. I will deal with Wasif.

speaker: Ali
en: Outside? Don't be foolish. This is the perfect beginning. We are going to pull this place down.

speaker: Rebel
en: The Warden has the key to our cells. Be careful! He is more dangerous than he looks.

speaker: Basim
en: There is the Warden.

speaker: Basim
en: Key to the cells. Now to release the others.

speaker: Soldier 9
en: Stay alert! There's been word of strange noises.

speaker: Soldier 10
en: When are there not strange noises?

speaker: Soldier 11
en: Just keep your head on a swivel.

speaker: Rebel 1
en: Here! Alhamdulillah! (Praise be to God!)

speaker: Rebel 2
en: You have our thanks! Ali will lead us to our revenge. For Beshi!

speaker: Basim
en: Your men are free. Now I must find Wasif.

speaker: Ali
en: There is a signal fire just above here. Once lit, it will raise an alarm throughout the Garrison. The guards will come to us.

speaker: Basim
en: And I will find a way into his room while he is alone. All right. We will light the fire.

speaker: Ali
en: Do not forget our agreement.

speaker: Basim
en: I have not forgotten.

speaker: Soldier 12
en: What do we do? We are surrounded.

speaker: Wasif
en: Be silent! Take this down, quickly. The Zindeeq (heretic) Ali and his rebels have attacked the garrison. Request reinforcements. Seal the letter. When the door is breached, find a way through and deliver it to the Caliph. On your life!

speaker: Soldier 12
en: Y-yes, sayyidi!

speaker: Basim
en: Composed and silent, even when trapped. Al-Mardikhwar indeed.

speaker: Wasif
en: A feather... isn't that ironic? Was it taken from an eagle who fell out of the sky?

speaker: Basim
en: A symbol of freedom. A word you did not use often. And never will again.

speaker: Wasif
en: Oh... so this is freedom? Yet, I do not see any way out...

speaker: Ali
en: Argh!

speaker: Ali
en: We will have to fight our way out. Our revolution begins now. With me!

speaker: Basim
en: This may not be good.

speaker: Basim
en: You mentioned needing my help, Dervis. With keeping the rebellion alive, I presume?

speaker: Dervis
en: Indeed. Coin goes a long way in securing that. But coin is hard to come by without the right... assets. Have a look. I hear that a number of rare and unique items line the pockets of our citizens. Bring me their burdens, Basim, and be rewarded.

speaker: Basim
en: I have this for you.

speaker: Dervis
en: A good harvest! Nicely done.

speaker: Basim
en: I have something for you.

speaker: Dervis
en: A fine haul! Well done.

speaker: Dervis
en: You have been a fine treasure hunter, Basim. Now you can look the part.

speaker: Basim
en: Greetings, ya 'amm (uncle). If I may, where is the scholar Ahmad ibn Musa?

speaker: Kahraman
en: Ah, yes, the most adventurous of the Banu Musa. His workshop is right behind me.

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you, ya 'amm (uncle).

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim! Hey, Nine-Fingers! Over here!

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal. What do you have there, Sneak-Thief?

speaker: Nehal
en: A book, I managed to save at least one from the fire.

speaker: Basim
en: If they catch you stealing...

speaker: Nehal
en: They cut off a finger. No, wait. A whole hand!

speaker: Basim
en: That is not funny.

speaker: Nehal
en: Then don't laugh.

speaker: Basim
en: All right, you are in a mood, and I have things to do. Nothing that concerns you.

speaker: Nehal
en: Oh, secret Hidden Ones stuff! What are you doing this time? Stabbing? Stealing? Stabbing and then stealing?

speaker: Basim
en: That is your specialty, Nehal..

speaker: Nehal
en: Just because you lost a finger does not mean you've lost your touch!

speaker: Basim
en: All these tools and books, looks like Ahmad's room. But where is he?

speaker: Basim
en: The letter says these books are for Ahmad.

speaker: Basim
en: Another book of poetry by Arib. Tabid would love this.

speaker: Basim
en: Measuring tools, like my father used to own. But these are Ahmad's.

speaker: Basim
en: Ahmad always signs his work. This is definitely his doing.

speaker: Basim
en: Ahmad seems to be working on something new. But what?

speaker: Basim
en: Diagrams, machine tools, and other oddities. This is definitely Ahmad's workshop. But where can he be?

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Pardon me, may I help you?

speaker: Basim
en: I am looking for Ahmad ibn Musa. Do you know where I can find him?

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: I may be able to help you. Follow me.

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Is this your first visit to the House of Wisdom?

speaker: Basim
en: No, a friend and I used to sneak in as kids. We taught ourselves to read in your library.

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: All young people should follow your worthy example.

speaker: Basim
en: The caretakers who chased us out of the stacks everyday did not think so.

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Merely doing their jobs. And what did you study in the House of Wisdom?

speaker: Basim
en: I loved poetry and heroic tales. My friend... preferred pagan gods and dark magic.

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Interesting. And did you follow your youthful passion and become a scholar?

speaker: Basim
en: When the whole world awaits? No, you might say I am a man on a mission.
