speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Ah. Well, what about your friend?

speaker: Basim
en: No, no, she... still searches for something, though what that is, I do not know.

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: A shame! It's not far now. Hurry, hurry.

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Guards, help! I'm under attack!

speaker: Basim
en: What? You lie!

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Please, don't hurt me.

speaker: Basim
en: You led me into a trap! I should slay you where you stand.

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Spare kindly Hamid!

speaker: Basim
en: Then tell me, where is Ahmad ibn Musa?

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: Please, sir! I don't know where he is. Truly, I do not!

speaker: Basim
en: Then why lead me into an ambush?

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: He... he made me do it!

speaker: Basim
en: Who is he? Not Ahmad, surely.

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: I don't know his name, for he always wears a mask.

speaker: Basim
en: And what does this masked man want?

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: He commands me to keep everyone away from the House of Wisdom's dig site. Or else...

speaker: Basim
en: Or else what?

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: He will hurt my head! Like with the others. Please, spare humble Hamid.

speaker: Basim
en: Where is this dig site?

speaker: Hamid Al-Haleem
en: It's in the wilderness, outside of the city. Here, let me draw you a map.

speaker: Basim
en: The map should lead me to the dig site.

speaker: Basim
en: Such a massive dig. What are they up to?

speaker: Basim
en: Impressive work, my friend. Are you digging up something for the Caliph?

speaker: Digger
en: Never you mind all that.

speaker: Basim
en: The remains of past empires intrigues me. Do you mind if I take a look around?

speaker: Digger
en: Look at the old rocks all you want, but don't touch our tools and chests.

speaker: Basim
en: I would not dream of it.

speaker: Civilian
en: This heat makes me ill. I want to vomit.

speaker: Digger 2
en: What ever you do, don't ask for Doctor Hassan.

speaker: Civilian
en: I know, I know. I'd disappear, just like the others.

speaker: Basim
en: Mercenaries guarding the site. They must have found something important.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: When do we get paid, captain?

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: We will get paid. One way or the other.

speaker: Mercenary 1
en: They don't have much to steal. But it's something.

speaker: Basim
en: Are you the leader of this battle-scarred band of war dogs? You must get paid well.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Not as much as we want to get paid, I tell you that.

speaker: Basim
en: Care to do a little work for me?

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Maybe. What's this job then?

speaker: Basim
en: See those fancy Caliph's men over there? I might need a hand.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Hmm. Let's work something out.

speaker: Basim
en: Spoken like a true mercenary. Here is a token of my appreciation.

speaker: Mercenary 2
en: Hey, it's honest work.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Why does that fool of a scholar travel with so many chests?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: They are so heavy, I swear they are stuffed with rocks.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I only need my blade, my waterskin, and my bedroll. Fool of a scholar.

speaker: Basim
en: Hmm, nothing. I should see if there are any more chests around.

speaker: Basim
en: This chest has Ahmad's signature seal on it. Must be his.

speaker: Basim
en: Interesting. A letter to Ahmad from a Doctor Hassan. Ahmad must be at the hospital, working with this doctor. But what is a famous inventor doing with a doctor? It must all link together somehow.

speaker: Basim
en: The Bimaristan, where the best healers in Baghdad gather. Finding Doctor Hassan should lead me to Ahmad.

speaker: Nurse 1
en: Another one from the dig site. This time with a broken finger.

speaker: Nurse 2
en: It is best never to speak of these things.

speaker: Basim
en: I need to find a way into Doctor Hassan's office.

speaker: Basim
en: The symbol of the Order. This all but proves that Doctor Hassan is one of them.

speaker: Basim
en: This letter proves it! Hassan is neck-deep in the Order.

speaker: Doctor
en: I have some burned scholars here. Some scholars from the House of Wisdom got burned trying to save the books. We need that room for the patients.

speaker: Doctor 2
en: No, that's Doctor Hassan's private laboratory. It's locked, no one must go inside.

speaker: Doctor 1
en: So we just leave the burn victims outside? Will someone answer me?

speaker: Doctor 2
en: Please, use your indoor voice. You're upsetting the patients.

speaker: Basim
en: Doctor Hassan keeps his laboratory locked up. I wonder why.

speaker: Basim
en: A broken window. Could be a way in.

speaker: Doctor Hassan
en: There is nothing wrong with my methods, only the mechanism itself. It needs more subjects. More work. I certainly do not need some useless inventor meddling with the Great Work. Am I not the great and dreadful Al-Azhdaha? Maybe I should not say that out loud. Focus, Hassan. Focus.

speaker: Basim
en: The doctor is dead. Now to find Ahmad and solve this bloody mystery.

speaker: Ahmad
en: Basim, what happened here?

speaker: Basim
en: Where were you, Ahmad?

speaker: Ahmad
en: I was around. I'm always around. Would you tell me what happened?

speaker: Basim
en: Are you aware this man works for the Order?

speaker: Ahmad
en: He called on me a few weeks ago, after they found something in the desert. An ancient mechanism of some sort. They needed me to

speaker: Basim
en: And you asked no questions?

speaker: Ahmad
en: I never ask questions when it comes to work. Do you?

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me about this mechanism.

speaker: Ahmad
en: It opens a path. In the mind. A path to the ancient world. This mechanism, somehow, seems to open... the doors of perception.

speaker: Basim
en: Have you seen this for yourself?

speaker: Ahmad
en: No, but I heard the stories of those who have. They are lost, Basim. Because they think what they saw is reality. They think they belong to this ancient world. I knew nothing about the Order being involved. If I did, I would have come to you. I just... I got caught up. You know me. You know me, Basim...

speaker: Basim
en: You will leave this place and return to the Bureau. I will not tell a soul if you do not.

speaker: Ahmad
en: How shameful it is that knowledge always ends up in the wrong hands. Isn't it, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: A bloody mess. Head bandages. But this is a hospital, after all.

speaker: Basim
en: I should continue investigating the library.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, I see our new Abbasiyah Bureau is well-guarded by an alert and active Rafiq.

speaker: Tabid
en: Basim! You startled me, I was just enjoying some poetry.

speaker: Basim
en: Oh, whose?

speaker: Tabid
en: The court poet, Sayyida (Lady) Arib. Her words chirp like the birds of paradise.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, yes. I have read her works. My friend Nehal and I used to sneak into the House of Wisdom when we were young. Hours we spent, reading of gods and jinn. I always enjoyed this place.

speaker: Tabid
en: The House of Wisdom is not what it once was.

speaker: Basim
en: Is not our friend Ahmad ibn Musa there? He went to his workshop, as I recall.

speaker: Tabid
en: Yes. I sent a message for him to come and help set up this Bureau. But he never replied. My spies could not contact him. A week has passed, and he cannot be found.

speaker: Basim
en: So one of the famous Banu Musa is missing in the House of Wisdom.

speaker: Tabid
en: Yes. Venture there and learn his fate.

speaker: Basim
en: It shall be done.

speaker: Basim
en: Tabid, I would like to ask you something.

speaker: Tabid
en: Please, go ahead.

speaker: Basim
en: What can you tell me about Ahmad ibn Musa?

speaker: Tabid
en: The son of a famous astronomer, Ahmad and his brothers excel at mathematics, invention, and scholarship. Together, they wrote the Book of Ingenious Devices, describing their wonderful clockwork automata.

speaker: Basim
en: What made him join our cause?

speaker: Tabid
en: The Banu Musa were once close to al-Mutawakkil, but grew disgusted with the Abbasid Caliphate.

speaker: Basim
en: What happened?

speaker: Tabid
en: They refuse to discuss it, so I cannot say.

speaker: Basim
en: There are many reasons to be disgusted with the Abbasids.

speaker: Tabid
en: Was there anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: What is important in Abbasiyah?

speaker: Tabid
en: This district is the heart of learning in Baghdad. All the world's knowledge can be found here.

speaker: Basim
en: Any key places to investigate?

speaker: Tabid
en: Follow the trail, wherever it leads. Besides the House of Wisdom, there are other vital landmarks. Be sure to visit the Four Markets, the Observatory, and the Dome of the Ass.

speaker: Basim
en: I remember the Observatory well. I met the great astronomer Al-Khwarizmi there when I was young.

speaker: Tabid
en: Excellent. Finally, if you need to soothe sore muscles, a steam bath at the splendid hammam of Abbasiyah is a joy.

speaker: Basim
en: After a night of clambering across rooftops, that sounds good.

speaker: Tabid
en: Was there anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: Any hint on what the Order might be doing in Abbasiyah?

speaker: Tabid
en: No, my friend, not more than what I've told you. Although ... no, it is probably nothing.

speaker: Basim
en: What is it? Any little bit may help.

speaker: Tabid
en: Before he left, Ahmad ibn Musa said something about books going missing from the House of Wisdom.

speaker: Basim
en: I will keep that in mind.

speaker: Tabid
en: Was there anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me more about yourself, Tabid.

speaker: Tabid
en: Me? Oh, not much to say. I love poetry, is that enough?

speaker: Basim
en: Come now, do not be so modest.

speaker: Tabid
en: As you wish. I come from Nubia, a dry land south of Egypt. My father sent me to Cairo to study Islam. There, I learned a fiery sense of right from wrong. And the corruption in Cairo was very, very wrong. We revolted. Our revolt failed and I fled to Baghdad. The Hidden Ones took me in and ... here I am.

speaker: Basim
en: Someday you should tell the whole tale.

speaker: Tabid
en: Was there anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you, Tabid. That is all for now.

speaker: Roshan
en: Come, Basim.

speaker: Roshan
en: An Order member is within our reach, Basim. And like those before and those yet to come, Al-Ghul's death will be just. This is a man who preys off the desperate and the disenfranchised. And such atrocities will only continue, for Al-Ghul is but a cog in a larger wheel. One that spins destructively. So long as it does, we Hidden Ones will make it our mission to slow it to a stop. Today you will lend your hand, your blade, to that very mission. And while Al-Ghul is your first target, he will not be your last. I have great belief in that. And in you. Through all my stoicism, my harsh lessons, know that you have impressed me, Basim. The Order's presence in Baghdad and beyond rests on shifting sands so long as you remain at the tip of our spear.

speaker: Basim
en: And that is where I intend to remain. Beholden to your guidance, Master.

speaker: Basim
en: As busy as a bee hive.

speaker: Roshan
en: Come. Set your sights on the trial that awaits you.

speaker: Basim
en: Merchants. Livestock. Caravans from all walks. And I thought Anbar's markets were disorderly.

speaker: Roshan
en: Where there is disorder, there is chaos. And chaos can bring opportunity. See what avenues present themselves. Be reactive, but patient. And trust your instincts.

speaker: Basim
en: That is Mas'ood, on the balcony. Just as Ali described.

speaker: Roshan
en: I see him.

speaker: Roshan
en: Go now. Wet it with the blood of the slain. I will find you when it is over.

speaker: Basim
en: You think your cruelties are well-hidden, Al-Ghul, for you chose those with little voice whose cries you knew would go unheard. They dug at your bidding, died at your hand and were cast aside like so much refuse. All to scour the desert for some artifact. Even now you haggle for flesh, safe in the Caravanserai. You prefer your victims chained and starved. It is time you faced a man unbound.

speaker: Roshan
en: The stage is yours, Basim. I will be watching. Remember, patience. Discipline. And when the opportunity presents itself, seize it. This is a test, Basim. For you, and you alone.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: What is the delay?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: I am not certain. Some guards came poking around and ordered us all to wait.

speaker: Basim
en: What delays your departure, friend?

speaker: Caravan merchant
en: Someone by the name of Mas'ood saw fit to inspect my wares and so, here I wait. Who does he think he is?

speaker: Basim
en: I am not sure I can be of any help at the moment.

speaker: Basim
en: Greetings, friend.

speaker: Caravan merchant
en: Ah! You again.

speaker: Basim
en: What is it you are carrying? I ask only so that I may collect it for you.

speaker: Caravan merchant
en: Would you do that? I would take great joy in seeing that man in a fit of anger. It is a crate of silks and spices.

speaker: Basim
en: Ready your camel. I will see what I can do.

speaker: Basim
en: If I can get that merchant to leave, his abrupt departure may lure Al-Ghul out.

speaker: Basim
en: Al-Ghul deserves a fate far worse than the one at the edge of my blade. My message will reach the Order, loud and clear.

speaker: Basim
en: A crate with spices and silks. There cannot be too many of those around.

speaker: Musician
en: Might we play for your pleasure?

speaker: Basim
en: Such a melody suits my mood of late.

speaker: Musician
en: Let the music flow!

speaker: Basim
en: A strange thing to happen upon. Perhaps I can use this to my advantage?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: You must think me a fool.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: You said it. Not me. Though I am inclined to agree!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: How dare you speak to me that way!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: If you want me to stop then you should move along. If not, I will gladly raise my fists in place of mincing my words.

speaker: Basim
en: Those two men are having a loud dispute, but not loud enough. How might I push them over the edge?

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Did you... argh! Now I've had it.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Do you take me for a fool? You did that!

speaker: Basim
en: The louder they get, the more onlookers they attract.

speaker: Basim
en: Hmm... pungent. This must be the caravan merchant's crate.

speaker: Caravan merchant
en: Is that what I think it is?

speaker: Basim
en: Is this your crate?

speaker: Caravan merchant
en: Ah! It is indeed! The guards returned it to you?

speaker: Basim
en: In a manner of speaking.

speaker: Caravan merchant
en: Very good, very good. I must repay you. You seem like a man who enjoys a good meal. Care for some spice?

speaker: Basim
en: Not today, no. But I will ask that you loudly proclaim your departure. Make sure Mas'ood notices.

speaker: Caravan merchant
en: Ha! We share the same mind. My thanks to you, ya sadeeqi (friend).

speaker: Basim
en: Word will surely get to Al-Ghul. Come out and spectate, coward.

speaker: Basim
en: There he is. Now is my chance.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: You there. Come over here, quickly. Get us out and I will make it worth your while. Please!

speaker: Civilian 4
en: We were promised steady work and fruitful returns. Now we're being made to slog in the desert! We were deceived. Please, you must help us!

speaker: Basim
en: I plan to, it is only a matter of how. Wait here, I will return.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: You've returned! Will you help us?

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me what I can do to help.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: The man who brought us has a deed that binds us to Mas'ood. If he has not collected his fee he should still be here.

speaker: Basim
en: If I can relieve these men of their duty, it will not be long before Al-Ghul catches wind of his disbanded work force.

speaker: Basim
en: Greetings, my friend. What sorts of goods are you travelling with?

speaker: Merchant 1
en: Ivory and honey. And you? Are you seeking to trade?

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps. For now I will browse for a little longer.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu'alaikum. (Peace be upon you.)

speaker: Merchant 2
en: Wa'alaikum as-salam. (And peace be upon you.) Could I interest you in some fruits today? My pomegranates are ripe and succulent!

speaker: Basim
en: Is that what you have come to trade? Let me think on it.

speaker: Basim
en: Well met, traveler. The caravanserai is rich with wares today. I was wondering if you had any goods to sell.

speaker: Merchant 3
en: I only deal in dirham, and what I sell are not goods, boy. Though I suppose that depends on who you ask.

speaker: Basim
en: I am not sure I understand.

speaker: Merchant 3
en: I sell men. Laborers. But my lot is spoken for.

speaker: Basim
en: Could I change your mind? I have coin to spare and could use men such as yours.

speaker: Merchant 3
en: Fifteen thousand.

speaker: Basim
en: That is absurd. Who has the means to pay so much?

speaker: Merchant 3
en: It is better to keep that question to yourself. Be on your way now.

speaker: Basim
en: A high price, but... it is one I can pay.

speaker: Merchant 3
en: But not one I expected you to. I said my men were spoken for. Nothing will change that, and for good reason. Now be gone.

speaker: Basim
en: If I am going to free those laborers, I will have to steal the deed.

speaker: Basim
en: Now to free those men.

speaker: Merchant 3
en: Oh, where... where is... wha... The deed! Have I dropped it? No, no, no. No!

speaker: Basim
en: I have claimed the deed from your handler. You are bound no longer. Go!

speaker: Basim
en: The laborers run amok. Al-Ghul will take notice. I must be ready to strike. Word will surely get to Al-Ghul. Come out and spectate, coward.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: We have come with the promise of work. Why bind our hands like this?

speaker: Basim
en: Death approaches, Al-Ghul

speaker: Civilian 5
en: Where is the overseer? I demand to know the meaning of this.

speaker: Civilian 6
en: This was a ruse all along! What do you mean to do with us?

speaker: Basim
en: This ends now.

speaker: Basim
en: Turn your hate inward, Mas'ood. It is your wickedness that has led you here.

speaker: Basim
en: Contribution to what?

speaker: Basim
en: Some things are meant to stay that way.

speaker: Basim
en: Me?

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal?

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim!

speaker: Roshan
en: Clear your mind.

speaker: Roshan
en: Al-Ghul's relentless pursuit at the expense of human lives has come to an end. It is a day of victory. Not only for those spared of his cruelty, but for the Hidden Ones. The Order's grand plot in Baghdad may still be a mystery, but we can at least be certain Al-Ghul's role in it has been vanquished.

speaker: Basim
en: I believe what he sought to uncover were more strange objects like the one I took from the Winter Palace. What does the Order want with these relics of the past? And why guard them with so much effort?

speaker: Roshan
en: You are beginning to ask the right questions, Basim. We shall find the answers together.

speaker: Basim
en: Lately all I have are questions.

speaker: Roshan
en: What do you mean?

speaker: Basim
en: Nothing. Forget I said anything.

speaker: Roshan
en: How am I to guide you if you will not speak openly?

speaker: Basim
en: I have... I have... struggled with nightmares. In these dreams a jinni torments me until I wake up panicked and soaked with sweat. In Alamut, I had nearly forgotten about it. But when I killed Al-Ghul, I felt its presence again. And I am left asking why. Why here? Why now? Why me? Piling questions and no answers. I meant to tell you, but...

speaker: Roshan
en: You were afraid I would think you weak of mind.

speaker: Roshan
en: We are only as weak as we allow ourselves to be. To shed a weakness, you must do what is necessary to mend that which causes you pain.

speaker: Basim
en: Will you permit me a brief respite? I wish to seek out an old friend.

speaker: Roshan
en: Nehal? I remember. She is important to you, isn't she?

speaker: Basim
en: She is, but last we spoke I led her to believe otherwise.

speaker: Roshan
en: This causes you pain. Then go and heal this wound without delay. Find me at the Harbiyah bureau when it is settled.

speaker: Basim
en: If that was indeed Nehal, I have not a clue where she went. Back home in Anbar, maybe.

speaker: Basim
en: Is there anything more you can tell me about the Shari' district? Why would it be of interest to Nur?

speaker: Roshan
en: The people there are in quiet support of the rebels. Common folk. Workers. Merchants. Come to think of it, Nur did make mention of a new contact. A merchant. It may be this merchant dwells in Shari', among the dyeing leather factory workers.

speaker: Basim
en: I will keep an eye out for a stall.

speaker: Dervis
en: Just a moment.

speaker: Basim
en: Dervis...

speaker: Dervis
en: Basim! Azeezi! (My dear boy!) I thought you were dead.

speaker: Basim
en: I feared the same.

speaker: Dervis
en: What are you doing here? You... Your clothes... You are one of them now? How?

speaker: Basim
en: A Hidden One. Under Roshan's guidance.

speaker: Dervis
en: Forgive me, this is all too much.

speaker: Dervis
en: When I did not find you among the dead, I hoped that somehow you had escaped. I spent many nights praying for your life, praying that you had found safety. Today, Allah has answered me.

speaker: Basim
en: I am not worthy of your prayers.

speaker: Dervis
en: What happened that night was not your doing. It was the doing of evil men. You know this. It is why you have chosen to walk this path. It is why I have found my way to Baghdad. Ali ibn Muhammad is brash and sees himself a great hero of prophecy. I loathe man, but we fight a common enemy. One I must help defeat if my soul is to one day rest.

speaker: Basim
en: So it is true. You are the rebel merchant who was helping Nur.

speaker: Dervis
en: What has become of him?

speaker: Basim
en: He clings to life, but he is safe among our people. I am to continue his work and hunt Baghdad's oppressors. Ali was helping Nur get closer to one such man, but as you may know, he has since disappeared.

speaker: Dervis
en: He hasn't disappeared. He has been captured. A fate shared by many rebels of late.

speaker: Basim
en: Do you know where he is being held?

speaker: Dervis
en: He was taken to the Khurasan Gate Guardhouse, but that was weeks ago.

speaker: Dervis
en: You even leave like they do.

speaker: Basim
en: It is good to see you again.

speaker: Dervis
en: Just watch yourself. You may be in better hands, but I am still a nagging old man. And Basim... If you ever are feeling a little ... thievish, come see me. I could use your help. For a good cause, of course.

speaker: Basim
en: This is the outpost Ali was taken to.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: I saw that before. Are you and the scribe ever going to play nicely along together?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Not likely. The man thinks he can let loose his tongue just because of his rank. If he gets in my way again I will kill him myself.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: And who will record the prisoners then? You? You cannot fasten your own bracers, let alone write.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: If it means we rid ourselves of his blithering, I will happily learn.

speaker: Basim
en: That one looks like a scribe.

speaker: Basim
en: I will hold on to that for you.

speaker: Basim
en: This looks like a scribe's quarters.

speaker: Basim
en: A list of prisons, all paired with different marks.

speaker: Civilian
en: Where is Hunayn? He owes me money.

speaker: Civilian
en: I don't know, ask the Caretaker of Books.

speaker: Civilian
en: Somebody posted guards around the library.

speaker: Civilian
en: What is going on these days?

speaker: Basim
en: A partial list of books that have been burned or gone missing. What is "an ancient manuscript in an unknown tongue"? I should check the second floor.

speaker: Basim
en: The library is guarded. Something must have happened.

speaker: Soldier
en: What a bloody mess.

speaker: Soldier
en: That's nothing. I saw worse in the eastern campaigns.

speaker: Soldier
en: But this is a library! We should do something.

speaker: Soldier
en: They don't pay me enough to care.

speaker: Basim
en: The Caretaker of Books!

speaker: Basim
en: He's dead! But he wrote "mansakh" (scriptorium) in his own blood. I wonder...

speaker: Basim
en: Something in his hand. Fabric, torn from a woman's gown. But whose?

speaker: Basim
en: Strange fires and a dead caretaker... horrifying. I should hurry.

speaker: Basim
en: Better keep my open.

speaker: Soldier
en: Attention! Prepare the prisoner on Zahra's orders.

speaker: Basim
en: A prisoner, here? That guard might have the key.

speaker: Soldier
en: Have a heart. The man's not had a good meal in days.

speaker: Soldier
en: We got our orders. Nobody goes in to see the guest.

speaker: Soldier
en: Poor guy locked in with a bunch of books. I'd go mad.

speaker: Hunayn
en: Books will only bring you sorrow, mother said. Go into business! Get a market stall, be happy. If only I had listened! How right she was!

speaker: Hunayn
en: Don't kill me! Please, give me more time, I... I almost cracked it!

speaker: Basim
en: Don't worry,, I'm not here to kill you. What are you trying to crack?

speaker: Hunayn
en: The book! I said I couldn't. This is not a language that I know. But she gave me no choice.

speaker: Basim
en: Who?

speaker: Hunayn
en: A woman named Zahra, one of the scholars here.

speaker: Basim
en: What is this book? What is it called?

speaker: Hunayn
en: The only thing I know is that it is written in a script unlike any other and I have seen hundreds... The way Zahra talks, it's more of an artifact or relic than a book. I lied about my progress so they wouldn't kill me. I can't read a single word. I don't even know if it's a language.

speaker: Basim
en: Where can I find Zahra?

speaker: Hunayn
en: I don't know, she could be anywhere in the city. I... I just want to go home.

speaker: Basim
en: All right. Get to safety before the guards return.

speaker: Basim
en: Must be something here to help me.

speaker: Basim
en: This book makes me uncomfortable. I will leave it here.

speaker: Basim
en: This Order letter mentions Arib. An innocent reference, or something more sinister?

speaker: Basim
en: This peculiar machine. I saw something like it in Ahmad's workshop.

speaker: Basim
en: This letter gives the location of the scholar Zahra's estate.

speaker: Basim
en: Time to visit Zahra's estate and see if she's involved with the Order.

speaker: Basim
en: Zahra's estate, but nobody's home. Now is my chance to search her place.

speaker: Basim
en: Another book of poetry by Arib. She is definitely popular in certain circles.

speaker: Basim
en: Zahra is definitely tied to the Order. Along with somebody named Al-Rabisu.

speaker: Basim
en: Learned all I can. Better get to high ground and get ready Zahra might return any minute.

speaker: Zahra the Scholar
en: Servants! Prepare a glass of date juice on ice. And serve it with a plate of honeyed bread and pomegranates. Then prepare the bath salts! I am utterly beat.

speaker: Zahra the Scholar
en: Paradise is where you find it.

speaker: Zahra the Scholar
en: That old fool tinkering with his worthless ancient disc and helpless patients. Bah!

speaker: Soldier
en: Of course, sayyidati (my lady).

speaker: Zahra the Scholar
en: The real answers are in books. They are always in books. Am I not right?

speaker: Soldier
en: Always, sayyidati (my lady).

speaker: Zahra the Scholar
en: When I get that book translated, then we'll see who is the real head of the Order.

speaker: Soldier
en: As you wish, sayyidati (my lady).

speaker: Zahra the Scholar
en: Something's wrong. Guards! Search the estate for intruders. Gut them like fish!

speaker: Basim
en: Zahra thought that strange book would get their "Great Work" functioning. Good thing Hunayn could not translate a single word. I should return to the Rafiq.

speaker: Basim
en: This is the place.

speaker: Basim
en: Time to leave.-->

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Refreshing to see the bazaar so lively. The traders only bring in the finest spices I want during the auction!

speaker: Civilian 2
en: It is a time to buy the exquisite, to mingle with elite, and to dress in your finest.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Yet we still have persons dressed in a hood...

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Ceramics and textiles from the East! Took a while to get past the blockade, but they made it for the acution

speaker: Civilian 5
en: Very good! I received a shipment of paintings from India as well. They will fetch me a stellar price!

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Good news from all over the world, and coin in our pouches!

speaker: Kong
en: Basim! Lái! (Come!)

speaker: Basim
en: Should have known you would be here, Kong.

speaker: Kong
en: Hah! You know me. Come, let us chat.

speaker: Basim
en: I do have something to ask of you... Do you have any information about the Treasurer? Someone who works for the Caliphate.

speaker: Kong
en: The Treasurer? Hmm, I do have something but, you know, it hurts to give precious information for free...

speaker: Basim
en: What job do you need now?

speaker: Kong
en: Hah! Already know what is on my mind, eh? You see, little finch, the Da'irat Al-mal is not only an important event for the upper-class of Karkh, but also for the thieves.

speaker: Basim
en: Did someone take something of yours again?

speaker: Kong
en: A precious ceramic saucer. Luca has it. He has always been jealous of me.

speaker: Basim
en: Where do you think it is?

speaker: Kong
en: I knew I could rely on you, little finch! You should be able to find it in the crates near the stall.

speaker: Basim
en: Be right back.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: The Da'irat Al-mal is not open yet. Come back later.

speaker: Basim
en: Maybe I can look around the bazaar before it starts. Might learn something useful.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Staying here will not make time pass faster. Come back later.

speaker: Civilian 6
en: I assume you heard about the commotion a few stalls down?

speaker: Civilian 7
en: Do not tell me it's Kong and Luca again...

speaker: Civilian 6
en: Oh, not them this time. Another pair of traders fighting to get a stall near the auction.

speaker: Basim
en: This must be the stall Kong mentioned. Now, to find that plate...

speaker: Basim
en: Trust Kong to own a plate like this. Now, maybe he will tell me what he knows about the Treasurer.

speaker: Basim
en: Hmm, suspicious activity on the rooftops...

speaker: Basim
en: Here.

speaker: Kong
en: Little finch delivers once again! Just the very thing I need to complete my set!

speaker: Basim
en: I thought this was yours...

speaker: Kong
en: It is now! Anyway, listen close... I was having my usual afternoon tea when I overheard two ladies speaking about an order they fulfilled for the Da'irat Al-mal. They made a beautiful robe for the Treasurer with intricate eastern embroidery. Open your eyes to that!

speaker: Basim
en: Eastern wear? Thank you, Kong.

speaker: Basim
en: The Treasurer is likely a foreigner from the East.

speaker: Merchant
en: Ahlan, Ahlan! (welcome, welcome!) Come upstairs and look at my wares, ya sadeeqi (sir)! Things you have never seen before in Baghdad! Exotic Chinese artifacts, here only! Nowhere else! Don't be shy! Come closer and be amazed at my selection upstairs!

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum (Peace be upon you). You mentioned Chinese artifacts?

speaker: Merchant
en: Yes friend, welcome, welcome! You will surely find something of interest here!

speaker: Merchant
en: Do you have a taste for the exotic? These melons are freshly imported from . No samples, only trust. Buy one for yourself and see!

speaker: Basim
en: There might be something else of interest.

speaker: Merchant
en: Beautiful threads, smooth as a camel's buttered bottom. A special for you, ya sadeeqi (sir). Buy two, get another free!

speaker: Basim
en: I should look at other wares.

speaker: Merchant
en: Longing for the exquisite, ya sadeeqi (sir)? I have ornaments that hail from the far East on auction! Rare vases, delicate tea cups... but the hairpin is my prize! One of a kind, a beauty even the Treasurer asked about!

speaker: Basim
en: Wait, the hairpin? Where is it?

speaker: Merchant
en: It's going to be up on auction! If you wish to purchase it, make sure to bring a good bag of coin!

speaker: Basim
en: A hairpin, from the East. This must be the item Al-Kullulu was after for the Treasurer. I must look out for it at the auction.

speaker: Qabiha
en: Tardiness is not something the Treasurer appreciates.

speaker: Perfume Supplier
en: ...not something we can rush, ya sayyidati (my lady).

speaker: Qabiha
en: The Treasurer will not be happy. Neither will I.

speaker: Perfume Supplier
en: I know that. The perfume creation is complex. We are already doing our best.

speaker: Qabiha
en: Your best is not enough.

speaker: Perfume Supplier
en: Come, we talk elsewhere. There are ears in the walls.

speaker: Basim
en: That woman mentioned the Treasurer. I should keep my ears close.

speaker: Qabiha
en: The Treasurer is fond of the Qina', as you know. No one is more unhappy when three dozen bottles go missing.

speaker: Perfume Supplier
en: With the harbor withholding our supplies, production has been slow, ya sayyidati (my lady). Certain... incidents there have also made our situation difficult.

speaker: Qabiha
en: You are not telling me exactly what it is we are missing.

speaker: Perfume Supplier
en: The... blood, my lady.

speaker: Qabiha
en: The blood is essential in the scent. It is what makes the Qina' perfume special. We must have it.

speaker: Perfume Supplier
en: I will talk to the Caliph, see what we can do. The Treasurer will have to wait for her supply.

speaker: Basim
en: This perfume on the Tax Collector's letters... I thought it smelled like iron. Was it blood? This woman could be from the Caliph's inner circle. She knows the Treasurer... I must speak to her.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum, ya sayyidati. (Peace be upon you, my lady)

speaker: Qabiha
en: Wa 'alaikum as-salam. (And peace be upon you.)

speaker: Basim
en: I could not help but overhear, sayyidati (lady), about the perfume...

speaker: Qabiha
en: It is not courteous to eavesdrop. Seeing as you are an admirer, you are pardoned. My name is Qabiha, the woman behind the Qina'.

speaker: Basim
en: It has a unique scent.

speaker: Qabiha
en: Rose, honey, ... and if you heard, a sliver of blood.

speaker: Basim
en: Blood... I should have guessed. I had thought it might be iron.

speaker: Qabiha
en: Blood is born from iron, is it not? But because of that detail, it proves difficult to bring in large quantities.

speaker: Basim
en: If it is so exclusive it must be popular amongst officials I think I caught a scent of it near the Treasurer...

speaker: Qabiha
en: Ning uses the Qina'. She is quite taken with its rich mystique, as are many. Curious. You do not look like one who is interested in the art of perfumery.

speaker: Basim
en: It is unwise to judge someone by how they look.

speaker: Qabiha
en: Indeed. Did I not catch your name?

speaker: Basim
en: Basim.

speaker: Qabiha
en: Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: I must not waste any more of your time. I wish you a wonderful time at the Da'irat Al-mal, ya sayyidati (my lady).

speaker: Basim
en: So, the Treasurer is a she... and her name is Ning.

speaker: Basim
en: The auction should be starting soon.

speaker: The Host
en: Marhaban, As-salamu 'alaikum, Yassas, ni hao, hello! It is the time of year again to fulfill your deepest yearning, to listen to your heart's desire and purchase what God has shown us!

speaker: The Host
en: It brings me great joy to welcome all of you esteemed individuals to our annual Da'irat Al-mal!

speaker: The Host
en: First on our exclusive, captivating list of exotic odds and ends, we have a stunning statue from India. Made of ivory and crafted by the finest artisans, it will be a perfect addiction to any home!

speaker: The Host
en: Oh, what do we have! One bidder already.

speaker: The Host
en: No, two! Calling once, twice...

speaker: The Host
en: A third! Would anyone like to best that price? No? Sold! This piece goes to the lovely lady.

speaker: The Host
en: Next, we have a one of a kind ethereal beauty. This hairpin hails from the East, and look at the detail on the dragon! Perfect as a collectible, and even better as a gift for a certain lady friend you might have.

speaker: The Host
en: S-so, what is this piece worth to you, ya asdiqa'i (my friends)?

speaker: The Host
en: O-one! For the Treasurer who graced us with her presence.

speaker: Basim
en: Ning, the Treasurer.

speaker: The Host
en: Two! Any others?

speaker: The Host
en: We have a third, there!

speaker: The Host
en: Ho! Two owns it again! Number three, what will you do? How much do you want this, my friends! Reach into your heart, listen to your desire!

speaker: The Host
en: No one? Then, sold! To the handsome bearded man! This hairpin belongs to you now, sayyidi (sir). Now, for the third item...

speaker: The Host
en: Sold! To the man over there! Kindly collect your idem from my associate after the auction. Now, moving on...

speaker: The Host
en: ...and we thank you, once again, for making the Da'irat Al-mal a success! May your purses be ever full, and your heart ever longing!

speaker: Civilian 8
en: Did you see her? Her calmness, her grace... like a lone, shining star against a dark night. If only I could speak to her.

speaker: Civilian 9
en: Not a chance. I hear only members of the Merchant Guild can arrange an audience in her chambers

speaker: Civilian 8
en: Well, maybe if I found out where she purchased her robe, or her beautiful fan...

speaker: Basim
en: I have to get the hairpin from that man. Why would the Treasurer want it so badly?

speaker: Basim
en: Found him. Now, to quietly "borrow" the hairpin...

speaker: Eager Merchant
en: This beautiful hairpin is mine! What poor fools, they stood no chance against me. The look on the Treasurer's face... Ah, to have the chance to see that again when I present her with this gift!

speaker: Eager Merchant
en: Ah, let me take a look at the hairpin again... Maláka! (Fuck!) Where is it?

speaker: Basim
en: Intricate and beautiful indeed, but this is nothing like these ancient objects the Order is seeking. I must confront Ning.

speaker: Rich Merchant
en: I have an appointment with the Treasurer. Move aside.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Apologies. My instructions were clear. No brooch, no entry.

speaker: Rich Merchant
en: Do you know who I am? I need to speak to the Treasurer! I was called, summoned!

speaker: Merchant
en: This is proof that I am of the Merchant's Guild! Look! See!

speaker: Spice Merchant
en: With respect, that does not entitle you to three bags of saffron, two of vanilla, and a bottle of honey without a single coin.

speaker: Merchant
en: Impossible! Bah, this is a waste of my time!

speaker: Basim
en: This could be my only chance to meet the Treasurer. I must get that hairpin.

speaker: Spice Merchant
en: Hello, spices for you?

speaker: Basim
en: Trouble with customers?

speaker: Spice Merchant
en: No more than usual. These people from The Ivory Coin think themselves touched by God himself.

speaker: Basim
en: The Ivory Coin?

speaker: Spice Merchant
en: I... I should not speak about it. I do not know much, really.

speaker: Basim
en: Whatever you know can help me.

speaker: Basim
en: Is this enough for some information?

speaker: Basim
en: Then I will not bother you. Thank you.

speaker: Spice Merchant
en: Wait, do you not want any spices...?

speaker: Basim
en: Any more trouble with customers?

speaker: Spice Merchant
en: Not since earlier. What can I help you with?

speaker: Spice Merchant
en: Well... it will not hurt to tell you what I know. The Ivory Coin is an exclusive merchant's guild. They have a brooch that grants them access to certain places.

speaker: Basim
en: How do you obtain this brooch?

speaker: Spice Merchant
en: I hear only respected merchants are part of The Ivory Coin, and that you can only be invited by another member. They think their status gives them permission to take goods without coin. Hmph. Have you ever seen such vanity?

speaker: Basim
en: This is expected in Karkh. Thank you.

speaker: Soldier2
en: No brooch, no entry. You know how this works.

speaker: Civilian 10
en: Yes, but I left my brooch in there! Do you not see the problem here?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: No brooch, no entry.

speaker: Civilian 10
en: La'anak Allah! (May God curse you.)

speaker: Basim
en: An exclusive union for the merchants of high society. I should have expected this to exist.

speaker: Basim
en: The Chamber of Antiquities is the Treasurer's haven. I need to find a way in.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: I do not care what you have to do! Burn them, or murder their dogs if you have to!

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Understood, sayyidi (sir). We will retrieve your coin from the merchant's stall on the morrow, at all cost.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Why not today? Gah. You lot are getting more incompetent by the day. Useless.

speaker: Basim
en: This must be The Ivory Coin's brooch. Shiny.

speaker: Basim
en: I have both trinkets. The guard will have to let me in now.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum (Peace be upon you), I am here to see the Treasurer.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: On what business?

speaker: Basim
en: I have a gift for the Treasurer, if she will see me.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Only members of The Ivory Coin are allowed to enter. No brooch, no entry.

speaker: Basim
en: Here, the brooch. Is this sufficient?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: The Treasurer will only see individuals with exotic gifts to offer. Come back when you have one.

speaker: Basim
en: I...I am a simple merchant, searching for advice and wisdom.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: If you do not have exotic offerings and are not part of The Ivory Coin, be gone. There will be no audience for riff-raff.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum. (Peace be upon you),

speaker: Soldier 1
en: You again. What is it now?

speaker: Basim
en: I have something that she wants. A Chinese hairpin, form the auction. I also have my brooch with me, here.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Very well. You may enter.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: This way, sayyidi (sir).

speaker: Basim
en: I have been looking forward to meeting the Treasurer. It is an honor.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Indeed, sayyidi (sir). She is busy and her time only allows for a few rare appearances.

speaker: Basim
en: I have never seen so many treasures in one place.

speaker: Ning
en: This is of inferior make. I wonder if you really are the expert you claim to be.

speaker: Civilian 11
en: This plate is priceless, I swear it! Treasurer, Ning, if only you

speaker: Ning
en: Go. Leave the vase, but get the plate out of my sight. Perhaps the dogs in the souq can use it for their meals.

speaker: Civilian 11
en: Her standards are too high. One has to be careful not to get bitten in there.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Please refrain from speaking about the Treasurer inappropriately.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: You may enter.

speaker: Soldier 7
en: Please, step no further.

speaker: Ning
en: You are a new face.

speaker: Basim
en: My name is Basim. New to Baghdad, but not to trade. I deal mostly in fine antiques and collectibles.

speaker: Ning
en: You must have a good eye for detail then. What have you brought me, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: You know what I brought.

speaker: Ning
en: A man not to be toyed with. Come, show it to me!

speaker: Ning
en: Exquisite. Ever seen something like this? So perfect, so delicate.

speaker: Basim
en: No, but I am surprised that you have not.

speaker: Ning
en: I do have a penchant for them. When I was but a child, my sisters and I would tie our hair with sticks, adorn them with stone. I pretended they were the rarest gems. We had nothing, but we felt that we had it all. There are many reasons why people see me. For advice, a taste of power, and most often to win favor. Why have you come, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: As a fellow collector, I have heard much about you from others. Your extravagance, your taste. I wish to learn.

speaker: Ning
en: Did they say I was lucky? I loathe word. When I first arrived in Baghdad I was one of many seeking my fortune. Now, I have even the East wrapped around my fingers. I clawed my way here when many gave up, preferring to spare their nails. But me, I don't mind a few scratches, a bit of blood.

speaker: Basim
en: Surely there have been connections, the people you met that helped you get where you are.

speaker: Ning
en: No matter what others say, you only have yourself. No one else.

speaker: Ning
en: Argh! Who are you? You will regret this. Guards!

speaker: Ning
en: "Everything prospers when family is harmonious." Family? The word has no meaning. The notions even more so. Only the self hears the deepest whispers of your soul and accepts you whole.

speaker: Basim
en: No one lives alone.

speaker: Ning
en: But we die lonely. In the end, we are absolutely, simply, truly alone.

speaker: Basim
en: The... the jinni... again... I... I should return to the Bureau.

speaker: Soldier 8
en: The Treasurer, she's dead! Guards, help! Someone killed the Treasurer!

speaker: Monk
en: Holy father, grant me guidance!

speaker: Basim
en: What grief moves you to invoke your god so openly?

speaker: Monk
en: Ah! Perhaps my prayers have been answered. Could you help a humble monk pay his respects?

speaker: Basim
en: You are well armed for a monk.

speaker: Monk
en: I was a violent man in a former life, who now seeks to atone in service to God. Though I will admit, some of my old skills have served me well in performing His work.

speaker: Basim
en: I can respect a warrior who has found a higher calling. What is your need?

speaker: Monk
en: I seek a holy man buried in one of the older overgrown graves, but I cannot read the epitaphs written in your tongue.

speaker: Basim
en: A simple enough task. I will see what I can find.

speaker: Basim
en: "Benedict the Dark. A man of great appetites." I do not believe the Christians sanctify gluttony.

speaker: Basim
en: "Jon of Shiraz. He gambled more than he gained, but always shared his winnings." A generous man, but not one worthy of worship.

speaker: Basim
en: "Theodore the Bold, who held nothing sacred but remained consistent in his actions." Admirable to some perhaps, but he does not have the sound of a saint.

speaker: Basim
en: "Leo the Enlightened. His wisdom was only exceeded by his piousness." Ah, here is one deserving of some reverence.

speaker: Basim
en: Monk! I believe I have found your saint!

speaker: Monk
en: God be praised! I must retrieve the bones before we are discovered.

speaker: Basim
en: I thought you were here to pay respects, not rob a grave.

speaker: Monk
en: There is no theft. His bones belong to the Church and will do more good among the faithful than rotting in the ground.

speaker: Basim
en: If your church has no objection, then who am I to judge?

speaker: Monk
en: There is only One whose judgement matters, and I trust He will be forgiving.

speaker: Soldier
en: Hey! Stop what you are doing!

speaker: Basim
en: Unfortunately, the Caliph's men are not so tolerant of unlicensed gravedigging.

speaker: Soldier
en: Explain yourselves, you filthy shits, or die!

speaker: Monk
en: They are guilty of worse crimes. God forgive me, but there are times when violence is the only answer.

speaker: Basim
en: On that, we are agreed.

speaker: Monk
en: You know not what you do!

speaker: Basim
en: There was no other way to resolve this. These kinds of men understand only violence and cruelty.

speaker: Monk
en: You have performed God's Will, my friend. He will surely bless you with good fortune.

speaker: Basim
en: I answer to another calling... but I will not turn down a bit of extra luck.

speaker: House of Memories
en: was a virtual representation of one of Basim ibn Ishaq's genetic memories relived through the Animus.

speaker: Basim
en: At last, I am almost there... But... what will I say after all these years? Will he even want to see me? My father left me in Samarra for a reason... Still, if I can at least understand why...

speaker: Basim
en: The robbers were here... Though there is no sign of bloodshed...

speaker: Basim
en: Father! Are you here?

speaker: Basim
en: These are his possessions... But where is he?

speaker: Basim
en: I remember this toy.

speaker: Ishaq
en: Here, Basim. I made this for you.

speaker: Young Basim
en: Thank you, Father!

speaker: Ishaq
en: You like?

speaker: Young Basim
en: It is the best toy ever! I want to make toys like this when I grow up.

speaker: Ishaq
en: With patience and practice, you will.

speaker: Basim
en: We played this game the night before he left.

speaker: Young Basim
en: Father! Where you going?

speaker: Ishaq
en: To a place not meant for little ones.

speaker: Young Basim
en: Why can't I come with you? Why can't I come?

speaker: Ishaq
en: Do not cry, Basim. Remember, you are the one who smiles. But I must go. Dervis—he will take care of you now.

speaker: Young Basim
en: Father, please! Do not leave me! Is it because of the toy I broke?

speaker: Ishaq
en: No, Basim, no!

speaker: Young Basim
en: I am sorry! I will be good! I promise! Don't leave me! Please, Father!

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, yes, the book of bedtime songs...

speaker: Young Basim
en: Father, sing it again.

speaker: Ishaq
en: Again? But you should be asleep.

speaker: Young Basim
en: Please, Father.

speaker: Ishaq
en: Fine, just one more time. "We will float as one, through waters so wide, no harm will come, I will be by your side."

speaker: Guard 1
en: Make it quick!

speaker: Guard 2
en: So they really took the old fool?

speaker: Guard 3
en: I doubt he even noticed as they did. "Confused" does not begin to cover it.

speaker: Guard 2
en: Where did they take him?

speaker: Guard 3
en: Some camp up north, middle of nowhere. That is where their real chief holds court.

speaker: Guard 4
en: For the sake of the idiot farmers living around here, we must appear dutiful while investigating this so-called disappearance.

speaker: Guard 5
en: I heard even with 'Abis gone, his men still set ambushes all over the north of AlUla.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Hope to catch a few rich travelers, no doubt.

speaker: Guard 5
en: How do they manage without that madman barking orders?

speaker: Guard 6
en: Ah, who cares, as long as we get our share of whatever they steal.

speaker: Basim
en: Smoke from the House of Wisdom. What does it mean?

speaker: Civilian
en: Who burned our precious books? This is worse than the loss of the Great Library of Alexandria!

speaker: Fazil
en: People, calm yourselves! The fire was small and has been contained.

speaker: Civilian
en: Allah's wrath is upon us!

speaker: Fazil
en: Most of our books are safe. The danger has passed.

speaker: Basim
en: Old man! How did this fire start?

speaker: Fazil
en: Old man? Fazil Fahim is old. As old as the House of Wisdom, which he commands!

speaker: Basim
en: Forgive me, ustadhi (master). I spoke in haste. Can I help?

speaker: Fazil
en: No, the fire has been quenched by the Water Master's bucket brigades.

speaker: Basim
en: Who started these fires?

speaker: Fazil
en: Ruffians, I suppose. Enemies of the Caliph, to be exact.

speaker: Basim
en: What sort of books were they burning?

speaker: Fazil
en: It is too soon to tell.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps the Caretaker of Books would know.

speaker: Basim
en: I am searching for Ahmad ibn Musa.

speaker: Fazil
en: Ah yes, he has a workshop here, but I have not spoken to him lately.

speaker: Basim
en: Peace be upon you, elder. I shall go.

speaker: Basim
en: I still need to find Ahmad ibn Musa, but I should also speak to the Caretaker of Books in the library.

speaker: Nur
en: My horse... below... she is yours now. Good luck, my friend.

speaker: Basim
en: Nur... Our patrols, our training... it feels like a lifetime ago.

speaker: Basim
en: Steady... steady, girl. All is well. All is well. Your master left you in my care.

speaker: Basim
en: Our temple... Whatever lies beneath, I must see it for myself... no matter the cost.

speaker: Basim
en: All this blood... and death... is this what Qabiha meant by "preparing the way"? Nehal, please be safe, wherever you are.

speaker: Basim
en: Ya ilahi (Oh my God...) No way through... except maybe up.

speaker: Basim
en: Some of my clan still live. Mentor Rayhan among them.

speaker: Kabeer Al-Jund
en: For all your reputation, I must say, I expected a far stronger response to our presence here. "Mentor", they call you. Is that so? And what exactly is it you teach here, eh? All I see are dead men and women. Men and women who thought you had something to offer them. To teach them. And now, when these final few need you most... you choose silence.

speaker: Kabeer
en: Do you hear that? Your "Mentor" could tell us what we want to know. He could spare your lives, yet chooses not to. I am not a cruel man. But I am impatient. Show yourselves, and you will have a fighting chance of seeing tomorrow. No? Then... let us see what your Mentor values more. His secrets, or his students.

speaker: Kabeer
en: The Mentor has chosen silence. So be it.

speaker: Basim
en: Tabban! I need to quicken my pace. They do not deserve to die.

speaker: Kabeer
en: One thing I never understood about your kind... With all the killing you are famed for, why do you always wear white robes? There I go again, wasting my breath on a man who wishes to say nothing, no matter the cost, no matter the blood on his hands. Perhaps your disciples will enlighten me! Tell me what I wish to know, and no more need die this day. Surely there is one among you who knows what we have been sent here in search of. Why my men have fought to claim your temple. Come, speak with me! Tell me of it!

speaker: Kabeer
en: No one? I see. You there. Carve up another. See if any secrets spill out.

speaker: Basim
en: My brothers, my sisters... this has nothing to do with them. I cannot leave them to die.

speaker: Kabeer
en: Stoic until the end. Rayhan, was it? What shitty tales will be told of Rayhan the Silent? None. None at all. So indulge me! Do none of you care to ensure some legacy for your pathetic kin before they are all wiped out? What in your temple is so coveted by those who sent us? The first one to speak will survive the day. La jadwa. (Useless.) Kill them.

speaker: Kabeer
en: Keep your secrets, you pathetic kalb (dog). Those I serve have far more... fascinating methods of making you talk. That is the choice you have made. No matter. I get paid either way. Let us hope you at least keep some wine up here.

speaker: Basim
en: Quick. Silent. Unseen. That is my best chance... and theirs.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Do as you will.

speaker: Basim
en: Suqhan lakum! (Death to you!)

speaker: Rayhan
en: Basim! What... Alhamdulillah! (Praise be to God.) I do not see any others. Come, help me out of these restraints. Basim? What are you doing? Free me.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Basim, how... I thought you were in Baghdad. Where are the others? Roshan?

speaker: Basim
en: I came alone. For the same reason these men did. I know the truth, Mentor. About the temple and what it shelters. Our enemies told me as much. They urged me to seek it, because only I could.

speaker: Rayhan
en: You...? Thus the Order used the Tahirids to decimate Alamut. Because you... you are their key.

speaker: Basim
en: To what? What are you protecting that is worth all this bloodshed?

speaker: Rayhan
en: Ancient ground. For generations, it has been our duty to watch over it. Defend it from the Order, who seek to exploit its secrets. The temple houses its entrance but, Basim, even though it is forbidden... I have searched. There is no means to access it.

speaker: Basim
en: Then I will find a way myself.

speaker: Rayhan
en: You must not. It is what the Order wants, don't you see? If what we protect should fall into the wrong hands...

speaker: Basim
en: It will fall into mine. Look around you. At what the Order is prepared to unleash upon us.

speaker: Basim
en: If I can gain the knowledge they seek, it can be what finally gives us an edge in this endless war.

speaker: Basim
en: This is the way forward. For the Hidden Ones.

speaker: Hidden One
en: Shukran (Thank you), Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: The Temple... Let us finish this. Nothing and no one shall get in my way. Not when I am this close.

speaker: Basim
en: It will take more than you to stop me.

speaker: Basim
en: More of them ahead. Suffice to say I am on the right path.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: We should not be here. Our orders were to secure the temple, not to

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Not to enter it, I know! Damn the orders! You saw what we've fought through to get here. The men we've lost! You think we will gain anything once our masters acquire what they seek? You think we will be rewarded? Of course not. Whatever it is they want in here... it must be worth a fortune. Think of all the land you could buy. And the servants!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Will you both shut up! Just find it, quickly. We will all think a lot more clearly without you two bickering like a pair of idiots!

speaker: Basim
en: Now, to see if I can achieve what these intruders could not.

speaker: Basim
en: What magic is this? Wait... I know this symbol. (deep breath)

speaker: Roshan
en: I warned you what would happen.

speaker: Roshan
en: Last chance.

speaker: Roshan
en: Very well.

speaker: Basim
en: So it has come to this? Killing each other? Is this your idea of a brotherhood?

speaker: Roshan
en: The brotherhood is unified. There is no place for those who would set themselves above it.

speaker: Basim
en: Is that what you think I am doing?

speaker: Roshan
en: Wake up, Basim! You walk the Order's path! The very people you swore to fight against. You're fulfilling their mission, endangering the very thing you swore to defend. Free will!

speaker: Basim
en: And where is mine? How can I champion something denied to me? Your creed is flawed!

speaker: Basim
en: There must... must be a way... to break her. Roshan's shoulder... it is unprotected. Take out the shoulder. Her shoulder... That is how to break her. Take out her arm, take out her blade.

speaker: Basim
en: Last chance.

speaker: Basim
en: I trusted you! I gave you everything I had and you lied to me. You knew. Since the night we fled Anbar, you knew my truth.

speaker: Roshan
en: I only feared what it could spell. But I set my worries aside. I had to. You were but a young man, broken and alone. Desperate for guidance. Wanting to do good.

speaker: Basim
en: I am still here!

speaker: Roshan
en: No good can come from what lies beyond those doors.

speaker: Basim
en: Yield!

speaker: Basim
en: Yield.

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim! Leave her. Come.

speaker: Basim
en: I never wanted this. But I need to know.

speaker: Roshan
en: I do not want to lose you to what you may find in there. You do not have to look to the past, to know who you are. Who you can be. You can choose, Basim! Put your faith in me.

speaker: Basim
en: I tried. And in the end, you thought it best to control me. No different than our enemies.

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim. Over here.

speaker: Nehal
en: I... I know what this is.

speaker: Basim
en: The key...

speaker: Nehal
en: She will follow.

speaker: Basim
en: No. She cannot. You saw it yourself.

speaker: Basim
en: More of those objects. I wonder what truths lie within. What stories they serve to tell...

speaker: Basim
en: Whatever lies within carries grave importance. For the Hidden Ones, for the Order of the Ancients, for me. What have we walked into? Where has my path brought us?

speaker: Nehal
en: You do not want to know why anyone was brought to this place.

speaker: Basim
en: Are my eyes deceiving me? Are you seeing this? Nehal?

speaker: Nehal
en: I am... I am here.

speaker: Basim
en: Wherever we are, it was built long ago. To serve what purpose, I do not know.

speaker: Nehal
en: I do.

speaker: Basim
en: How?

speaker: Nehal
en: I... I do not know.

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal... you are worrying me.

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal, look in here.

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal, please, talk to me...

speaker: Nehal
en: No... No, no, no... no... no!

speaker: Basim
en: I know this place... Nehal?

speaker: Basim
en: Ugh!

speaker: Basim
en: It... it cannot be.

speaker: Nehal
en: Hrgh! Enough! Let me out of here!

speaker: Basim
en: How... What... what are you?

speaker: Nehal
en: Look! See for yourself!

speaker: Prisoner
en: srræsnos! dű hm làygw r zàrhàsi! (Enough, please! Let me out of here!)

speaker: Guard
en: Seylos! (Silence!)

speaker: Basim
en: That is...

speaker: Basim
en: No!

speaker: Basim
en: Show yourself! You dare to hide from me now? After all you have put me through! Where are you?

speaker: Basim
en: The jinni in my dreams. The figure from these visions. They are one and the same... Is this what I have been seeing? The memories of a life long ago? Are they mine? Is that why the jinni feels so real? My tormenter. The source of all that ails me. If this is so, then I must face you.

speaker: Basim
en: No... Why am I seeing this?

speaker: Basim
en: This space... As I move through it, I see nothing but the memories that stir my soul. In these moments of adversity is when I felt the jinni nearest. That unrelenting fear. Paralyzing me in my weakest state.

speaker: Basim
en: I never understood what it was born of, or why it haunted me so. But I am beginning to remember. I am in a cold cell. Begging for it all to stop.

speaker: Basim
en: Who I once was may seek retribution. But if I am to move beyond this pain, then what I want is peace.

speaker: Basim
en: It is time to put an end to this.

speaker: Basim
en: The cell. My cell. I am nearly there. No going back...

speaker: Basim
en: Agh! The jinni... I can hear it. (tense breathing)

speaker: Basim
en: I know you now. I see you for what you are.

speaker: Basim
en: A crippling memory from a past life.

speaker: Basim
en: And that is where you will remain.

speaker: Basim
en: It is over.

speaker: Nehal
en: ...No, Basim. It is only the beginning. For us. For what lies ahead. A deeper understanding of the world we left behind. And our place in it.

speaker: Basim
en: All my life I wrestled with who I was. Who I was meant to be. And there you were. All this time. The side of me I resisted. A reflection of who we... once were.

speaker: Nehal
en: Of who we shall be once more. There is so much that awaits us. A new world. Let me show you...

speaker: Basim
en: I will never see you again, will I?

speaker: Basim
en: Will I be... alone?

speaker: Nehal
en: You are never alone.

speaker: Basim
en: (catching breath) H-how...? How long has it been?

speaker: Roshan
en: It is done. You made your choice. Now I make mine.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Wada'an (farewell), Roshan bint-La'Ahad. It was an honor.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Come, Basim. We have much to discuss.

speaker: Basim
en: That we do, "Mentor".

speaker: Basim
en: This memory I buried of this place... this prison, the torture I suffered here... it festered for years, in darkness and dreams... masked as a jinni, to haunt and hollow me... until it consumed my waking life. But I have faced my past. My pain. Embraced it. I shed my skin once, in another time, another place. But I am whole again. I remember. And as for those who thought to bind me... should any of them still walk the earth, I so look forward to our reunion. But until that day... a new world awaits.

speaker: Basim
en: I must locate the proper spot to sound the signal.

speaker: Basim
en: The note I found on that robber spoke of a certain mark upon the ground.

speaker: Basim
en: This symbol is wrong. I must find the correct one.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, good, here it is. The right mark. Now, to gain entry, I must give the signal.

speaker: Basim
en: This is where it begins. My father is somewhere inside. I must find a way to gain entry into the fort's inner compound.

speaker: Basim
en: I should listen to these robbers. They could have valuable information.

speaker: Robber 1
en: Nimlot says the inner wall is weak in places, fit to crumble at any moment.

speaker: Robber 2
en: Too bad the Caliph's so-called architect cannot mend it. Not in his state.

speaker: Robber 1
en: This is no jest. Make sure no explosives remain too close or they may accidently blow a breach wide open.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: You! Come over here! I have never seen you here before.

speaker: Basim
en: I seek an audience with the one they call Nimlot.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: You wish to trade with him?

speaker: Basim
en: In a manner of speaking. But first, I must get past the gate.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: Seems you are looking to strike a bargain...

speaker: Basim
en: And what price do you set?

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: I trade in rare items—amulets, talismans, charms of protection. Offer me something of worth, and I will see you through that gate.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: It seems you have nothing of worth to me. Go, find something that might please me. The desert contains many rare treasures and charms.

speaker: Basim
en: I must not make any noise.

speaker: Basim
en: I trust this meets your requirements?

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: Very much so. We have a deal. Now, I will honor my end. You will follow me and carry one of my crates inside.

speaker: Basim
en: Am I to act as your servant?

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: You learn fast. Pick up that crate and follow me.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: Stay close, we must not draw attention.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: Speak no word. There are ears everywhere.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: Let us pass. I have a delivery for Nimlot.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: For appearances' sake, we must take this crate to the supply room.

speaker: Basim
en: You are risking much to help me.

speaker: Blackmarket merchant
en: I have my vices, but breaking a bargain is not one. You may set down the crate. And if anyone asks how you gained entry, keep me out of it.

speaker: Basim
en: I hold the key to this door.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps I can put these explosives to good use.

speaker: Basim
en: I need to find out what is stirring among these robbers.

speaker: Basim
en: What is happening over there?

speaker: Robber 3
en: If you ask me, Nimlot puts too much faith in that crooked astrologer's horoscopes.

speaker: Robber 4
en: This time it's not about the predictions.

speaker: Robber 3
en: Then what brings the charlatan here?

speaker: Robber 4
en: He stole an astrolabe on Nimlot's orders. A merchant in wants it, and Nimlot is always happy to oblige on such matters. Word is, the astrologer even killed a helpless old woman to get his hands on it. Cracked her skull wide open.

speaker: Robber 3
en: Ruthless dog! I did not think he had it in him. He is no better than we are!

speaker: Basim
en: The astrologer is as bad as the robbers... Still, his attire may serve me well as a disguise.

speaker: Astrologer
en: Why does Nimlot keep me waiting? Does he truly want the astrolabe?

speaker: Robber 5
en: You will see him when he's ready. For now, he has more urgent affairs to attend to.

speaker: Basim
en: Now is the time!

speaker: Basim
en: The "astrologer" is ready to make his grand entrance... Hopefully it is enough to persuade any guards to grant me passage.

speaker: Basim
en: Open this door at once!

speaker: Robber 6
en: Who is there?

speaker: Basim
en: It is the astrologer. I bring the astrolabe Nimlot requested.

speaker: Robber 6
en: Nimlot is busy. You must wait.

speaker: Basim
en: I have other matters to attend to. If Nimlot wants the astrolabe, he must see me now.

speaker: Robber 6
en: Fine, fine, keep your temper.

speaker: Basim
en: None of them are the man I seek.

speaker: Basim
en: Father?

speaker: Civilian
en: Who are you to call me father? I have no offspring, spare me your delusions!

speaker: Basim
en: Is that my father suffering such torments?

speaker: Basim
en: No... this is not my father.

speaker: Tortured man
en: Thank you... I feared it was the end for me.

speaker: Basim
en: You can show your gratitude by telling me where I can find Nimlot.

speaker: Tortured man
en: He locked himself in the tower... but to pass through, you will need the key. It is in the captain's pocket.

speaker: Robber
en: You, stay right where you are.

speaker: Basim
en: Nimlot is in the tower... and he alone knows where my father is located.

speaker: Nimlot
en: Astrologer! You are early, and I am busy with other

speaker: Nimlot
en: Let me correct myself. You, Basim, are on time.

speaker: Basim
en: Where is my father?

speaker: Nimlot
en: "Where is my father...?" I could ask the same of you.

speaker: Basim
en: What are you blathering on about? You think you can use my father as a hostage to save your own life?

speaker: Nimlot
en: That was never the plan.

speaker: Basim
en: Then what!?

speaker: Nimlot
en: To watch you suffer as I slowly slit the old pig's throat.

speaker: Basim
en: Why involve him? Your fight is with me!

speaker: Nimlot
en: Indeed. You truly have no idea, do you? Let me demystify it for you... A father... for a father.

speaker: Basim
en: Your father?

speaker: Nimlot
en: What was it you called him? Al-Ghul?

speaker: Basim
en: You... are his son?

speaker: Nimlot
en: Was, Basim. I was his son.

speaker: Basim
en: Killing Al-Ghul was an act of justice.

speaker: Nimlot
en: Ah yes, the Hidden Ones and their moral high ground. You believe so fiercely in your spotless justice. But what of Ishaq ibn Khalid? You only know him as a memory. And yet here you are, ready to kill anyone standing in your way.

speaker: Basim
en: Your father was a monster!

speaker: Nimlot
en: Your kind never pause to consider the consequence of your deeds, do you? You think of justice as an end in itself, yet justice is consequence.

speaker: Basim
en: Where is my father?

speaker: Nimlot
en: As I said, you will kill anyone standing in your way... I stand in your way.

speaker: Basim
en: Father?

speaker: Nimlot
en: I know exactly what you are thinking... Can you reach me before I reach him? Of course, if my dagger parts his flesh, even as yours parts mine... for me, it will be worth it.

speaker: Basim
en: Speak your final words.

speaker: Nimlot
en: Some months ago, after many years away, I returned home to Baghdad to see my father one last time... But as we were merely starting to rekindle our ties... You stole that from me. My chance to show him I had made something of myself!

speaker: Basim
en: Your father deserved death... You... deserve death.

speaker: Nimlot
en: Who are you to decree a man's death, Basim ibn Ishaq?

speaker: Nimlot
en: Your prize... Choke on it.

speaker: Basim
en: Father... Father!

speaker: Ishaq
en: Are you looking for your father, young man? I do not think he is here... I do not like this place, I must go.

speaker: Ishaq
en: You do not smile much, young man. That... that thing... Where did you get it?

speaker: Basim
en: In Samarra.

speaker: Ishaq
en: Why has Samarra changed so much? It is very dark... I do not like it.

speaker: Basim
en: What do you remember of Samarra? Of home?

speaker: Ishaq
en: I have lived here all my life. But now... The Khalifa says that I must go. To another place. No coming back.

speaker: Basim
en: And what of your son?

speaker: Ishaq
en: Yes, yes... Basim, that is his name. He is my son. My boy must not suffer for my failure. The journey I must take, the dangers. The shame... He will not taste them. They are mine. Alone. My son, he has a future... I have none.

speaker: Basim
en: Why not tell him this?

speaker: Ishaq
en: He is too young. He cannot understand. I must do something.

speaker: Basim
en: Sit. What must you do?

speaker: Ishaq
en: I will see the sunrise one more time... before I leave Samarra. There is a tomb out there... Like the ones in AlUla... I never had the chance to witness the monuments of that land.... Only... what I have read... in stories...

speaker: Basim
en: My father once read those same stories to me. Do you want to see the sunrise from near the tomb? It will be just like AlUla. I can take you there. We will go together.

speaker: Ishaq
en: Good, good.

speaker: Basim
en: Do you... do you remember your wife?

speaker: Ishaq
en: Wife? I have no wife. Not since Basim's mother.

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me about her. Who was she?

speaker: Ishaq
en: I once saw a young woman in the bazaar, brought here from across the sea. From a land far to the north, they said... Such a delicate beauty... eyes like the bluest sky in winter... And her smile... Basim inherited my looks, but the way he smiles... that belongs to his mother. She left this world too soon... taken by a sickness before she could see more of it.

speaker: Basim
en: What was her name?

speaker: Ishaq
en: I... I cannot recall. It is gone.

speaker: Basim
en: After you left Samarra, where did you journey?

speaker: Ishaq
en: I have not left Samarra. I am here even now. Though that time draws to an end.

speaker: Basim
en: Then... where do you wish to go?

speaker: Ishaq
en: I would dearly love to behold the (Córdoba) in ... And one day, the ancient marvels of AlUla. They say those wonders are unsurpassed.

speaker: Basim
en: My father spoke of Qubbat al-Sakhrah, that sacred dome in Al-Quds (Jerusalem).

speaker: Ishaq
en: Ah yes, it would be a sight! Yet for grandeur, surely nothing compares to al-Ahram, the great pyramids of Misr!

speaker: Basim
en: Imagine scaling their heights and gazing out over endless sands!

speaker: Ishaq
en: Truly, none have dared such a feat!

speaker: Basim
en: Of all the cities, Qustantinīyah (Constantinople) is the one I feel drawn to most... though I cannot understand why.

speaker: Ishaq
en: Yes... home to Aya Sofiya. They say she is the grandest and loveliest of all kanīsa (cathedrals). How I wish I could behold her beauty. But my time is much too brief...

speaker: Basim
en: One day, I shall journey to Qustantinīyah... and you will be with me. In my heart.

speaker: Ishaq
en: What is that you say? Your heart?

speaker: Basim
en: It is nothing.

speaker: Basim
en: Look, we are nearly at the tomb.

speaker: Ishaq
en: I wish my son could see this... Basim, the one who smiles... He is a good boy... He will grow into a fine man one day.

speaker: Ishaq
en: It is time. I must go... I will not be coming back.

speaker: Ishaq
en: Tell my little Basim... Tell him one day, when his time comes, we will be together again. Until then, he has a life to live... Tell him that, if you see him.

speaker: Basim
en: I will tell him.

speaker: Ishaq
en: So... you have a smile after all...

speaker: Dervis
en: Well? Did you find him?

speaker: Basim
en: A mere echo of the man I once knew. Time has wrought its changes. Yet... my heart remains thankful.

speaker: Dervis
en: I do not understand?

speaker: Basim
en: I have faced my past, Dervis. Few get that chance. Now, I must look toward the future. Toward the man I am destined to become.'

speaker: Basim
en: Fuladh has gone ahead to scout a way into the Damascus Gate Prison. I should find him. But before I do, it may serve me well to seek out this blacksmith. Any improvements he could offer would prove useful.

speaker: Fuladh
en: There it is. As cruel and unforgiving as I remember.

speaker: Basim
en: You were once imprisoned here?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Oh, no, I have never been inside. In fact, I have never stood close than this very place. It was from here that I would fly my kite high over these prison walls. It had an unique pattern, you see. One I stitched together with my father when I was just a boy. So here I came day after day, hoping for a gust that would take it high enough so that he would see it and know that I was here. I do not know if he ever did.

speaker: Basim
en: I know this pain. And I am sorry for yours.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I am not. Such pains forge our paths. Remind us of who we are. Who we can be.

speaker: Basim
en: Speaking of paths, I see only one. And it is not inviting.

speaker: Fuladh
en: No. We need to find a way to get you inside without being seen.

speaker: Basim
en: Could this help?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Where did you get that?

speaker: Basim
en: Beshi. He told me these tokens command a high value among the common folk.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Indeed. You could perhaps bribe the guards to look the other way. Or enlist the help of some merchants.

speaker: Basim
en: I shall see what flavor best suits me.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I will take my leave and return to the Bureau. Waffaqaka Allah. (May God grant you success.)

speaker: Basim
en: Are you men with Ali?

speaker: Rebel
en: We were. But it has been weeks since we have seen him and the rebels have all but disbanded.

speaker: Basim
en: That is only temporary. Ali is being held in this prison.

speaker: Rebel
en: Ali! Here? I feared him dead..

speaker: Basim
en: I will free him, but I need your help to get me inside.

speaker: Rebel
en: And who are you? We want nothing more than to see our leader returned but... how do I know you can be trusted?

speaker: Basim
en: Beshi told me I could exchange this token for your help. What say you?

speaker: Rebel
en: If he gave you this, he must hold you in high regard. We will take care of the guards. Watch us closely, then make your move.

speaker: Basim
en: It stinks of sweat and hopelessness.

speaker: Basim
en: Lords, you are shrewd men of business. Care to hear a proposition?

speaker: Merchant
en: So long as it is an attractive one, my friend. What is it?

speaker: Basim
en: I need to go into the prison. Unnoticed. I thought perhaps you could let me pose as one of your aids.

speaker: Merchant
en: Hmm... possibly. And in exchange?

speaker: Basim
en: This token. Do you recognize it?

speaker: Merchant
en: Well, well... an attractive proposition indeed! Stay close to me, and follow my lead.

speaker: Merchant
en: Guards, if you would please displace yourselves.

speaker: Soldier
en: Yes, yes.

speaker: Merchant
en: Please, give way. Move, please. Hadhari! (Look out!)

speaker: Basim
en: I shall not trouble you further. My thanks, sadeeqi (friend). Into the lion's den we go.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Where are you returning from smelling like that?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Where do you think?

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Ah. The "dungeon". Is the jailer poking truths out of our mouthy friend?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Only insults and globs of spit, both of which are equally foul.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Eh, give it time. It is all part of the method, is it not?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: How should I know? I am not a mad man...

speaker: Basim
en: Ali has been taken somewhere beneath the prison and likely tortured. I need to hurry.

speaker: Basim
en: Who did this to you?

speaker: Civilian
en: The... jailer...

speaker: Basim
en: Where is he?

speaker: Civilian
en: With another... beneath us. Death... will come for him soon.

speaker: Basim
en: He may be speaking of Ali. I pray I am not too late.

speaker: Elder 1
en: I never thought demons could walk the earth but that man... is evil.

speaker: Elder 2
en: Do not lose hope. That is what the jailer wants. He wants to break us.

speaker: Elder 1
en: He already has.

speaker: Jailer
en: I thought you would have had your fill by now. But still you persist. Not to worry. There are ways to encourage you along. Your friend in the white hood. You are to tell me all about him. Who he is. Where he hails from.

speaker: Ali
