en: You mother's arse.

speaker: Jailer
en: I can keep doing this, little rodent. The question is, can you?

speaker: Ali
en: Let us find out together, shall we?

speaker: Jailer
en: A slow death it is.

speaker: Ali
en: And you are?

speaker: Basim
en: Basim. Friend to Nur. Let us save the details for another time. We need to get you out of here.

speaker: Ali
en: Slow yourself, ya 'azeezi (my dear boy). We cannot leave, not yet. I need to get into the guards' quarters.

speaker: Basim
en: What for?

speaker: Ali
en: It is Al-Ghul you are after, is it not? The guards of this prison serve him. They take shifts escorting groups of prisoners to dig sites under the cover of night. If we can find their orders, we may know where Al-Ghul is going next. Is that reason enough?

speaker: Basim
en: Stay close to me. Stay low. And do not

speaker: Ali
en: Oh, come Basim. I know how to defend myself.

speaker: Basim
en: Really? What with?

speaker: Ali
en: Let's try to not get in each other's way. Tell me, Basim, because I must know... just how did you make it down here?

speaker: Basim
en: Easy. I sucked in my belly and wiggled through the cracks.

speaker: Ali
en: Take it as a compliment. I know your kind like to frolic in the dark but even the world's greatest thief would steer clear of this prison.

speaker: Basim
en: Ali, one day I will tell you all about my past. Then you will understand.

speaker: Ali
en: Such a tease.

speaker: Ali
en: The guards' room is through that door.

speaker: Soldier
en: There they are! Quickly!

speaker: Soldier
en: They're in here!

speaker: Basim
en: We will not have much time.

speaker: Soldier
en: Break it down!

speaker: Basim
en: Ali!

speaker: Ali
en: I heard you!

speaker: Basim
en: Over there! By the armor. Hurry!

speaker: Ali
en: I have it!

speaker: Basim
en: Take it to Roshan, my master. She is with your rebels at the watermill stronghold. I will slow the guards. Now go!

speaker: Basim
en: The Mazalim courts are close. Dervis once told me it is where the commons can appeal when justice itself is dealt unjustly. My father once said, to know the measure of a man, ask those who work beneath him. These judges must know the Governor better than most.

speaker: Basim
en: Greetings, sayyidi (sir). I wonder if I could ask you some questions about the Governor, Muhammad ibn Tahir.

speaker: Basim
en: Would you accept this token of appreciation from a humble citizen?

speaker: Basim
en: I serve justice, not spoil it. Take your money.

speaker: Basim
en: You drive a hard bargain. Too hard.

speaker: Basim
en: I will see what I can do.

speaker: Basim
en: You drive a hard bargain. Too hard.

speaker: Basim
en: I will see what I can do.

speaker: Basim
en: A little ill for a greater good. But it leaves a bad taste.

speaker: Civilian
en: Abu 'Abdallah should be tried for treason. If her were in my court, why I... Well, it is better left unsaid.

speaker: Basim
en: I have what you asked for.

speaker: Basim
en: Let me think about it.

speaker: Basim
en: I will see what I can do.

speaker: Basim
en: I am, but your price is too steep.

speaker: Basim
en: Now... what do you know about the Governor?

speaker: Basim
en: That is all you know? You work here. Muhammad ibn Tahir keeps office at the courts!

speaker: Basim
en: You are whom I seek. Lead, and I will follow. I see you now. Come, lead me to what it is I truly seek. There you are. Now lead on.

speaker: Basim
en: They are gone. Today, I was to hasty. Tomorrow, I must be better. Tabban (Damn it), Basim. I got too close. I will have to try again tomorrow.

speaker: Basim
en: That messenger could lead me to the Governor's office... and whatever secrets he buries there.

speaker: Basim
en: There you are, just as I thought.

speaker: Messenger
en: Stay alert... something is amiss.

speaker: Soldier
en: Yes, sayyidi (sir).

speaker: Basim
en: Good. Now stay where I can see you, would you?

speaker: Basim
en: Lost. I can almost here Roshan scolding me now. Perhaps I can redeem this failure tomorrow.

speaker: Basim
en: Not good enough. Tomorrow it is. And I must remain unseen.

speaker: Basim
en: Dervis always warned me I would be dragged to the Shurta. Who would have imagined I would walk in willingly?

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Poverty was my only crime! Free me from these chains! Please!

speaker: Elder
en: Sa'idni! (Help me!) I cannot bear this any longer.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Alhamdulillah! (Thank God!)

speaker: Basim
en: Fi amanillah, ya sadeeqi. (May God protect you, my friend.)

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Has the governor returned?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: I am not sure. I did not see him go upstairs.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: It's been mad in the streets today. If it's not Abu 'Abdallah's thugs sowing chaos, it's the damn rebels!

speaker: Soldier 4
en: It's all we can do to keep riots from breaking out. The Governor has a plan. He will see us through this storm.

speaker: Basim
en: Muhammad ibn Tahir's office, at last.

speaker: Basim
en: Abu 'Abdallah swears allegiance to the Caliph, and that he will not seek the throne himself...

speaker: Basim
en: "Ocean, Desert, Cobra, Dove." It seems he is an admirer of Arib the Poet.

speaker: Basim
en: A man who puppets the powerful, who seeks to purge the Hidden Ones at Alamut... I have seen enough.

speaker: Muhammad
en: You can tell your masters I've had copies made. Shred that page, slit my throat, our bargain stands.

speaker: Basim
en: My masters?

speaker: Muhammad
en: The masked cabal, the Order of... I don't care. Are you not in their service?

speaker: Basim
en: Are you not in their service?

speaker: Muhammad
en: I serve the Caliphate. I serve Allah. And I do it without hiding my face. Now, if you'll excuse me.

speaker: Basim
en: Why were you giving commands to Wasif al-Turki? A member of the Order?

speaker: Muhammad
en: The brute was stoking the fire of a thousand rebellions. Thankfully someone spared me the trouble of putting him down. A Hidden One, I heard. Are you the one to thank?

speaker: Basim
en: I read your letters. You forced your cousins to remove their protection from Alamut. You sold us out to our enemies!

speaker: Muhammad
en: And brought peace to Baghdad. You've already helped yourself to the receipt.

speaker: Basim
en: Abu 'Abdallah's Oath of Allegiance? What does he have to do with anything?

speaker: Muhammad
en: His ambition would have torn the Caliphate apart. I offered the Order Alamut, they gave me assurance he'd threaten us no more.

speaker: Basim
en: So to trap a fox you loose a wolf? The Order will see Baghdad burn, Governor! History will judge you for this.

speaker: Muhammad
en: History can hang me for it! I'll leave this world knowing that there is courage in compromise!

speaker: Basim
en: There is also cowardice!

speaker: Muhammad
en: How old are you? Twenty? I was your age when I came to this city. Righteous beyond reproach.

speaker: Basim
en: What happened?

speaker: Muhammad
en: I grew up. If you really wish to spare Alamut, turn that blade on your enemies.

speaker: Basim
en: Give me their name. The one you brokered the deal with.

speaker: Muhammad
en: I could. But if you fail, then I die... and I'd prefer not to. Now, I have things to do. No hard feelings.

speaker: Muhammad
en: GUARDS!

speaker: Basim
en: So the day ends with me fleeing the Shurta after all.

speaker: Soldier
en: Quick, to the Governor!

speaker: Basim
en: Order or no, Governor Muhammad is no friend to the Hidden Ones.

speaker: Child 1
en: You will break your neck!.

speaker: Child 2
en: You are going to get caught!

speaker: Young Eagle
en: Stop shouting at me!

speaker: Basim
en: Who is the brave little squirrel up there?

speaker: Child 1
en: He is not a squirrel, his name is "Young Eagle"! We should not have dared him to go up there, but he was being so boastful! Now we're all going to get in trouble!

speaker: Basim
en: I will get him down.

speaker: Young Eagle
en: Give me a moment!

speaker: Basim
en: That child looks like he has gotten himself into a tricky situation.

speaker: Basim
en: The boy is quite a climber.

speaker: Young Eagle
en: If you come close, I will jump!

speaker: Basim
en: My name is Basim, and I climbed up here without thinking it through. Do you think you could help me get down?

speaker: Basim
en: When I was your age, I did all kinds of foolish things to impress my friends.

speaker: Young Eagle
en: I did not do it for them, I did it for the Hidden Ones.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah. The Hidden Ones.

speaker: Young Eagle
en: Not everyone believes in them, but I do. They're the true protectors of the people. They were the ones who avenged my mother. Not the Caliph or his men. The Hidden Ones did that.

speaker: Basim
en: I see. And you thought this would get their attention? Climbing up here?

speaker: Young Eagle
en: I heard they can dive from great heights and not get hurt. But I cannot do something unless I see someone else do it first.

speaker: Basim
en: Do you think you can do it if I showed you?

speaker: Basim
en: You see? I am unharmed! Now, you go!

speaker: Young Eagle
en: I cannot!

speaker: Basim
en: Yes, you can! Do not overthink it! You simply need to have faith!

speaker: Young Eagle
en: I am ... fine! Gimme a second...

speaker: Basim
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Young Eagle
en: No ... nothing broken.

speaker: Basim
en: You are a fast learner!

speaker: Young Eagle
en: I told you. I can do anything if only someone shows me first.

speaker: Basim
en: That is a valuable talent. Be sure to have a good teacher next time you try something risky like that.

speaker: Young Eagle
en: You could teach me.

speaker: Basim
en: I am no teacher. I still have much to learn.

speaker: Young Eagle
en: No, you are a good teacher. You teach by example. A-are you.../

speaker: Basim
en: Seek me out when your voice begins to break. Then we will talk.

speaker: Child 1
en: Wah, that was amazing! Come on, Hytham! Before the mu'azzin catches us!

speaker: Young Eagle
en: I am coming!

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: Not my son as well! I cannot lose him like his father!

speaker: Civilian
en: Maybe he's safe somewhere. He could be lost.

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: No. He is gone. I haven't even had a chance to gather flowers for my husband's funeral and now my son is gone too.

speaker: Basim
en: This must be the place. Poor woman. I will need to win her trust.

speaker: Basim
en: Excuse me.

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: Who are you? What do you want?

speaker: Basim
en: Forgive me, I did not mean to startle you. The teahouse owner told me of your trouble. Perhaps I can help.

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: I do not see how. I don't know you.

speaker: Basim
en: You need flowers for your husband's burial. I too once lost those close to me, but could not bury them. It would be an honor if you let me do for you what I could not do for my friends. I will gather these flowers.

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: My husband often brought some White Savory to me. If you bring me some, I will leave them at his grave once he is buried, as my final gift.

speaker: Basim
en: It will be done.

speaker: Basim
en: The flowers will be nearby. I should look around.

speaker: Basim
en: These look like the flowers I need.

speaker: Basim
en: These are beautiful flowers. My friends would have approved.

speaker: Basim
en: I brought the flowers, with my sympathy.

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: They are such elegant flowers. My husband loved them. Thank you. Is there something I can do for you?

speaker: Basim
en: I am trying to find who is taking slaves from Jarjaraya. I know your son is missing.

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: Yes. I lost his father. It would be more than I can bear if I lost him too.

speaker: Basim
en: Can you tell me what he was doing before he went missing?

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: When his father was taken, he became very unhappy. He started going out at night. Last night, he never returned.

speaker: Basim
en: I will look around. There might be something here that tells what happened.

speaker: Basim
en: I could pick up her son's tracks around here.

speaker: Basim
en: There are a lot of tracks here. The tracks lead to that small building. I need to find a way inside.

speaker: Basim
en: The oil is low. He was working late.

speaker: Basim
en: A letter! He mentions a nearby farm. I should let his mother know what I have found.

speaker: Basim
en: I found a letter from your son. He was looking for the men who took his father.

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: That foolish boy!

speaker: Basim
en: He mentioned a nearby farm. Do you know what he was talking about?

speaker: Zanj Widow
en: Oh no. That is Dogan's farm. It is crawling with mercenaries. If he went there... Please! Find my son!

speaker: Basim
en: If he lives, I will send him back to you. You have my word.

speaker: Basim
en: Dogan's farm will be heavily guarded. I should return to Ali and discuss the next move.

speaker: Merchant
en: Come, friend! Over here!

speaker: Basim
en: How may I be of service?

speaker: Merchant
en: A band of four robbers keep attacking my caravans.

speaker: Basim
en: What would you have me do?

speaker: Merchant
en: Their camp is at Al Khuraymat. Deal with them so they never trouble me again. But please, let their deaths seem like misfortune... Otherwise I may face retribution.

speaker: Basim
en: All who perish, either these four or any who get in my way, shall bear the mark of mischance, nothing more.

speaker: Basim
en: It is done. To any who chance upon them, the dead will appear to be the most unlucky scoundrels to have ever roamed this land.

speaker: Basim
en: Time to leave.-->

speaker: Basim
en: Back to where it all began.

speaker: Basim
en: Now, a door. It cannot be hard to find.

speaker: Basim
en: Hmm... Iftah ya simsim (Open sesame.)

speaker: Basim
en: That worked. Even the Banu Musa would be impressed. Now, to find the King of Thieves.

speaker: Basim
en: A man's life is not a loose end. The King of these Thieves shall pay.

speaker: Thief 1
en: ...the burst of fire as it emerges from the sheathe... If only the King would let us take a few swings.

speaker: Thief 2
en: You wish.

speaker: Thief 1
en: And it cost him no coin too!

speaker: Thief 2
en: When you are us, most things come free.

speaker: The King of Thieves
en: You let the girl live? I must have overestimated the lot of you.

speaker: The King of Thieves
en: Who is this now? Did Ali Baba's daughter send a loyal pup instead? What a waste of my time.

speaker: Basim
en: I see that you are no legend. You are just a man.

speaker: The King of Thieves
en: Ever watched as the skin blisters from pure fire?

speaker: Basim
en: You talk too much.

speaker: The King of Thieves
en: Dance, dance! You can do better than that! Stop. Moving!

speaker: Basim
en: You besmirch the name of kings and thieves.

speaker: Thief
en: La! King! La'anakum Allah!

speaker: Murjana
en: I'm sorry, I took longer—He is...

speaker: Basim
en: Gone.

speaker: Murjana
en: It was all just smoke and mirrors. Clever tricks, illusions... He had us all fooled.

speaker: Basim
en: Not for long.

speaker: Murjana
en: The blood has been paid. I thought I would feel lighter.

speaker: Murjana
en: Here, payment for your services.

speaker: Basim
en: What will you do now?

speaker: Murjana
en: I will join a caravan to Samarkand. When my father was alive, we saw many cities and partook in the joys life had to offer. Now, he is dead. I have nothing to stay for.

speaker: Basim
en: Your father's wish for you came true in the end.

speaker: Murjana
en: That it did, but not at a cost I desired. But I will go this road alone, and meet my father when it ends.

speaker: Basim
en: I wish you well, Murjana. I hope we find each other again, some day.

speaker: Murjana
en: You will find me, but I doubt I could find you, man of the shadow. Wada'an (Farewell), Hidden One.

speaker: Basim
en: Goodbye, Murjana. May Allah light your path.

speaker: Basim
en: You seek some assistance?

speaker: Farmer
en: For the sake of my beautiful Bahja, I have come far to buy the resin of the poppy, and paid handsomely for it.

speaker: Basim
en: Bahja? I take it she is ill?

speaker: Farmer
en: Her teeth trouble her greatly, poor girl. She cannot chew a single mouthful, and I fear she will waste away.

speaker: Basim
en: So you no longer posses the resin?

speaker: Farmer
en: It was seized by a band of crooked soldiers located in this camp.

speaker: Basim
en: I will retrieve the resin and return it to you.

speaker: Farmer
en: I beg you, sneak in and avoid shedding blood. See those robbers over there? Doubtless they covet the resin as well.

speaker: Basim
en: For poor Bahja's sake, I must make haste.

speaker: Basim
en: These rogues know how to move unseen. I must not let them reach the prize before me.

speaker: Basim
en: In stealth, these fools are no match for a Hidden One. With this resin, Bahja's pain will soon be eased.

speaker: Basim
en: Well met again.

speaker: Farmer
en: You are back!

speaker: Basim
en: Here is the poppy resin, and no blood was spilled in its retrieval.

speaker: Farmer
en: Thank you! Bahja, the sweetest of all camels, will be most grateful.

speaker: Basim
en: Bahja is a camel?

speaker: Farmer
en: What else could she be? Now then, time to administer this resin.-->

speaker: Basim
en: Young lady, what troubles you that you weep so bitterly?

speaker: Young woman
en: Let me be. Let me die.

speaker: Basim
en: Do not say such things. What is the trouble that brings these tears to your eyes?

speaker: Young woman
en: The courtyard. I left something within its walls that I must retrieve. I must! But those horrible men, they will not allow me inside.

speaker: Basim
en: What do they say? What is happening within its walls?

speaker: Young woman
en: I am afraid to ask. They frighten me. Would you try to get it for me please? My journal. It is everything to me.

speaker: Basim
en: I will try.

speaker: Basim
en: I have learnt some things about your story, as you well expected to hear upon my return.

speaker: Young woman
en: Then you have retrieved my journal. Will you please return it to me?

speaker: Basim
en: There were a hundred ways you might have found to avoid spilling his blood.

speaker: Young woman
en: No! He...

speaker: Basim
en: The authorities will see this and decide your fate, not I.

speaker: Young woman
en: No...

speaker: Basim
en: By all accounts, your father seems to have been a wicked man, and although one might argue that he did not deserve to die... You did not deserve the fate that he had in store for you.

speaker: Young woman
en: Then you understand.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps I understand enough. Be well.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: She's done for. She should have paid them off the first time they threatened her.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Do you blame her? I find myself only scraping by with this new "tax" on our stalls.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Business is not easy...

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Broken, completely destroyed! Those guards, they know no mercy.

speaker: Civilian 5
en: This is nothing. Do you know what they are doing to the perfume merchant?

speaker: Merchant
en: Do not touch those bottles! They're a special import! I just need more time, please...

speaker: Soldier
en: You have wasted enough of ours. Now, stop begging. How about we take a walk instead? Somewhere far away...

speaker: Perfume Stall Guard Captain
en: This is taking too long! I have somewhere to be, and this is hardly worth the coin they pay me.

speaker: Soldier
en: Cut off a finger. Maybe that will loosen her coin purse.

speaker: Perfume Stall Guard Captain
en: No coin, no safety. You know this. Or, we can just take your perfume as payment.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum. (Peace be upon you.)

speaker: Perfume Stall Guard Captain
en: This is not your concern. Move along.

speaker: Basim
en: Maybe this can free your time.

speaker: Perfume Stall Guard Captain
en: Hmm. Perhaps it can.

speaker: Perfume Stall Guard Captain
en: We have worked hard, men! Time for a rest.

speaker: Soldier
en: What? Wait we are still

speaker: Perfume Stall Guard Captain
en: Do not question me. Let's go!

speaker: Basim
en: What did yo do to incur such aggression from the guards?

speaker: Merchant
en: I did nothing! I... I'm only short of coin. Business is business, but I do not have the means to pay their tax.

speaker: Basim
en: Are your wares moving slow?

speaker: Merchant
en: No, but in recent times they have increased the coin requested. Therein lies the trouble.

speaker: Basim
en: Not just for you, but for others as well?

speaker: Merchant
en: Mostly for people like us who are not from here, or not of the same faith. We find it's hard to feel safe in Karkh. I have a shipment that's late. I fear my goods and camels might have been seized by the guards. They should have arrived with some merchants bound for the Da'irat Al-mal. If I could ask a favor, my friend, please look for them.

speaker: Basim
en: Very well.

speaker: Merchant
en: They should be along the road that leads to the south gate of Baghdad.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah! I might catch them at the watering hole along the southern road.

speaker: Merchant
en: Thank you, sayyidi (sir).

speaker: Basim
en: The road beyond the south of Baghdad... I should see if I can find those stranded merchants.

speaker: Basim
en: The merchants should be down this road, perhaps near a ridge for shelter.

speaker: Basim
en: That camp must be where the merchants are.

speaker: Merchant
en: Halt! Who goes?

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum. (Peace be upon you.) I was sent by a friend of yours who was worried for your safety.

speaker: Merchant
en: As you can tell from the horse's head, she was right to be. We do not know what to make of this...

speaker: Basim
en: Let me help. Perhaps I can find out what happened.

speaker: Merchant
en: We would be grateful.

speaker: Basim
en: The culprit must have left a clue.

speaker: Basim
en: Footprints... and a blood trail. The horse's head was carried to the center of the camp.

speaker: Merchant 2
en: My horse, my sweet Legume! Maláka! Who would do such a terrible deed?

speaker: Merchant 3
en: Do not cast your eyes on me. I did no such evil!

speaker: Basim
en: The head is cut clean. Must have been a sharp blade.

speaker: Basim
en: Was this your horse?

speaker: Merchant 2
en: He is claimed by Hades now! Not only do I have to worry about Baghdad's ridiculous thirst for coin, now I must be concerned about my livestock! Maláka! Rest in peace, Legume...

speaker: Basim
en: What happened here?

speaker: Merchant
en: It happened in the dark of night. I could not see well... but... I saw someone. I think... I cannot be sure.

speaker: Basim
en: I think I know what happened.

speaker: Basim
en: This is a work of intimidation. Someone is trying to prevent your arrival.

speaker: Merchant
en: La! (No!) Who... who would do such a thing? I have no enemies, no bad blood...

speaker: Basim
en: There could be worse fates if you continue down the road. Let me escort your crew to the gates.

speaker: Merchant
en: You would do that for us? Shukran! (Thank you!) God bless you. Quickly, get us away from here!

speaker: Basim
en: Let us move. The city is not too far.

speaker: Basim
en: Hold on. There is something I must do.

speaker: Merchant
en: What? Alright, alright but mind you, we're easy pickings here. Please hurry!

speaker: Basim
en: Sayyidi? (Sir?)

speaker: Merchant
en: You're back! Quickly, we must hurry back to Baghdad. We are not safe here.

speaker: Basim
en: Come, we should leave this place. Quickly.

speaker: Merchant 2
en: Should have stayed home. Hmph.

speaker: Basim
en: Where is home?

speaker: Merchant 2
en: I come from a place called Greece, west from here across the water. With my horse Legume, we carried goods to and from Baghdad. Oh, the cities we visited! Al-Quds, , and even Samarra!

speaker: Basim
en: Your merchant friend tells me that these goods are bound for the Da'irat Al-mal.

speaker: Merchant
en: Nai. (Yes.) The Great Auction is a big event, and that meant bigger demands.

speaker: Basim
en: So you are attending, then?

speaker: Merchant
en: Attending? I only wish I had the coin to spend! No, we are just providing stock for the preparations.

speaker: Soldier
en: Found them! Argh!

speaker: Basim
en: Who sent you?

speaker: Soldier
en: You cannot run or hide! To enter Baghdad you have to pay the price!

speaker: Basim
en: The guards report to someone called Al-Anqa. This confirms my suspicions.

speaker: Merchant
en: Good heavens, could they have been sent to kill us?

speaker: Basim
en: Likely.

speaker: Merchant
en: This is not surprising. We've been vocal against the Caliphate and unfair taxes. It can cost us our heads. But the silent sheep is an ally to corruption.

speaker: Basim
en: They do not like this opposition.

speaker: Merchant
en: I would not be surprised if they made an example out of us to others who might try the same.

speaker: Basim
en: Baghdad. You are safer now.

speaker: Merchant
en: You are wonderful! Thank you!

speaker: Basim
en: Here we are.

speaker: Merchant
en: A thousand thanks, ya sayyidi (sir). Baghdad is not safe. Rumors swirl through the markets of merchants dragged from their stalls. Have you heard of such injustice? Who would do this? Rumors say they target the dhimmiyun (foreigners), traders who are not from here. The Abbasids want a stake in all businesses. As long as there is coin, lives are secondary.

speaker: Basim
en: The note dropped by the guards was from someone called Al-Anqa. This person is the one behind the attack.

speaker: Merchant
en: Hmm. I overheard the guards refer to the Tax Collector as Al-Anqa... which was odd because is the Anqa not female?

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me his name, and where I can find him.

speaker: Merchant
en: Suhail lives in a mansion west of Karkh. Be careful, friend. I doubt he works alone.

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you, friend. Waffaqaka Allah. (May God grant you success.)

speaker: Basim
en: The Tax Collector is due a visit.

speaker: Al-Anqa
en: Where are they? They should be back with the coin! My head will roll if we do not deliver it. How hard is it to shake the coin from those fools, hm? Greece... India... China... hmph. No partiality, not even to their own kind. The Da'irat Al-mal is almost here. If I do not get the coin before then...

speaker: Basim
en: The taxes have been paid.

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim...? It's really you...

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal, I...

speaker: Nehal
en: Say nothing, ya sadeeqi (friend), I am as sorry as you.

speaker: Basim
en: I have so much to tell you.

speaker: Nehal
en: And I you. We will grant each other an audience. But first, I must know something...

speaker: Basim
en: What?

speaker: Nehal
en: Why are you dressed like a peasant?

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps I have less to tell you than I thought.

speaker: Nehal
en: I think I can surmise what our time apart has been like for you.

speaker: Basim
en: And you? You have not been living here, I hope?

speaker: Nehal
en: Less living, more working.

speaker: Basim
en: On what?

speaker: Basim
en: Why do I know this?

speaker: Nehal
en: Because you have seen it. On the object we found at the Winter Palace. I have been trying to remember the specifics of its design.

speaker: Basim
en: You have spent all this time obsessing over this symbol? Why?

speaker: Nehal
en: Because I too have seen it before. I know not where or when. Only that I have. Whatever it is, it calls to me. I intend to unravel its mystery. And so should you.

speaker: Nehal
en: Ah, but of course, duty calls.

speaker: Basim
en: Stop. I will bear in mind if it means you will spend more time outside these musty walls than you do within.

speaker: Basim
en: You really do spare a thought for everyone, don't you, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: Araki Lahiqan.

speaker: Basim
en: The Order of the Ancients are far from defeated. Master Roshan is certain to have a plan brewing to uproot them. ...and perhaps I should look into Nehal's obsession.

speaker: Basim
en: I have seen enough from my three subjects. Time to seek Roshan's counsel, and end this once and for all.

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim. Have you investigated your three subjects? If not, then your work is not complete. You appear decided, Basim. What have you learned?

speaker: Basim
en: Arib is innocent. The Governor, less so. He made a deal with the Order and removed his cousins' protection from Alamut.

speaker: Roshan
en: Tabban (damn it), just as we had feared. We've been bared to our enemies.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes. In exchange for Abu 'Abdallah renouncing his claim to the throne. He cedes his crown to suit the Order, led by

speaker: Roshan
en: His mother, Qabiha, is the head of the snake. Where is she now?

speaker: Basim
en: Fled to the palace. If we act now, we can spare Alamut. Give me the feather, Master!

speaker: Roshan
en: Qabiha will meet swift justice. And I will be the one to deliver it.

speaker: Basim
en: What? What are you saying?

speaker: Roshan
en: That a more seasoned hand is needed. The last time you entered a palace, you left it in disarray. To put it lightly.

speaker: Basim
en: Have I not proven myself since? Master, I have earned the right

speaker: Roshan
en: Earned what? The right to kill?

speaker: Basim
en: No, no, that is not

speaker: Roshan
en: A blow from one of us is a blow for all of us. Or does your ego demand the honor?

speaker: Basim
en: It is not ego, Master. It is duty. I took an oath to leave my life behind, to walk the shadows and to serve the light. I mean to.

speaker: Roshan
en: Qabiha is more dangerous than her underlings. Strike quickly and end this. Do not hesitate.

speaker: Nehal
en: Blood from a stone. Who is she to keep you from Qabiha, or to tell you when to strike?

speaker: Basim
en: My Master and mentor, without whom I would be nothing but a corpse in the streets of Anbar. You spy on me now?

speaker: Nehal
en: Always. So you will swallow your questions, strike at her enemies, serve without complaint... and live your life dogged by a jinni in the hovel you once hoped to escape! You know where to find me when your "duty" is done.

speaker: Alnitak
en: Our brother was careless. He took too many risks. That is what got him killed.

speaker: Alnilam
en: Perhaps, but we have taken a risk ourselves by coming here together. Something about that message makes me suspicious.

speaker: Alnitak
en: Then let us go. You keep an eye on the docks, while I see to the men.

speaker: Basim
en: Twins! Or should I say triplets? Until recently... No matter, both of these wretches must die.

speaker: Basim
en: One more to go.

speaker: Alnitak
en: Listen up, you idiots! Keep your minds and blades sharp or you will end up as dead as my weakling brother.

speaker: Basim
en: It is clear which dog is the bully of the litter.

speaker: Basim
en: The brothers have been reduced to nothing.

speaker: Basim
en: I gather you are in need of assistance?

speaker: Organizer
en: Indeed. As you are likely aware, I am AlUla's organizer of grand diversions.

speaker: Basim
en: Grand diversions?

speaker: Organizer
en: A neighbouring comes to strike a pact of trade, and our merchants wish to honor him. Among the entertainments, there is to be a contest of speed and skill of my devising. But first, I require someone to test the design. Your task is simple—shatter the pots in the allocated time. Any means are acceptable. Even explosives may be used.

speaker: Basim
en: I will meet your challenge.

speaker: Organizer
en: When I give the command, your trial begins at the first step.

speaker: Organizer
en: Now, are you ready?

speaker: Basim
en: Let us begin.

speaker: Organizer
en: Let the trial commence!

speaker: Organizer
en: Let the trial be concluded!

speaker: Basim
en: The task is complete.

speaker: Organizer
en: Your speed was most commendable, yet it is my design that bears the mark of greatness.

speaker: Basim
en: You honor me with your praise.

speaker: Organizer
en: Yes, yes, though the lion's share of that praise goes to me.-->

speaker: Merchant
en: Have you come to fulfil the contract?

speaker: Basim
en: How may I aid you?

speaker: Merchant
en: I am late with my delivery. One final bundle lies at the rear of the house, but it is heavy and I cannot lift it. Venture there and retrieve the goods for me.

speaker: Basim
en: I will do so without delay.

speaker: Merchant
en: The goods are inside a chest. Handle them gently, for their worth is great and they must not suffer damage.

speaker: Basim
en: I will bear them as if they were my own.

speaker: Civilian
en: Help! Help!

speaker: Basim
en: Does any wound trouble you?

speaker: Civilian
en: I suffer no lasting injury, thank God! That merchant who sent you here is no honest trader but a robber in disguise. He lures workers with offers of coin, sedates them with foul fumes, and delivers them to his comrades for ransom.

speaker: Basim
en: I will see this impostor dealt with.

speaker: Basim
en: I must confront this merchant.

speaker: Basim
en: I found your last victim inside the house... He spoke freely.

speaker: Merchant
en: Victim? What victim? I know nothing of such a person.

speaker: Basim
en: Spare me the lies. The only reason you still draw breath is because your hand holds no weapon.

speaker: Fake Merchant
en: What do you intend to do with me?

speaker: Basim
en: You shall learn in the moments to come...

speaker: Tabid
en: Basim! Join me on the roof.

speaker: Tabid
en: Basim! I knew it was you. You are not the only one with eyes that see afar.

speaker: Basim
en: So, Tabid. You have filled the streets with eyes and spies?

speaker: Tabid
en: Such is the life of a Rafiq. Without my knowledge, where would we be?

speaker: Basim
en: Knowledge is a tool, a weapon. It can be used for good or ill, and the Order is using it for ill indeed.

speaker: Tabid
en: What have you learned?

speaker: Basim
en: Rot runs deep through the House of Wisdom. They are using some ancient book, hoping to build a wicked device.

speaker: Tabid
en: I have heard rumors of this blasphemous contraption. They call it their "Great Work."

speaker: Basim
en: The Order is experimenting on people. Lethally. I have stopped them for now, but someone called Al-Rabisu is running things at the House of Wisdom.

speaker: Tabid
en: Any idea about who this Rabisu character could be?

speaker: Basim
en: I have my suspicions about the Great Scholar, Fazil Fahim.

speaker: Tabid
en: That fragile old man?

speaker: Basim
en: The clues I have gathered tell me so.

speaker: Tabid
en: Hmm, it could be. The House of Wisdom will be hosting a Great Symposium soon. An informal gathering of scholars. A lecture, refreshments, chatter. Even the great Arib will attend! Go, spy out this Fazil with care. But do not draw your blade at the Symposium. We don't want to show our hand just yet. But if Fazil is guilty and alone, then like a viper, strike! But you must be sure.

speaker: Basim
en: Before I act, I will be sure.

speaker: Basim
en: This estate could hold a hundred horses and camels. I never knew dealing with thieves could be so lucrative.

speaker: Civilian
en: Allahumma ighfir lahu warhamh wa'fu anh... (Oh God, absolve him of his sins and grant him mercy and forgiveness...)

speaker: Basim
en: You are a good daughter.

speaker: Murjana
en: I was not the child he expected. I wanted to see the world, heed the call of the chase. Steel meeting steel, hearts into battle... For him, someone who enjoyed the simple, diplomatic life would be a better fit. Despite that, he loved me all the same. The only time we disagreed was due to his dealings with the Forty Thieves.

speaker: Basim
en: It can be difficult to resist the lure of coin, especially when you are accustomed to a certain way of life.

speaker: Murjana
en: I thought that as well, but that was not the only reason. Look... I found drawing and notes among his belongings. They speak of a wondrous cave, full of coin and jewels. He wrote about fulfilling my desire to see the world. Somehow, the Forty Thieves were the key to this cave. There was still so much I did not know about my father. I could have helped him... or figured out a plan...

speaker: Basim
en: Sometimes we keep secrets, especially from the ones we love most.

speaker: Murjana
en: The Mark of the Thieves! They still live.

speaker: Basim
en: This means you have been targeted. Now they know where you are, and more will come until you lie still.

speaker: Murjana
en: Is taking my father's life not enough?

speaker: Basim
en: We shook them up. If we mark the other houses, I can intercept the thieves before more lives are lost.

speaker: Murjana
en: I cannot let them touch my father's body...

speaker: Basim
en: I will go.

speaker: Basim
en: Would not want to endanger innocents... Marking a few empty houses will throw them off.

speaker: Basim
en: One here.

speaker: Basim
en: Two.

speaker: Basim
en: One more mark. I should hurry. The thieves could appear at any moment.

speaker: Basim
en: Last one. This should confuse them. Now to wait somewhere above.

speaker: Basim
en: The thieves should be here soon.

speaker: Thief
en: What... what is this? I swear I marked only one house! Why are there more than one? Was it this one? Or that one? They all look the same!

speaker: Thief
en: Spread out! Find the right house, quickly!

speaker: Basim
en: I hope Murjana is safe.

speaker: Thief
en: This does not have to be difficult!

speaker: Murjana
en: Difficult for who?

speaker: Thief
en: Drop your sword!

speaker: Murjana
en: Try and make me!

speaker: Murjana
en: Back not a moment too soon.

speaker: Murjana
en: Thank you. They danced well and took the wind out of me. Ugh...

speaker: Basim
en: Your injuries are grave.

speaker: Murjana
en: We have bigger concerns.

speaker: Murjana
en: I overheard them before they found me. The King of Thieves was the one who ordered my father's execution, and now mine.

speaker: Basim
en: What does he want with you?

speaker: Murjana
en: He knows I have knowledge about this cave of theirs. After killing my father, I am just a loose end. He also knows he will not have a moment's peace with me alive. Neither will I, as long as he lives. My father's blood is on my neck.

speaker: Basim
en: Then we must hunt him first.

speaker: Murjana
en: No, I will not ask you for more. I have yet to pay you for your services...

speaker: Basim
en: I am not fond of leaving a task unfinished. We can talk payment after this is over.

speaker: Murjana
en: I will go with you.

speaker: Basim
en: No, let me go on ahead. Lay your father to rest, then look for me.

speaker: Murjana
en: Wait. I found this amongst my father's things...

speaker: Basim
en: "Iftah ya simsim..." ("Open Sesame...")

speaker: Murjana
en: A watchword. It could be a key to what my father wanted to find... their real hideout, the cave. Thank you, Hidden One. I will meet you there...

speaker: Basim
en: Time to end your reign, King of Thieves. I will find you.

speaker: Murjana
en: Go, Hidden One. I will find you once I regain strength.

speaker: Hind
en: Greetings, Basim. It is always a pleasure to see you.

speaker: Basim
en: Greetings—I have found something that will please you. Distribute this as you see fit.

speaker: Hind
en: Truly, you are a champion of AlUla.-->

speaker: Novice 1
en: As-salamu 'alaikum (Peace be upon you), Basim!.

speaker: Basim
en: I must see Al-Hasan. He awaits me.

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum (Peace be upon you), Rebekah!

speaker: Rebekah
en: Wa 'alaikum as-salam (And peace be upon you), Basim. What a slow and boring day...

speaker: Basim
en: Did you not know that I have been called to be initiated?

speaker: Rebekah
en: Oh? We are really initiating anyone now!

speaker: Basim
en: Where's this all coming from?

speaker: Rebekah
en: Oh, calm down! I am well aware this is the great day of Basim. Waffaqaka Allah! (May God grant you success!)

speaker: Basim
en: Al-Hasan!

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: Wrong again. It's Abu Jafar.

speaker: Basim
en: I apologize. What are you reading?

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: The works of a poet named Arib Al-Ma'muniyya. Tabid was kind enough to lend it to me. I would recommend her highly. Now, if I may continue.

speaker: Basim
en: Of course. I will leave you to it.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: Basim, go see my brother Al-Hasan. You remember who he is, yes?

speaker: Basim
en: It is strange, Al-Hasan. My head is calmer than I believe it would be. I thought I would be a stormy sea inside, but I am calm and quiet.

speaker: Al-Hasan
en: Because you have dedicated yourself to your training and left nothing to chance.

speaker: Al-Hasan
en: Here, Basim. You have earned this.

speaker: Al-Hasan
en: It is a great honor. I suspect you understand that.

speaker: Basim
en: Roshan and the others are waiting for me. Wada'an (Farewell)... and thank you, Al-Hasan.

speaker: Novice 2
en: I wish I could just look into the cave for a moment... to see what is there.

speaker: Novice 3
en: There is one thing I do know about today's ceremony. Basim will leave the cave a little lighter than he went in!

speaker: Novice 2
en: Oh, do not be wicked! This is a big day for him.

speaker: Basim
en: Good day, Tabid! What are you busying yourself with?

speaker: Tabid
en: Have you heard about Iltani? One of the first of our founders. She assassinated Alexander the Great with an ingenious poison. I have attempted to recreate it from historical records... Iltani has taught me that no enemy is untouchable... no matter how powerful they appear!

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you for this lesson.

speaker: Tabid
en: Waffaqaka Allah! (May God grant you success!)

speaker: Novice 4
en: I would be honored to be called to initiation.

speaker: Novice 5
en: I must work harder to become worthy of it. I feel I am making no progress at all!

speaker: Novice 4
en: The road to initiation is long and very hard. We must take it a day at a time.

speaker: Novice 5
en: Ah, patience again! A more difficult art than sword combat!

speaker: Basim
en: As-salamu 'alaikum! (Peace be upon you!)

speaker: Novice 6
en: Wa 'alaikum as-salam (And peace be upon you), Basim! I did not see you there. How was it?

speaker: Basim
en: If I may? If you swing through your target, it my give you more power to strike.

speaker: Novice 6
en: Thank you.

speaker: Fuladh
en: How are you feeling?

speaker: Basim
en: Ready to make the leap!

speaker: Fuladh
en: I wish you to know it has been an honor to watch you walk your path as a Novice... and as a man.

speaker: Basim
en: I am grateful to you for leading the way before me.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I am honored. Come. Your new robes await.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Ah, they suit you well. Come, it is time.

speaker: Basim
en: How did you feel on that day so long ago?

speaker: Fuladh
en: I felt afraid! My palms were slick with sweat and my knees were shaking.

speaker: Basim
en: I can not imagine you being afraid.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Allow me to share a secret with you on this important day... To have courage means to act in the midst of feeling great fear.

speaker: Roshan
en: Basim ibn Is'haq. Are you ready to leave your life behind and walk the path of shadows?

speaker: Basim
en: I am.

speaker: Roshan
en: Are you ready to give up who you once thought you were, ready to sacrifice everything you held close?

speaker: Basim
en: I am.

speaker: Roshan
en: Never forget the tenets you have sworn to uphold. Stay your blade from the flesh of an innocent. Hide in plain sight. Never compromise the Brotherhood. Then out of the dark, you will come into the light.

speaker: Roshan
en: And from the light, you will return to the dark.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Basim ibn Is'haq, you now follow in the eagle's path.

speaker: Roshan
en: Welcome, Hidden One. You have died and been reborn. Now, fight me... as your equal.

speaker: Roshan
en: Aha! Well done!

speaker: Basim
en: Take that! You have trained me well, Roshan.

speaker: Roshan
en: Which one will I strike with next... my dagger or my sword?

speaker: Basim
en: How is that for focus?

speaker: Novice
en: When the student finally faces the master as their equal! I love when this happens!

speaker: Nur
en: Sa'iduni! (Help me!)

speaker: Basim
en: Nur!

speaker: Basim
en: Nur! Do not strain... Save your strength.

speaker: Roshan
en: He traveled unprepared. Left Baghdad in a hurry.

speaker: Basim
en: Here. Drink.

speaker: Nur
en: Ali... he is gone... they took him in the night.

speaker: Basim
en: They?

speaker: Roshan
en: The Order.

speaker: Roshan
en: Bring him to my tent.

speaker: Rayhan
en: If Ali is gone, we are blind. The Order has put a fog over Baghdad and their movements.

speaker: Fuladh
en: We must go to Baghdad.

speaker: Rayhan
en: Roshan, Basim, go with Fuladh. Leave at once.

speaker: Basim
en: I will need to clear the way to get the boat out.

speaker: Basim
en: Now to get onto the canal.

speaker: Basim
en: Should be smooth sailing from here.

speaker: Basim
en: I am in the clear. I will dock near the drop-off. Done to perfection.

speaker: Basim
en: Dervis' men will recognize the boat. My part is done.

speaker: Basim
en: A list of what is inside these jars would make my search easier.

speaker: Basim
en: This sample should suffice.

speaker: Soldier
en: I am glad we are just guarding these jars and not handling them. Did you hear what happened to Hakeem?

speaker: Basim
en: I have all the samples I need. Now to drop them off.

speaker: Basim
en: Who would think to look for these samples in a planter? Only those in the know. Done to perfection.

speaker: Soldier
en: Can you believe all this? I thought officers were supposed to be more disciplined.

speaker: Soldier
en: It's the opposite from what I have seen. Corruption rises up the rank...

speaker: Soldier
en: Good to see you! Help yourselves to refreshments! I insist!

speaker: Soldier
en: Make sure the guests have plenty to drink.

speaker: Basim
en: The key is plucked, now on to my prize. I really should attend more parties.

speaker: Basim
en: A nice piece of work, but I have no time for idle admiration.

speaker: Basim
en: Done to perfection.

speaker: Basim
en: Here is the drop-off. I trust the right person finds it.

speaker: Basim
en: It seems Nehal is trying to discover the location of a secret chamber.

speaker: Basim
en: A Tha'abeen member is near. That person looks suspicious. I should investigate. There, one of the Tha'abeen members. I should investigate.

speaker: Basim
en: A small strange shard... yet it weights heavily in my hand. What is it, I wonder? Another shard. This shard brings me one step closer to uncovering the mysteries of the chamber.

speaker: Basim
en: I should find a use for all these shards.

speaker: Basim
en: This must be the oasis Nehal had in mind.

speaker: Basim
en: I wonder where this leads?

speaker: Basim
en: What magic is this? Surely there is a way to diminish it?

speaker: Basim
en: What is this? A note?

speaker: Basim
en: It seems the members of the Tha'abeen have already unearthed the shards. I should keep an eye out for them.

speaker: Basim
en: Excellent, the shards work. Perhaps I can use some more?

speaker: Basim
en: I have seen floor stones like this. They move under great weight.

speaker: Basim
en: There are no more heavy jars nearby. I should look elsewhere.

speaker: Basim
en: Vow of povery my eye! This could blind one with greed!

speaker: Basim
en: The Carolingian! I see why Dervis would covet this coin!

speaker: Basim
en: I am tempted to keep this coin, but I could never cross Dervis.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Wait, Ali. Let us hear from Basim, first. Were you successful in your tasks?

speaker: Basim
en: General Jasoor and Admiral Nadir are dead.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Did you find anything to identify Al-Mardikhwar?

speaker: Basim
en: Not exactly. General Jasoor was commanded to meet Al-Mardikhwar at the Great Garrison. It seems his past finally caught up to him. Admiral Nadir was questioned about missing supply shipments meant for the Turkic military. Al-Mardikhwar was not happy.

speaker: Fuladh
en: So ... Al-Mardikhwar is at the Great Garrison, overseeing supplies for the Turkic mercenaries. There is only one officer of sufficient rank who fits. Warlord Wasif al Turki.

speaker: Ali
en: Wasif! This makes sense. There are few others who could have taken Beshi.

speaker: Basim
en: Beshi has been taken?

speaker: Ali
en: He never came back.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Wasif just returned from an excursion for the Caliph, and is at the Garrison. If he has Beshi, that is where he will be.

speaker: Ali
en: Then that is where I am going.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Wasif controls half of Baghdad. If we challenge him and fail, it could start a war that reaches even Alamut. You need Basim.

speaker: Ali
en: Fine. I will meet Basim near the Garrison before I move. But do not take long. I am finished waiting.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Enter the Great Garrison and kill Wasif. He must not escape, and it must look like Ali did it. The safety of Alamut depends on it.

speaker: Basim
en: It will be done.

speaker: Basim
en: Act as usual.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: That guard who likes me said she and Ali's followers are trying to overthrow the Prince.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: What madness! They will surely fail.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: I heard His Favorite was a spy.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: And that could be why he had her locked up.

speaker: Guard Captain
en: You rebels need to learn your place!

speaker: Civilian 5
en: Help!

speaker: Soldier
en: Tell me what I wish to know, and no more need die this day.

speaker: Basim
en: Argh... come on!

speaker: Basim
en: Yasmeen?

speaker: Dancer
en: Softly now, or the guards will hear you. Yasmeen might be in the reception room on the second floor.

speaker: Basim
en: Yasmeen?

speaker: Dancer
en: Yasmeen? I'm not certain. You could try the next room.

speaker: Basim
en: Yasmeen?

speaker: Yasmeen
en: At last! My prayers are answered! You look like you could help me to safety. Now, follow me.

speaker: Yasmeen
en: They are coming. You deal with the guards while I unlock the door down this corridor.

speaker: Basim
en: It is safe now.

speaker: Yasmeen
en: They are searching the garden. Take care of them.

speaker: Basim
en: The danger has passed.

speaker: Yasmeen
en: We're almost free!

speaker: Basim
en: The course is clear.

speaker: Yasmeen
en: I cannot believe I am free! Is there some way I can repay you?

speaker: Basim
en: Your safety is payment enough.

speaker: Basim
en: There you are. Now lead on.

speaker: Basim
en: So this is where the messages are sent. I must be discrete when it comes to making the swap.

speaker: Basim
en: I have swapped the messages and my task is complete.

speaker: Basim
en: A fine finish.

speaker: Basim
en: What beautiful homes ... far different from the slums of Anbar.

speaker: Basim
en: The home of the poetess.

speaker: Basim
en: Adoring fans? They are very well-armed if so.

speaker: Basim
en: Let us hope she is home.

speaker: Arib
en: You will not bar mme from my guests! This is my house!

speaker: Patron
en: Bought with my generosity!

speaker: Arib
en: Bought by my genius!

speaker: Patron
en: For tokens, favors, and personal dedications, you may find Sayyida Arib in the garden after her recital. Good day.

speaker: Basim
en: You must be her patron! It is an honor, sayyidi. If I may, I seek a private audience with the poetess.

speaker: Patron
en: Do you.

speaker: Basim
en: I have been moved beyond words by her ... words. "Symmetry of Sky and Sea..." I only wish to express my sincere admiration.

speaker: Patron
en: Pretty words. Nearly as pretty as hers. And just as false. We both know what mask she wears, don't we?

speaker: Basim
en: Mask, sayyidi?'

speaker: Patron
en: Enough, "sayyidi". I know what you are, and I know why you've come. You think I haven't seen you skulking in the shadows? She is no longer party to your plots. Your secret meetings, your foolish nicknames. I have scrubbed her clean of them. For I have set a watch on her door. My men dog her recitals. Every letter she's had of you, I have shredded or sent back!

speaker: Basim
en: Sent back?

speaker: Patron
en: Youll find them piled at the Postal Bureau. Burn them, bury them, do what you will. You can choke on them for all I care.

speaker: Basim
en: Foolish nicknames, secret meetings ... the patron may have thought me a member of the Order of the Ancients. The piles of letters at the Postal Bureau may reveal more... Let us see what mask you wear, Poetess.

speaker: Basim
en: The Postal Bureau. I will do as the 'Uyun (spies) do, sift through strangers' mail and sniff out conspiracies.

speaker: Basim
en: There must be mail here from every corner of the Caliphate... Now to find Arib's.

speaker: Basim
en: "Please note that your payment of fifteen dinars is overdue and must be..." No.

speaker: Basim
en: "Abu 'Abdallah is the true Caliph and will soon reclaim his stolen throne..." I will leave this one for the 'Uyun.

speaker: Basim
en: "Dearest Arib, your poetry has touched me deeply. You are my oasis, lush and..." Ya lalqaraf. (Yuck.)

speaker: Basim
en: "Silence your song of sin or I will do it for you." How kind. Moving on...

speaker: Basim
en: "After the honey drips from her lips, Al-Tha'lab (The Fox) leaves the garden and follows the mouse." Secret Order correspondence? Bad poetry? A bit of both? Arib could be Al-Tha'lab. The patron spoke of a recital in the gardens... I could give this letter to Arib and see where the vixen leads me.

speaker: Basim
en: I will go to the garden, give Al Tha'lab her letter, and follow where she goes.

speaker: Arib
en: "Rage as the ocean, I'll sweeten your storms. Scorch as the desert, I'll bathe in your heat. Strike as the cobra..."

speaker: Arib
en: "Be you ocean, desert, cobra, dove, all shapes and humors will I embrace."

speaker: Arib
en: Hello there .. have we met? Come, don't be shy! I rarely bite and I never leave a mark.

speaker: Arib
en: It seems there's no privacy in the public eye.

speaker: Arib
en: How came you by that letter? Who put you up to this?

speaker: Basim
en: I work in the dark to serve the light.

speaker: Arib
en: I've met the men who "serve the light". It seems its glare oft leaves them blind. Are your masters so blinkered and bumbling?

speaker: Patron
en: You were warned, you son of a dog! Come, Arib! We wll set no tongues to wagging here.

speaker: Arib
en: Yours is the tongue that will not still itself, even when I beg for silence.

speaker: Patron
en: You spurn the counsel of he who raised you and without whom you would still be nothing!

speaker: Arib
en: I raised myself. I authored myself. I have written myself into history. You are banished from my pages, now be gone!

speaker: Patron
en: How could I leave you to wolves such as these? You're a woman alone, unharmed...

speaker: Arib
en: Words are weapons enough for me.

speaker: Patron
en: Than let us see what defense they offer. Take her.

speaker: Basim
en: There is somewhere the sayyida needs to be. And you are delaying her.

speaker: Arib
en: It seems that words can summon shields.

speaker: Basim
en: We will need to make this quick.

speaker: Basim
en: Arib has left for her secret meeting. I must hurry.

speaker: Basim
en: The letter commanded Al-Tha'lab to leave the garden and follow the mouse. Perharps Arib is not lost to me yet.

speaker: Basim
en: How far will the fox flee?

speaker: Basim
en: Yet another painted mouse.

speaker: Basim
en: Another crumb to follow. I am growing tired of this chase.

speaker: Arib
en: "Follow the mouse." Really?

speaker: Sara
en: You should bring him before the Mazalim Court!

speaker: Arib
en: But he thinks only of my reputation, Sara! To safeguard success I must be palatable. Discreet. He fears I am too proud.

speaker: Sara
en: You? Never.

speaker: Arib
en: I write that love is feral and free, unbound by stricture or statute. Should I not practice what I publish?

speaker: Sara
en: Practice makes perfect. It also makes enemies.

speaker: Arib
en: So be it, but let me choose them. Courtiers, Caliphs, patrons, partners, so many men have tried to decide my enemies ... and friends. Though Allah knows I once chose poorly.

speaker: Sara
en: He hid himself well. And a poet needs patrons, even one so great as Al-Tha'lab.

speaker: Arib
en: Well, I have my pick.

speaker: Sara
en: Good. There's troubled times ahead.

speaker: Arib
en: I will be fine. I have survived six Caliphs. I will survive

speaker: Sara
en: Six more.

speaker: Arib
en: Don't worry, Sara. I'll kiss the rings I need to kiss but I will not be bound again. Not by anyone.

speaker: Basim
en: Secret meanings, coded names... There is no trace of the Order here. Still, she has her pick of patrons... Maybe the Head of the Order is not Arib herself, but an admirer.

speaker: Basim
en: The symposium should be here. Baghdad's brightest, sharing their wisdom.

speaker: Scholar
en: I am excited about Fazil's lecture! He will share the wisdom of the universe.

speaker: Scholar
en: Nonsense. We have already learned everything there is to know. Nothing more will be discovered.

speaker: Basim
en: Pardon me, I am looking for the Great Scholar's lecture.

speaker: Kahraman
en: Fazil Fahim's lecture about the antediluvian antecedents of humanity will begin soon. In the meantime, please enjoy our ample stock of exquisite delicacies and tasty refreshments.

speaker: Nehal
en: Hey, Nine-Fingers! Over here! I told you I'd see you around.

speaker: Basim
en: Indeed. And what brings you back?

speaker: Nehal
en: I want to show you something.

speaker: Nehal
en: These House of Wisdom bores collect the wildest trinkets and gadgets.

speaker: Basim
en: I have been here before, Nehal. This is Ahmad ibn Musa's office. Have you been sneaking in there?

speaker: Nehal
en: Ahmad and his brothers are capable of designing some fantastic devices.

speaker: Basim
en: Not all of his ideas are that practical, I'm afraid.

speaker: Nehal
en: Don't be so smug, the world is full of wonders.

speaker: Nehal
en: Does this remind you of your nightmares?

speaker: Basim
en: No. More like something from the Bimaristan. Or a training chart of the Hidden Ones.

speaker: Nehal
en: Ah, yes. The swift ways to kill silently. Death in seconds.

speaker: Nehal
en: It gives me a tingle down my spine. Like I'm nearing a cosmic secret.

speaker: Basim
en: You read too much about magicians and lost cities buried beneath the dunes.

speaker: Nehal
en: You don't read enough. Perhaps there are other worlds, other people, out among the stars.

speaker: Basim
en: Nonsense.

speaker: Basim
en: This. I have seen this before. Is this what you wanted to show me?

speaker: Nehal
en: Yes. It reminded me of that object we found at the palace. What is it?

speaker: Basim
en: A drawing from an ancient book.

speaker: Nehal
en: There is something you are not telling me.

speaker: Basim
en: You do not want to know what happens behind closed doors.

speaker: Nehal
en: Why? Because you do not know either?

speaker: Basim
en: Because, as Dervis says, sometimes it is better not to know the truth behind the things we must do.

speaker: Nehal
en: The truth, Basim, is that everything is here, in front of you, but you refuse to look at it. This is about you. It has always been about you, ever since that night...

speaker: Basim
en: I took an oath, Nehal. To leave my old life behind and walk this path of shadows.

speaker: Nehal
en: And maybe some day you will find the light. But until then I will walk behind you, every step of the way, to remind you not to forget who you are.

speaker: Basim
en: Is that a threat?

speaker: Nehal
en: I do not know.

speaker: Basim
en: The Translator! What is he still doing here?

speaker: Basim
en: Hunayn. You should not be back so soon.

speaker: Hunayn
en: I know, I'm still nervous, but... I couldn't stay away from my books.

speaker: Basim
en: I guess we must always do our duty.

speaker: Hunayn
en: Wada'an. (Farewell).

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Where is Arib Al-Ma'muniyya, the poet? Where is Arib? I hoped to catch a whiff of her magnificent aura. So rare to see her outside of the Round City.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: The beloved is in the garden, ruminating upon the perfection of nature.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Oh, to be a flower held in her discerning hands, inspiring such languid verse.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: She must be relieved to be free of her wealthy patrons for a change.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: Oh! Perhaps she leads an exciting, secret double life, slipping out of the palaces to find inspiration in common life.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: I doubt it.

speaker: Basim
en: There is that poet Tabid loves, whose work keeps turning up in unexpected places.

speaker: Arib
en: Spirit of the sands, pilot of desert ships, from distant lands, bring to our ears... From your wind-touched lips, the mirage's song, the kiss that grips.

speaker: Arib
en: Yes?

speaker: Basim
en: Symmetry of sky and sea, but only in thine eye do these two planes meet.

speaker: Arib
en: You have read my work. And who might you be?

speaker: Basim
en: A lover of poetry, nothing more. And of order... or should I say chaos?

speaker: Arib
en: I know only one living poet who loves chaos that much, Ali ibn Muhammad. Are you a fan of his pedestrian work?

speaker: Basim
en: The rivalry between you two is legendary, it enhances the craft. I cannot choose.

speaker: Arib
en: You are most diplomatic, but I would rather seek inspiration among these lovely blooms. Good day.

speaker: Basim
en: That astronomer might be one of them, though I doubt it.

speaker: Basim
en: Sayyidi (Sir), I am honored to make your acquaintance.

speaker: Al-Farghani
en: Good to see more young people enjoying the House of Wisdom.

speaker: Basim
en: Do you think the Great Scholar will give a good lecture?

speaker: Al-Farghani
en: Do not waste time listening to his nonsense. I have written many more edifying and practical books instead.

speaker: Basim
en: On which topics?

speaker: Al-Farghani
en: I have written extensively about sun-dials, astrolabes, stars and planets, and the circumference of the Earth.

speaker: Basim
en: Fascinating, sayyidi (sir). I shall read more of your work soon. Wada'an. (Farewell.)

speaker: Basim
en: Impressive door. Where does it go?

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Those Who Came Before are...?

speaker: Basim
en: What?

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: I said, Those Who Came before are...?

speaker: Basim
en: Never mind.

speaker: Kahraman
en: Attention, Symposium attendees! The Great Scholar's lecture will begin after a short delay. Meanwhile, enjoy our bounteous snacks and the sparkling wit of your fellow guests.

speaker: Basim
en: Sounds like the lecture is about to begin. I should return to the Kahraman (chief servant).

speaker: Basim
en: Pardon me, is Fazil Fahim's lecture ready to begin?

speaker: Kahraman
en: Indeed it is. Head inside, if you please.

speaker: Fazil
en: Welcome, one and all, to the House of Wisdom, center of learning in Baghdad. Indeed, of the entire world. I am Fazil Fahim al-Kemsa, first scholar of the House of Wisdom, wisest of the wise. Today I will shock you with what may sound like outrageous blasphemies.

speaker: Fazil
en: Do not fear, good people. Though I am old, my mind remains sharp as steel. Today I speak of mysteries, of creatures from the antediluvian age. Do not the ancient prophets tell us about giants from before the flood, who forsook Allah and worshiped false idols?

speaker: Fazil
en: Is it not possible that these giants built marvels, works of wondrous power now lost to us?

speaker: Kahraman
en: Zahra and Hassan are both dead, slain by an assassin's blade.

speaker: Fazil
en: They're dead?

speaker: Kahraman
en: Sayyidi (Sir), I urge you to hide until it's safe.

speaker: Kahraman
en: Apologies people, but our lecture has concluded. Please, feel free to explore the House of Wisdom's many fine chambers.

speaker: Basim
en: You call yourself "the Great Scholar", Fazil. You who burn books and hope the smoke will hide your crimes. How many did you sacrifice in your search for knowledge? How many did you use, damage, and discard in the name of discovery? Now you hide within the House of Wisdom, the house you led astray. But I will find you, and I will exact justice for every soul you savaged for your "Great Work".

speaker: Basim
en: It is true! Fazil leads the Order in Abbasiyah. I need to hunt him down.

speaker: Al-Farghani
en: The old fraud Fazil went into hiding.

speaker: Arib
en: How exciting! What do you think frightened the Great Scholar?

speaker: Al-Farghani
en: The old fool must have imagined one of his antediluvian creatures. He's an absolute disgrace.

speaker: Arib
en: But where did he run off to?

speaker: Hunayn
en: There's rumors of hidden passages beneath the House of Wisdom. Maybe he hid down there.

speaker: Al-Farghani
en: I have heard the rooftop gardener mention these places, yes.

speaker: Arib
en: What a colorful detail to include in my verse! "The scholar by secret tunnels fled, chased by delusions of deities who want him dead!"

speaker: Scholar
en: Where is the Kahraman? I wish to complain about the shortness of the lecture. I remain profoundly unedified!

speaker: Scribe
en: Did you see the powerful terror on the Great Scholar's face?

speaker: Architect
en: He looked like somebody about to get his skull drilled.

speaker: Scribe
en: How revolting!

speaker: Architect
en: Forget I mentioned it.

speaker: Gardener
en: Keep to the roof, I say. Plenty of work to do up here. Safer, too. Avoid dark hallways, especially after the murder in the library. What's this place coming to? And those screams from the basement! Makes my stomach crawl to hear such pain.

speaker: Basim
en: This key could be useful.

speaker: Basim
en: Pardon me, but I heard a rumor about a hidden basement beneath the House of Wisdom.

speaker: Kahraman
en: A secret basement? You must be joking.

speaker: Basim
en: No, not at all. Surely, such a large building must have basements and cellars to store books and inks.

speaker: Kahraman
en: I am aware of no such locations on these premises.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps a little token of my appreciation will jog your memory.

speaker: Kahraman
en: Most generous. Murders, mayhem, and bonfires. It's time for me to depart the House of Wisdom. Father has a fine carpet shop in Samarra. He always wanted me to take up the family trade.

speaker: Basim
en: A wise choice. Now, about any hidden cellars?

speaker: Kahraman
en: Oh yes, of course. Forgive me. Now that you mention it, there is a basement hatch in the northwest courtyard.

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you.

speaker: Basim
en: Never mind. I will look around on my own.

speaker: Kahraman
en: As you wish.

speaker: Kahraman
en: Yes?

speaker: Basim
en: I was asking about underground places in the House of Wisdom.

speaker: Kahraman
en: What about them?

speaker: Basim
en: Gatekeeper, let me pass.

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Those Who Came Before are...?

speaker: Basim
en: What are you talking about?

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Those Who Came Before are...?

speaker: Basim
en: Let me get back to you.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: I've lost Fazil's greatest work.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: What do you mean you lost the Great Scholar's masterwork?

speaker: Civilian 1
en: I'm sorry! I was distracted by the presence of the famous poet, Arib.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Forget the poet! We better find Fazil's book or we're both dead.

speaker: Basim
en: Sounds like part of a passphrase.

speaker: Basim
en: That book looks out of place, wedged behind a desk like that. A History of the Great Scholar and His Magnificent Reforms of the House of Wisdom by Fazil Fahim. Not sure if this is the correct volume.

speaker: Basim
en: Looks like somebody left a book in the stairwell.

speaker: Basim
en: The Folly of Poetry by Fazil Fahim. Does not sound too romantic, to be honest.

speaker: Basim
en: This letter mentions a private reading balcony. Might be where the reader has taken the book.

speaker: Basim
en: An impressive volume, written by Fazil Fahim. Could be his masterwork. Its title is "Those Who Came Before are Those Who Shall Return." That has to be it.

speaker: Basim
en: Gatekeeper!

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Those Who Came Before are...?

speaker: Basim
en: ...Are Those Who Shall Return.

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Correct! You may proceed.

speaker: Basim
en: The Great Scholar in the House of Wisdom.

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: No. We are done.

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: Again, I ask. Those Who Came Before are...?

speaker: Basim
en: The Folly of Poetry.

speaker: Gatekeeper
en: No. Wrong answer. Goodbye.

speaker: Basim
en: I will return with the pass phrase.

speaker: Basim
en: The scholar's notes... He believes in these ancient beings, the masters of memory.

speaker: Basim
en: No question about it. Fazil was neck-deep in the Order.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Nobody's putting me in that thing. Not ever.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Don't worry, we've got plenty of volunteers.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: You can pull out my teeth with hot irons before you get me in there.

speaker: Basim
en: There is a deep wrongness here, a reek of rot and iron.

speaker: Basim
en: Those robes might help me get closer to Fazil.

speaker: Basim
en: What have they done to these people?

speaker: Basim
en: Poor guy will not need this anymore.

speaker: Basim
en: This should help me blend in.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Please... take me back there, I don't belong here.

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Where is my robe? I can't meet the scholar without my special robe!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: This world doesn't look right. Someone, take me back to the bright, shiny place.

speaker: Guard
en: Next subject, in here now!

speaker: Basim
en: There are horrors here. But the most terrifying thing is that I have seen it all before. Somehow.

speaker: Fazil
en: Who dares meddle with my Great Work? Killing my allies and spoiling my lecture, it's an outrage.

speaker: The Fist of Wisdom
en: It looks like the handiwork of a trained assassin.

speaker: Fazil
en: Must be some faction in the Round City. Or one of those jealous brutes in Sharqiyah.

speaker: The Fist of Wisdom
en: These killings were too subtle for mercenaries.

speaker: Fazil
en: No matter! Once I understand how the mechanism works, I will prove myself to Al-Bahamut.

speaker: The Fist of Wisdom
en: In here, lackwit.

speaker: Fazil
en: You are new, aren't you? I don't recognize you. They promised you gold when you volunteered, yes? No matter, what you are about to behold surpasses all worldly riches. Don't be afraid. Are you afraid?

speaker: Fazil
en: This is my Great Work. I call it Alruh. It will take you on a journey to another realm. Why did the First Ones leave this world behind filled with fools, I wonder? And make so few of me? We call this the House of Wisdom, but its foundations are unsound. For beneath the House of Wisdom lies the Dungeon of Ignorance. And upon such dark secrets we build our philosophies. Science is the noblest purpose. Knowledge is the greatest power.

speaker: Basim
en: No.

speaker: Fazil
en: No? Then what?

speaker: Fazil
en: Argh...

speaker: Basim
en: Justice.

speaker: Fazil
en: This may be the place. It may be here where lies absolute knowledge. It... it is not how I remember it. Behind the doors. It looked... brighter.

speaker: Basim
en: But in the end, all we see is darkness.

speaker: Basim
en: I need to get out of here, get back to Tabid.

speaker: Nehal
en: Easy, Basim. I am here.

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim, tamahhal (slow down).

speaker: Basim
en: I cannot keep them waiting.

speaker: Nehal
en: Are they aware, your companions, that their hunter is hunted in his sleep?

speaker: Basim
en: If it were in my sleep alone I could bear it. But it followed when I fled Anbar. Now it stalks me when I slay those I hunt.

speaker: Nehal
en: The ones from the palace... in the masks.

speaker: Basim
en: Four are dead at my hand. The last, the Head of the Snake, will join them soon.

speaker: Nehal
en: Why slit its throat when you could loosen its tongue?

speaker: Basim
en: What? Why would I...

speaker: Nehal
en: The jinni only struck in sleep. It never dogged you by the day until you reached into that chest. The masked ones prized what lay within, the ancient object that woke at your touch. They may hold more answers living than dead!

speaker: Basim
en: I hunt my enemies, I do not break bread with them. I took an Oath, Nehal.

speaker: Nehal
en: How can you hunt when you are hounded? If you could walk the dark unburdened, you could better serve the light.

speaker: Basim
en: I stay my blade from the flesh of the innocent. Not from the Order of the Ancients!

speaker: Nehal
en: If you will not ask your foes, then at least ask your friends what slept in that chest... and why they sought it.

speaker: Basim
en: My companions wait for me at the Harbiyah Bureau. Clear your mind, Basim. Focus on the task before you.

speaker: Roshan
en: You took your time.

speaker: Basim
en: Did you wait up, Master?

speaker: Roshan
en: I wait for no man. You look tired.

speaker: Basim
en: Nothing a little adventure won't fix. What news?

speaker: Roshan
en: Ali thinks the time is right to attack the palace. The Uyun (spies) are distracted and the people divided.

speaker: Basim
en: Divided how?

speaker: Roshan
en: Some are claiming the new Caliph stole the throne from Abu 'Abdallah, son of Al-Mutawakkil. What do you know of him?

speaker: Basim
en: Little. He was there at the palace, the night his father... The night I reached into that chest. Master, have we learned anything more about the object within?

speaker: Roshan
en: Why do you ask?

speaker: Basim
en: It seems a shame we know so little about something the Order prized so much. Should we not seek to know our enemies better, the better to defeat them?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Marhaban (Welcome), Basim! Have I interrupted?

speaker: Roshan
en: No. We must turn to the task at hand.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Of course, Abu 'Abdallah. Rebekah tells me you have met his mother, Qabiha?

speaker: Basim
en: I did. I think she could be first among our foes. She, or Arib the Poet, or Muhammad the Governor. All three had ties to our enemies.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Muhammad ibn Tahir... His cousins govern the land on which Alamut sits.

speaker: Roshan
en: Their protection is all that shields us from our enemies.

speaker: Basim
en: I cut our enemy's legs beneath them, Master. Let me strike while their stumps are bloody. I will unmask them and learn their intent.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Basim is right. We must act swiftly.

speaker: Roshan
en: Go to the Round City. Investigate all three, but take no further action. Report back to me atop the House of the Privy Seal.

speaker: Basim
en: Fuladh, my finder of facts, my fielder of questions.

speaker: Fuladh
en: How can I be of help, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me about Arib. Her words were as scripture to members of the Order.

speaker: Fuladh
en: A gifted artist and poetess, Arib won her freedom through her skill. Tabid tells me she keeps a luxurious home in the Round City. Anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: What do you know of Qabiha? She had ties to the Treasurer.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Born to slavery, Qabiha rose to become Al-Mutawakkil's favorite concubine in the Harem. Yet her son was not made Caliph, leaving her future uncertain. Anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me about the Governor. I saw him give orders to Wasif al-Turki.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Muhammad is one of the Tahirids, powerful viceroys of the Caliphs in Persia. He governs all Baghdad from his seat at the Courts. Anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: Where can I find our suspects?

speaker: Fuladh
en: All three live within the glorious Round City, the power center of the Abbasid Caliphate. Anything else?

speaker: Basim
en: Shukran (Thank you), Fuladh.

speaker: Basim
en: Poet, politician, and concubine. I will soon know which one wears the mask.

speaker: Prison Master
en: Ah, my new pet. Mark my words, your stay here will be most disagreeable.

speaker: Prison Master
en: Return to your duties! Tell the others the threat is over.

speaker: Basim
en: This falls far short of my hopes.

speaker: Guard 1
en: Have you noticed... there are more of us on the day shift lately?

speaker: Guard 2
en: No one wishes to serve under that new captain overseeing the night guard. He is as ruthless as 'Abis himself. And better trained for battle.

speaker: Guard 1
en: But how are those few left on night duty meant to patrol the entire prison?

speaker: Guard 2
en: Harsh methods are their only hope.

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: Anyone alive in there? Newcomer... You still breathing?

speaker: Basim
en: Apparently.

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: Then look on the bright side, you will not be for much longer!

speaker: Basim
en: The ugly man who acts as if this place belongs to him... I get the impression he does not serve the Caliphate?

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: You mean 'Abis?

speaker: Basim
en: So that is 'Abis.

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: He treats the prison as if it is his own den. Even has a special chamber here.

speaker: Basim
en: What does he use it for?

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: To concoct his poisons... which he then tries out on us.

speaker: Basim
en: Does no one attempt to escape from here?

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: Attempt, yes. But never successfully. You can still stumble upon what is left of their unfinished escape tunnels.

speaker: Basim
en: I must keep watch for any chance to slip free... though opportunities are scarce in this place.

speaker: Basim
en: I wonder what has become of Enkidu...

speaker: Guard 3
en: Stop fretting, cook. He does not get to eat. That is the order of 'Abis. One of his little experiments. You are new here, but soon you will understand.

speaker: Servant
en: Abis is a stain on all this land.

speaker: Guard 3
en: Shut up, wench. Or maybe you would like to become the next experiment?

speaker: Basim
en: I cannot help but pity this silversmith. As for the cook, was that Hind's servant?

speaker: Basim
en: This cell is a sentence of death. Forget 'Abis or the food, boredom here is the cruelest of killers.

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: You, are you awake?

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: What crime brought you here?

speaker: Basim
en: I have committed no crime.

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: Why are you here, then?

speaker: Basim
en: I was looking for someone...

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: Who?

speaker: Basim
en: Have you heard of a man named Ishaq ibn Khalid?

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: The old fool who claims to be the Caliph's architect? He dwells in the oasis—a house with a blue door, in the farmers' quarter.

speaker: Basim
en: You are certain?

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: In AlUla, everyone knows everyone. We are a small community, after all.

speaker: Basim
en: Nimlot did not know of him.

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: Nimlot? The foreign merchant from Misr (Egypt)? He is rich. Why would he care about the likes of Ishaq ibn Khalid?

speaker: Basim
en: What more can you tell me? About Ishaq?

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: What more do you want?

speaker: Basim
en: How is he?

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: How would I know? I recognize his face, but we are not friends. If you want details, escape from here and learn them yourself.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Abis has gone too far this time. Two deaths in such a short time... First the poisoning, now the silversmith dies from starvation.

speaker: Guard 5
