en: The silversmith, especially! Outside, he was a respected member of the community.

speaker: Guard 4
en: Inside too. There will be consequences, trust me.

speaker: Basim
en: This could be poisoned. I should not take the risk.

speaker: Basim
en: There once stood a man here. Now, only bloodstains remain. I must be more than this.

speaker: Basim
en: Whoever left these marks must have been touched by madness. May I not follow the same path.

speaker: Basim
en: I pray the robbers learn nothing of Dervis. With me confined, he stands unguarded against their threat.

speaker: Guard 6
en: Abis himself nearly had us the other day. It was a close call.

speaker: Guard 7
en: You were fortunate. Keep clear of him next time.

speaker: Guard 6
en: And then there is the matter of the roof...

speaker: Guard 7
en: What about the roof?

speaker: Guard 6
en: I have been venturing up there in the evenings to take my meals. I am not the only one, to be fair.

speaker: Guard 7
en: You and the others should be careful... or you may find yourselves confined in these very same cells as punishment.

speaker: Neighboring prisoner
en: No, no! Please! Have mercy!

speaker: Guard 8
en: Not even a dog deserves that...

speaker: Guard 9
en: I am not going to tell him to stop.

speaker: Basim
en: This confinement, the threat of torture... I feel as if I have lived such a fate before... In some distant memory I cannot fully grasp...

speaker: Guard 10
en: For a man who starved to death, he is heavier than I expected.

speaker: Guard 11
en: He had plenty of friends here. Now the other prisoners are getting restless. One even struck me. I can still feel the blow.

speaker: Servant
en: You there...

speaker: Basim
en: You are Hind's servant, correct?

speaker: Servant
en: So it is you! My rescuer from the warehouse!

speaker: Basim
en: I should be equally surprised to see you in this place.

speaker: Servant
en: I did say I intended to seek a new path in life.

speaker: Basim
en: And you chose a prison, run by criminals and crooked guards, as your new calling?

speaker: Servant
en: All men must eat. Although I am not sure what I cook here counts as food, or just another form of 'Abis's torture.

speaker: Basim
en: When we last met, you swore not to forget the service I did you...

speaker: Servant
en: I remember.

speaker: Basim
en: Then perhaps you could fetch the key to this cage and hand it to me?

speaker: Servant
en: To steal the key would be far too dangerous for me. But if you can find a means to slip free of these bars, I may be able to aid you in some other way...

speaker: Basim
en: How exactly?

speaker: Servant
en: There is mandrake in the kitchen. With it, I can try to brew a sedative strong enough to lull the guards to sleep.

speaker: Basim
en: That would be a tremendous aid.

speaker: Basim
en: Where have you gone, Enkidu? If you still draw breath, I would welcome your help.

speaker: Basim
en: I should have known you would find me. If only you could aid me. The key to my cell... It is somewhere in this forsaken place.

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you, my friend! I can always count on you!

speaker: Basim
en: Though of humble make, these weapons should serve me well.

speaker: Basim
en: Freeing these captives would sow chaos, and aid my escape.

speaker: Basim
en: This is not a fate I would wish on my worst enemy.

speaker: Basim
en: The potion that Hind's servant brewed has proven potent indeed.

speaker: Basim
en: That plunge is too great, even for me.

speaker: Basim
en: That list of weapons I stole the other day... one of the hiding spots lies within these walls.

speaker: Basim
en: That poisoned blade... I can feel its filth in my blood, stronger than anything I have felt before. Perhaps Dervis can offer aid... I must reach him, and endure until then.

speaker: Basim
en: I must reach Dervis... only he can cure me.

speaker: Civilian
en: Dervis! Come!

speaker: Dervis
en: What happened? Is he alive?

speaker: Civilian
en: If so, for how much longer I do not know.

speaker: Dervis
en: Drink.

speaker: Basim
en: Nimlot did warn me. I was a fool to walk right into their trap in the market.

speaker: Dervis
en: Perhaps you still have some lessons to learn, Basim. You will mend soon enough.

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you for recovering my things.

speaker: Dervis
en: I may be old, but I still have a few tricks left. I also took the liberty of grabbing a rather fine dagger. The same one that almost ended your life. While you were away, I sought word of your father. The oasis came up...

speaker: Basim
en: During my captivity, I spoke with another prisoner. He said my father is there—the house marked by a blue door. With 'Abis dead and his men leaderless, nothing can stop me from finding him.

speaker: Dervis
en: If you wish, I can come with you...

speaker: Basim
en: I know you yearn to see him again, but for now, I must go alone.

speaker: Dervis
en: I understand, Basim. Go, find your father.

speaker: The House of Folly
en: was a genetic memory.

speaker: Known Owners
en: Unknown Current Status: Unknown For more information about this Piece of Eden, see page 186 of the Assassin's Creed – Animus Handbook.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Good, you are here.

speaker: Fuladh
en: You have kicked many nests. Mercenaries are everywhere, like angry ants.

speaker: Ali
en: It explains Beshi's absence. He's avoiding the mercenaries.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I hope the trouble was all worth it.

speaker: Basim
en: I have discovered two of the officers are working with the Order. And there is another, their leader.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Three! That would explain the Order's reach in Sharqiyah.

speaker: Basim
en: The first two go by the names Al-Rukh and Al-A'eshma. The third, they call Al-Mardikhwar.

speaker: Ali
en: They hide behind pompous names like prideful children!

speaker: Fuladh
en: Do not mistake the Order's vanities for childishness. They are the real power behind the Abbasids. Did you discover anything that would identify them?

speaker: Basim
en: The one named Al-Rukh was called Jasoor by his companion. He is hiding from his past, and lives in fear because of it.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Jasoor, yes. That must be the Arab General Jasoor ibn Basil.

speaker: Ali
en: I know of him... a coward who stole credit for victories on the battlefield won by others.

speaker: Fuladh
en: A past he has gone to great efforts to hide. Jasoor has a villa at Qasr Salih to the west. You could look for him there.

speaker: Basim
en: The one called Al-A'eshma, his real name is Nadir. He has command of ships, and is not timid like his companion. Arrogant, in fact.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Nadir...

speaker: Ali
en: That must be Admiral Nadir ibn Havid. A boastful fool, concerned more with his ships than his own men.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Ah yes, the Admiral. Boastful, perhaps, but brilliant. He has created several new warships for the Caliph. The Order's reach has grown if they have recruited Nadir. You should look for him at the Lower Harbor, to the north.

speaker: Basim
en: As for their leader, Al-Mardikhwar, I learned only that he is away from Sharqiyah, and expected to return soon.

speaker: Fuladh
en: This one I do not know. It is the first time I have heard the name.

speaker: Ali
en: If he is their leader, he ordered the death of my men. He's the one you must find.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Yes, and for other reasons besides. Our best hope of finding him is through the first two.

speaker: Ali
en: Find this Al-Mardikhwar, Basim, as we agreed. I will wait for Beshi. I am grateful for your help freeing my men.

speaker: Ali
en: Take this token, with thanks.

speaker: Basim
en: I will find Jasoor and Nadir, and unmask their leader.

speaker: Fuladh
en: They will be wary now, protected within their strongholds. You may have to lure them out. Tread carefully, Basim. These are dangerous men.

speaker: Basim
en: So am I.

speaker: Basim
en: I have some questions, Fuladh.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I hope I have answers for you.

speaker: Basim
en: What do the rebels want?

speaker: Fuladh
en: You yourself know well the divide between rich and poor. Many have grown tired of the injustice, and want change. In the beginning it was mostly slaves, but now tradesmen, the wealthy, and even some nobles support Ali's cause.

speaker: Basim
en: And Ali intends to lead them in overthrowing the Abbasid Caliphate?

speaker: Fuladh
en: Ali believes the most qualified should rule, not just the wealthy or highborn. Ironically, he considers himself the most qualified, and claims descent from the Prophet's to support it.

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me of the .

speaker: Fuladh
en: It is a bitter story. The Zanj are peoples stolen from their homelands in the of Africa, and brought here to work the fields for the wealthy.

speaker: Basim
en: So they are slaves?

speaker: Fuladh
en: They are paid, but they are not free. Like all men, they desire to be masters of their own lives.

speaker: Basim
en: What do you know about Jarjaraya?

speaker: Fuladh
en: It is a small village to the south, home to a divided population of rich and poor. Most of the Zanj are there. It has also become a refuge for those who came to Baghdad looking for work, and failed.

speaker: Basim
en: No wonder Ali has gained support there.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Yes. In few other places is the divide between those who have everything and those who have nothing so sharp.

speaker: Basim
en: What of yourself, Fuladh? How did you come to the Hidden Ones?

speaker: Fuladh
en: That is a story that should be shared around a good fire after a long meal.

speaker: Basim
en: Will you tell me nothing?

speaker: Fuladh
en: I was the child of my father's concubine. His favored wife, worried I could claim inheritance, threw us both out. I grew up in the desert alone. My friends were the animals, particularly birds. We understood each other.

speaker: Basim
en: That explains your love of eagles.

speaker: Fuladh
en: After I grew to manhood, a Hidden One saw me hunting with my birds. He brought me to the Brotherhood, and I stayed.

speaker: Basim
en: Shukran (Thank you), Fuladh. That is all for now.

speaker: Ali
en: Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: Ali.

speaker: Ali
en: Are you ready? We must go.

speaker: Basim
en: Let us go.

speaker: Ali
en: We must leave for Jarjaraya!

speaker: Ali
en: You Hidden Ones are strange. You give weapons you don't want me to use, then give me credit for your victories.

speaker: Basim
en: War would be bad for everyone, especially you.

speaker: Ali
en: That is your masters speaking.

speaker: Ali
en: Does it not bother you that those you obey are the same ones who make the rules demanding your obedience?

speaker: Basim
en: They do not control me, I am free. I fight so that others are free as well.

speaker: Ali
en: Everything you do serves the Hidden Ones. That is a strange kind of freedom.

speaker: Basim
en: The Hidden Ones are my family. There is no contradiction.

speaker: Ali
en: If you say so.

speaker: Basim
en: Once, I lived on the streets and answered only to myself. But I was not free.

speaker: Ali
en: Now that others tell you who you are, are you any freer?

speaker: Basim
en: You could not understand.

speaker: Ali
en: I understand better than you.

speaker: Civilian 1
en: There's another one. Who is he? I've never seen him before.

speaker: Civilian 2
en: Where are all these strangers coming from? Jarjaraya isn't safe anymore.

speaker: Civilian 3
en: Ali, you are here! Alhamdulillah! (Praise be to God!)

speaker: Civilian 4
en: Ali, I know you will avenge us!

speaker: Ali
en: If you are truly free, why the struggle within?

speaker: Basim
en: What do you mean? There is no struggle.

speaker: Ali
en: I see that what you think is at war with what you feel. You will never find truth if you are not first truthful with yourself.

speaker: Basim
en: No man can see what another thinks.

speaker: Ali
en: No normal man. But look at me. I obey no one, I am ruled by no one. I am free.

speaker: Basim
en: I want to look around before Beshi arrives in Jarjaraya with the bodies.

speaker: Ali
en: That would be wise. People here are already angry. Things will be worse after the burials. There is a teahouse nearby. Tea drinkers talk. You might hear something there about who is taking our men.

speaker: Basim
en: What will you do?

speaker: Ali
en: I have my own inquiries to make. Meet me back here if you discover something.

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: Marhaban! (Welcome!) Please, find a seat. Or perhaps view my unparalleled selection of teas. The finest in all Baghdad!

speaker: Basim
en: This looks like the teahouse Ali mentioned.

speaker: Civilian
en: How is your tea, ya sayyidi (sir)?

speaker: Elder
en: This is cold! Get me another, and heat it this time!

speaker: Civilian
en: Yes, sayyidi (sir). A thousand apologies.

speaker: Elder
en: Perfectly good Zanj slaves go missing, yet incompetents like you remain. No! Stop talking. Just get my tea!

speaker: Civilian
en: You work and work and what do you get? Nothing! Damned slaves! I treat them well, I pay them well, I feed them... and then they disappear. And no one's left to work!

speaker: Basim
en: He might talk... if I can sober him up.

speaker: Basim
en: Time to sober up.

speaker: Civilian
en: Enough! I'm better!

speaker: Basim
en: A teahouse is a dangerous place to be drinking. You could have been arrested.

speaker: Civilian
en: I've just had a lot of trouble lately.

speaker: Basim
en: You said some of your slaves have gone missing.

speaker: Civilian
en: Did I? I don't remember. Not just missing, they disappeared!

speaker: Basim
en: People do not just disappear.

speaker: Civilian
en: These did! Last night two of mine did not come back from the fields. No one saw anything. They just disappeared. Poof!

speaker: Basim
en: So you thought you would get drunk in a public teahouse.

speaker: Civilian
en: Well... yeah. Oh, my head. Look, do not tell anyone. I have to go home and fall over.

speaker: Basim
en: Someone who loves tea would find this irresistible.

speaker: Basim
en: I overheard you mention that slaves have gone missing.

speaker: Elder
en: What? Who are you? How dare you talk to me. Go away!

speaker: Basim
en: You are obviously a man of taste. I would be willing to part with a brick of tea for a moment of your time.

speaker: Elder
en: I thought I... wait, tea? All right, but be quick, before anyone sees me talking to you.

speaker: Basim
en: You mentioned Zanj slaves have been going missing.

speaker: Elder
en: I don't see what it has to do with you, but yes. A stranger, one of those rebels, has been disturbing the slaves. After he spoke with them, they disappeared. No doubt he's an acquaintance of that troublemaker Ali ibn Muhammad. That's all I know. Now leave before someone who matters sees me talking with someone like you.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps a token will change your mind.

speaker: Elder
en: How dare you! What do you... Wait, how did you come by one of those? Fine, but make it quick!

speaker: Basim
en: You mentioned Zanj slaves have been going missing.

speaker: Elder
en: I don't see what it has to do with you, but yes. A stranger, one of those rebels, has been disturbing the slaves. After he spoke with them, they disappeared. No doubt he's an acquaintance of that troublemaker Ali ibn Muhammad. That's all I know. Now leave before someone who matters sees me talking with someone like you.

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: Hey! Over here! This way!

speaker: Basim
en: Did you want something?

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: Not here, there are too many... ears, if you take my meaning.

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: Ah, yes sayyidi (sir)! Our special teas are kept in the back. This way, watch your step!

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: Follow me. Act casual.

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: All right. It's clear.

speaker: Basim
en: Well, we... seem to be alone. What did you want?

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: Sorry for the melodramatics, but you never know who is watching. And this sneaking about is all rather exciting! I saw your red sash and heard you talking about missing slaves. Another has disappeared form a farmhouse near here.

speaker: Basim
en: How do you know of this?

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: I am friendly with the family. The husband was one of those executed. Now the son has gone missing as well. His mother is beside herself with worry. I thought you might be able to help her.

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me where this farmhouse is.

speaker: Tea House Owner
en: A little to the west. Slaves don't trust easily, but if you can do anything for her, I would consider it a personal favor.

speaker: Basim
en: I should return to Ali and tell him what I have discovered.

speaker: Ali
en: Did you know I can hear what men think?

speaker: Beshi
en: We should not do this. It will only make more trouble for us.

speaker: Ali
en: More trouble than executions?

speaker: Ali
en: They slaughtered our brothers. How do you not understand?

speaker: Basim
en: Ali, what is this? This is not what we agreed to.

speaker: Ali
en: I do what must be done. I do not need your approval. Did you discover something?

speaker: Basim
en: Slaves are disappearing from all over Jarjaraya, one from a nearby farmhouse. I will go there, and see what I can find.

speaker: Ali
en: Good. Our friend here has been spending his mornings at the harbor, meeting with one we think is informing for the Caliph. You could find this informant and follow him. See where that leads. Meanwhile, Beshi and I will loosen our friend's tongue.

speaker: Beshi
en: This is a mistake, Ali.

speaker: Ali
en: Let us see...

speaker: Basim
en: I should look for the informant, and help the widow find her missing son.

speaker: Basim
en: This is the harbor. The informant is here somewhere.

speaker: Informant
en: Hmph. No notes today. I should get going. It's almost time.

speaker: Basim
en: Time for what, I wonder? I should follow him, but I cannot let him see me.

speaker: Informant
en: I've got new information.

speaker: Soldier
en: What have you got for me?

speaker: Informant
en: Apart from that slave kid I already told you about, someone's been sniffing around Jarjaraya, asking questions.

speaker: Soldier
en: Is it the one we reported last time, that troublemaker Beshi?

speaker: Informant
en: This one is new. No one seems to know anything about him.

speaker: Soldier
en: What are you doing then? I'm carrying letters for the boss, and you're wasting my time! Come back when you've got a name.

speaker: Basim
en: These two were gathering information for someone called Dogan bin Arslan. I must find this Dogan, but first I should help the widow with her missing son. Perhaps it is connected.

speaker: Ali
en: You return at last.

speaker: Basim
en: What have you done?

speaker: Ali
en: What I had to do.

speaker: Basim
en: Is this what your freedom looks like?

speaker: Ali
en: I do not follow your creed, nor do I answer to the Hidden Ones. This is the price of war.

speaker: Basim
en: Beshi would disagree...

speaker: Ali
en: Beshi does not lead this rebellion! He does his part, and I do mine. But enough. What have you discovered?

speaker: Basim
en: The missing slaves were taken at the order of one called Dogan bin Arslan. Something big is happening soon. I do not know what.

speaker: Ali
en: I do. This one said my men are being interrogated, and are to be executed by their leader afterward at the villa.

speaker: Basim
en: Ali, the informant mentioned Beshi by name. They are looking for him.

speaker: Ali
en: Let them look. Go free my men. I will prepare our attack on the villa. Meet me near the farm when you are done.

speaker: Basim
en: This looks like the farm where Ali's men were being held.

speaker: Soldier
en: These stupid slaves are going to be sorry they didn't just do their work.

speaker: Soldier
en: The boss won't go easy on them. He loves his work.

speaker: Rebel
en: Alhamdulillah! (Praise be to God!) We thought we were dead.

speaker: Rebel
en: Get me out of here.

speaker: Basim
en: Ali is waiting just outside the farm. Go quickly.

speaker: Basim
en: The widow's son is not here.

speaker: Soldier
en: I heard the kid is the son of one of those executed rebels. He came looking for his father's killers.

speaker: Soldier
en: Well, he found them, didn't he? He'll go the same way as his father now.

speaker: Basim
en: Your mother is waiting for you.

speaker: Basim
en: You are brave. Fine, meet Ali outside the farm.

speaker: Basim
en: That is all of them. I should meet with Ali.

speaker: Basim
en: Is everyone here?

speaker: Ali
en: Dogan bin Arslan dies now. We wait only for you.

speaker: Basim
en: I am ready. Let us go.

speaker: Ali
en: They stole you from your homes when you were free, and brought you here to die in their fields as slaves. They slaughtered our brothers like dogs in Sharqiyah. Now they have taken more of us.

speaker: Rebel
en: No!

speaker: Ali
en: I promised you a new life. I gave you my word. More join us every day, from the least in Baghdad to the greatest. Allah is with us. Our cause is righteous. Our justice is destined. God is great! God is great! There is no God but God, and God is great!

speaker: Rebel
en: There is no God but God!

speaker: Ali
en: There is no judgement but by God!

speaker: Dogan
en: You rebels need to learn your place!

speaker: Ali
en: When word gets out of this victory, many will join our cause.

speaker: Basim
en: Dogan bin Arslan was carrying orders. He was to report to superiors at the Officers' Club in Sharqiyah.

speaker: Ali
en: Those superiors may be who ordered the executions. Does it name them?

speaker: Basim
en: It uses codenames. Al-Rukh and Al-A'eshma. Only the Order uses such names. I will go to this club and see what I can find.

speaker: Ali
en: I wish you luck. I must return and wait for Beshi.

speaker: Basim
en: Be careful, Ali. The Caliph will be hunting you both after this.

speaker: Ali
en: There are things we cannot hide from if we are to be truly free.

speaker: Basim
en: I should go to the Officers' Club in Sharqiyah.

speaker: Soldier
en: Where is that ugly two-faced dog! He is hiding somewhere!

speaker: The Informant
en: Achoo... Achoo... ACHOOO!

speaker: Basim
en: That noise demands a closer look.

speaker: Basim
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: The Informant
en: Yes. My legs ... I cannot walk.

speaker: Basim
en: Then I will carry you.

speaker: The Informant
en: We are up against some very dangerous people... I had no idea.

speaker: Basim
en: I am sure Ali will be most interested to hear what you have learned.

speaker: The Informant
en: The spices in that pot. Ya lalqaraf! (Yuck!) They tickled my nose. (sneezing)

speaker: Basim
en: Done to perfection.

speaker: The Informant
en: Thank you. You can go. I will be okay now.

speaker: Basim
en: They are not expecting trouble. I could likely slip in without any bloodshed.

speaker: Basim
en: I am here to get you out.

speaker: Scholar
en: Alhamdulillah! (Praise be to God!) There is only one small problem. I have suffered some injuries and I am not sure I can walk.

speaker: Basim
en: Why did the bandits kidnap you?

speaker: Scholar
en: They uncovered an ancient legend concerning a great treasure in this region. And given that I am an historian of some renown, they assumed I might be of use in locating said treasure.

speaker: Basim
en: A fine finish.

speaker: Basim
en: You are safe here. Now, about this treasure...

speaker: Scholar
en: Treasure? Ha! There is none. At least not of the golden variety. Of course, I could not tell the bandits that. Otherwise they would have slit my throat and moved on.

speaker: Basim
en: So, if not gold...

speaker: Scholar
en: It is the water that flows beneath our feet. In a barren land, that water is more precious than many armfuls of gold.

speaker: Basim
en: I see... Alhamdulillah. (Praise be to God.)

speaker: Basim
en: I have to get out of here. I have to tell Nehal what I have learned.

speaker: Soldier
en: You will not escape justice!

speaker: Basim
en: Alhamdulillah. Again, I have escaped with my life... and left things broken behind me.

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim? Are you well? Basim...

speaker: Basim
en: I... I do not know, you... you were right, Nehal. My enemy, Qabiha... she held the answers.

speaker: Nehal
en: What did you learn?

speaker: Basim
en: That there is more to who I am. A truth Qabiha tried to tell me. A truth my Master sought to silence. That truth lies at Alamut.

speaker: Nehal
en: So we ride for Alamut.

speaker: Basim
en: I need to think on this, still.

speaker: Nehal
en: Fine. Come back to me when you are ready to face your future.

speaker: Nehal
en: Are you now ready to ride for Alamut?

speaker: Basim
en: I will go, Nehal. I alone.

speaker: Nehal
en: You need me.

speaker: Basim
en: I need you safe.

speaker: Nehal
en: I am safe with you. And you with me.

speaker: Basim
en: I may find find nothing there but danger and death. This is my fate. I will not turn back from it but neither will I have you face it.

speaker: Nehal
en: Where you go, there I will go. Where you rest, there I will rest. I will walk behind you every step of the way. You are never alone. Now get packing. We will not leave Alamut until you have found the answers you seek.

speaker: Basim
en: Yah! Imshi (Go)!

speaker: Basim
en: Yah Yah! Yalla (Let's go)!

speaker: Basim
en: NEHAL?!

speaker: Basim
en: R-Roshan...?

speaker: Basim
en: Nur?

speaker: Nur
en: Not the welcome you were expecting, eh? Well, at least you had the fortune to be elsewhere when the Tahirids came for us.

speaker: Basim
en: What happened?

speaker: Nur
en: I... fear Alamut has fallen. I was tasked with finding help. I went into the desert, to find other patrols. Then I found you.

speaker: Basim
en: Were there... others? With me?

speaker: Nur
en: No. Only you.

speaker: Basim
en: Then Nehal lives. And Roshan?

speaker: Nur
en: I had hoped she would be with you.

speaker: Basim
en: Come, brother. We must head out. Find any survivors, and cleanse Alamut of its infestation.

speaker: Nur
en: I... fear I cannot.

speaker: Basim
en: How bad?

speaker: Basim
en: I will make every last one of them pay.

speaker: Nur
en: Vengeance is not our way, brother.

speaker: Basim
en: Our way? You sit bleeding to death and still cling to this... foolish dogma! And for what? Our Creed could not protect Alamut. And neither could I.

speaker: Nur
en: Nor I. But... our beliefs are why you still draw breath. And are why you must save any of us who may yet live.

speaker: Basim
en: On that we can agree. You have my word.

speaker: Nur
en: Waffaqaka Allah, Basim. There is nothing left to say, brother. Go. Save who you can.

speaker: Basim
en: A curious choice for a meeting place. Do you have the marked coins?

speaker: Hidden One
en: They are waiting for you at Damascus Gate.

speaker: Basim
en: What! Is this some kind of trick?

speaker: Hidden One
en: No trick. A race! I believe I am fast enough to outrun your reputation. See you at the gate!

speaker: Basim
en: I should retrieve the coins at Damascus Gate before someone else does.

speaker: Basim
en: A good effort, but no matter how loud the wind howls, it will never move the mountain.

speaker: Hidden One
en: Today you were lucky. Tomorrow, perhaps not?

speaker: Basim
en: Today you have enjoyed a fine victory. But do not let it swell your head.

speaker: Basim
en: I have the coins. Now to make haste and deliver them.

speaker: The Trade Delegate
en: I appreciate the service, but you are late. Please be a little quicker next time.

speaker: Basim
en: Gah!

speaker: Nehal
en: Easy, Basim. Breathe.

speaker: Nehal
en: Was it the jinni again?

speaker: Nehal
en: And what did our friend want this time?

speaker: Basim
en: To strip the flesh from my bones? Dine on my innards? Never has much to say, yet it leaves its mark. I can still feel it crawling on my skin.

speaker: Nehal
en: Hardly original. You should tell it as much.

speaker: Basim
en: Forget the jinni for the moment. The day is new, there is work to be done. Dervis has left another contract.

speaker: Nehal
en: Who for?

speaker: Nehal
en: Them again? We would make more money selling water to a camel.

speaker: Basim
en: Come, Nehal. Where is your sense of duty?

speaker: Nehal
en: Duty does not fill our bellies.

speaker: Basim
en: No, but it does enrich the soul.

speaker: Nehal
en: I will be outside.

speaker: Basim
en: I told Nehal this would be impossible to sell when she stole it. But she could not resist. Wonder what it is about these ancient baubles that fascinates her so.

speaker: Nehal
en: Kick up some sand, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: Cheap jewels and tarnished coins. The spoils of a rogue's life.

speaker: Basim
en: "It takes but a few simple tools to build the ." I hope to continue to share your wisdom father... wherever you are.

speaker: Nehal
en: The sun casts a long shadow.

speaker: Basim
en: Let us not keep Dervis waiting. I cannot bear another lecture.

speaker: Nehal
en: These contracts... it is quite a few Dervis has pushed your way now.

speaker: Basim
en: He knows I will come through.

speaker: Nehal
en: You have his trust, that much is clear. Do you suppose you have theirs? These... shadowy types.

speaker: Basim
en: I should hope so by now.

speaker: Nehal
en: Then they should show it. You take all the risk and they offer little in return.

speaker: Basim
en: They are liberators, Nehal. Not merchants.

speaker: Nehal
en: I know the stories. Still, the price of liberty should be enough to feed us.

speaker: Nehal
en: About this contract... I do not want you to mistake my words for pestering. I am only looking out for you, ya sadeeqi (friend).

speaker: Basim
en: It is no inconvenience to stand up to our oppressors as the Hidden Ones do.

speaker: Nehal
en: Do you think yourself some hero of tomorrow? The next Gilgamesh?

speaker: Basim
en: No, I am merely the son of a public servant who dedicated his life to the betterment of his people... only to be slighted and forgotten.

speaker: Basim
en: But I am honored you think I could reach such heights. I may just aim for them.

speaker: Nehal
en: That is not at all what I said.

speaker: Basim
en: It is what I heard!

speaker: Nehal
en: Such crowds. Something important must be happening.

speaker: Basim
en: The Caliph (Steward) has been summoned to the Winter Palace. It is surely his wealthy retinue that drives this crowd.

speaker: Nehal
en: Ah... Perhaps they're in the mood to offer donations...

speaker: Basim
en: Ah. I see your meaning. A little sleight of hands to sharpen our wits?

speaker: Nehal
en: If this contract will not feed us, the Caliphate might as well.

speaker: Nehal
en: That merchant has left his purse on the table. An easy one to begin with.

speaker: Basim
en: Better leave before they notice.

speaker: Civilian
en: Gah! Liss! Liss! (Thief! Thief!)

speaker: Nehal
en: Come here! Ready yourself. I will pick them out.

speaker: Basim
en: A keen eye and an agile hand. A formidable duo.

speaker: Nehal
en: Hmm. There. The boisterous one. He must have something of value.

speaker: Nehal
en: Sneaky sneaky...

speaker: Nehal
en: And... over there, by that stall. She's got some coin.

speaker: Nehal
en: Well done. You truly are the Master Thief of Anbar.

speaker: Basim
en: Is that jealousy I hear?

speaker: Nehal
en: Hardly, oh Great Looter of Purses.

speaker: Basim
en: Insufferable... Come, we are late to Dervis'.

speaker: Nehal
en: They're all looking spry. I wonder what tales we will hear today.

speaker: Basim
en: Tall ones, most certainly.

speaker: Fehmi
en: Ahlan (Welcome), Basim! Come here, come here!

speaker: Basim
en: Fehmi.

speaker: Fehmi
en: Basim! The Caliph has arrived with his court! Have you seen them?

speaker: Basim
en: I have not. Though I did meet some of his merchants at the markets.

speaker: Fehmi
en: I saw them up close. Al-Mutawakkil is much, much larger than I had imagined. A towering man, indeed.

speaker: Basim
en: Of course. He gorges on food served with the finest spices you and I can only hope to one day taste.

speaker: Fehmi
en: I heard whispers of an important visit. But I cannot say from whom. I am sworn to secrecy!

speaker: Basim
en: Let me guess. Halaa. The palace guard's daughter.

speaker: Fehmi
en: What? How did you know?

speaker: Basim
en: I know where you really go when you say you are fetching water. She is kind. A good friend to you. And... maybe more, someday.

speaker: Fehmi
en: Ooh Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: I am serious! She will keep you out of trouble. You could use that. See you, Fehmi.

speaker: Ameen
en: Steal anything good today?

speaker: Basim
en: Ameen, how is your knee?

speaker: Ameen
en: Much better, Basim! Wrapped it and rested a few days, like you said.

speaker: Basim
en: Good. So long as each day is better than the last and you take care not to extend yourself, you will recover fine.

speaker: Ameen
en: Has this happened to you before? Is that why you know how to treat it?

speaker: Basim
en: I am no stranger to scrapes and bumps, but I have learned to prevent them. And so should you. If I may, your sandals are worn and cannot grip the ground. Your knees are taking the brunt of your movements. We need to find you something better. Something that fits. But that part is not so easy.

speaker: Ameen
en: The mosques have plenty. I am sure to find a better pair there! Erm, if you will not pass judgement...

speaker: Basim
en: Hah! Do not look to me. That will be between you and Allah, ya sadeeqi (friend).

speaker: Dervis
en: Vay vay vay (Well well well), here is the lazy boy. I have been waiting on you.

speaker: Basim
en: Someone has to plan our meals.

speaker: Basim
en: Hold.

speaker: Basim
en: Food. I would not flaunt that around the markets. Trust me.

speaker: Dervis
en: Go to Zaida'! She uses lots of butter.

speaker: Nehal
en: That she does.

speaker: Dervis
en: You look weary. Are you well?

speaker: Basim
en: It is nothing a little adventure wouldn't fix. What do they need?

speaker: Dervis
en: A shipping ledger at the harbor. It is worth nothing by itself, but the information it contains is valuable to them.

speaker: Basim
en: This is child's play. Do they not have anything more difficult? I can do more.

speaker: Dervis
en: Never mind your ego. The Caliph's guards are here in number and you would do well to remember that.

speaker: Basim
en: You worry for me more now than when we lived in Baghdad.

speaker: Dervis
en: My worry is the same, I've only grown too old and too tired to hide it. Bring the ledger here, and do it swiftly.

speaker: Basim
en: We have not talked about my fee.

speaker: Dervis
en: And we won't. Not until the deed is done. You know how they are.

speaker: Nehal
en: Shocking.

speaker: Basim
en: He is just a messenger.

speaker: Nehal
en: And you are still an errand boy. You can do this one on your own.

speaker: Fehmi
en: I saw them with all the soldiers parading into the Winter Palace.

speaker: Ameen
en: Did they have swords and spears?

speaker: Fehmi
en: Of course they did, they are soldiers.

speaker: Ameen
en: I'd like to steal a sword. Or a helmet.

speaker: Basim
en: Mutee'a, where has your smile run off to? What has happened?

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, but I refuse to leave until you do. We need someone to offset the grouchy winds that billow from Dervis' quarters. Is he responsible for the clouds that hang above you?

speaker: Basim
en: Harsh! I would have done the same as you.

speaker: Basim
en: Ah, Mutee'a, you do not know him as well as I, so I will only say this. Dervis may appear rough, but he has a soft underbelly. He's only trying to protect you. Still, some retribution is in order. What can we do, what can we do... Ah! Tomorrow, when all is quiet, we will sit on a nearby rooftop and stone his walls while he tries to sleep.

speaker: Basim
en: Did they say anything else about the ledger? Or why they want it?

speaker: Dervis
en: Ugh, I tell you what they tell me, Basim. As always, it's just enough. Why are you asking, hmm?

speaker: Basim
en: I would like to know just what it is I am contributing to.

speaker: Dervis
en: You have done much in the way of facilitating their endeavors, and so I will speak a word on your behalf. My one caution, and I have been doing this long enough to share it... Anyone, anyone who works from the shadows does so only because they must. In the face of looming danger, for example. By working alongside them we have invited the danger to our door. And we must be very careful not to let it in.

speaker: Nehal
en: You are on your own, Basim. This is no contract, it is a favor. I do not work for scraps.

speaker: Basim
en: I do not wish for you to be upset. I took the contract, so I will see it through.

speaker: Nehal
en: I am not upset, Basim. I simply cannot understand why you overlook your own interests to serve theirs. You owe nothing to anyone but yourself. Remember that.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: What was the final tally of what we received?

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Sixteen crates. One chest. Half a dozen satchels. Only three crates remained last time I checked the ledger.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Give their handlers until tomorrow evening. If they don't show by then, we must assume they've forgotten about their wares. Open them up. Keep whatever catches our eyes. Dump the rest.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Wait here.

speaker: Basim
en: If I am seen I will have to flee. Good thing I can outrun these sagging guards.

speaker: Basim
en: Locked. A minor delay.

speaker: Basim
en: There. That may be what I'm looking for.

speaker: Basim
en: I wonder wat secrets this ledger holds. Maybe I can get the old grouser Dervis to squeeze a hint out of our contact.

speaker: Nehal
en: Still in one piece, I see.

speaker: Basim
en: It was all too easy.

speaker: Nehal
en: Ugh, how the stench of pride seeps from your pores...

speaker: Roshan
en: We could use some eyes around the city.

speaker: Dervis
en: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Nehal
en: She looks important. You should haggle for a better fee.

speaker: Basim
en: Shh.

speaker: Dervis
en: Ah, Basim. What timing. Did you get it?

speaker: Basim
en: Without a fuss.

speaker: Roshan
en: Give it here.

speaker: Basim
en: You are one of them.

speaker: Roshan
en: There. It looks as though it was delivered this morning.

speaker: Dervis
en: You're certain it is the chest you seek?

speaker: Roshan
en: I am certain. Pay the boy.

speaker: Basim
en: You need something stolen, I am your man. Dervis can attest. He has given me all your contracts.

speaker: Roshan
en: Then you have done your part.

speaker: Basim
en: I can do more.

speaker: Roshan
en: Two of my best men died on this pursuit. I doubt a street thief would fare much better.

speaker: Basim
en: Then let me join you. You have two openings!

speaker: Dervis
en: I should take half this fee for that insult.

speaker: Basim
en: Thank you, Dervis.

speaker: Dervis
en: Listen here, Basim. You want to keep working for me, you keep your head down and your mouth shut!

speaker: Nehal
en: Why must you embarrass yourself like that?

speaker: Basim
en: Like what?

speaker: Nehal
en: Like a beggar. Desperate for them to notice you.

speaker: Basim
en: Desperate? Nehal, I am good at what I do. That woman would be lucky to have me.

speaker: Nehal
en: But she does not want you. You are a street thief with dirty feet. So why bother? Why keep pushing yourself down this path?

speaker: Basim
en: Because being a street thief is not the peak of my ambition. I have more to offer this world than my nimble fingers. They just cannot see it yet.

speaker: Basim
en: Almost, Jasib.

speaker: Basim
en: What is this?

speaker: Jasib
en: Aha! It is my latest creation. It helps me fend off angry merchants when they, uh, catch me digging around their wares.

speaker: Basim
en: I will consider myself spared. You smell foul. What is that?

speaker: Jasib
en: Ha! We have been fishing at the harbor since morning. Terrible luck, though.

speaker: Basim
en: The harbor? Did you happen to see or hear any fuss over a chest?

speaker: Jasib
en: Hm. Ah yes! A black one. Very beautiful. Some burly guards took it with them to the palace.

speaker: Basim
en: Shukran lak ya (thank you), Jasib.

speaker: Nehal
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Basim
en: They want that chest, and I am going to get it for them. Then they will see.

speaker: Nehal
en: There is just no getting through to you, is there?

speaker: Nehal
en: Then we will do this together. If you get caught at the Winter Palace, they will kill you on sight. We will need a safe way in. And I know where we might scout one. That is, if you can follow my lead for a change. Shall we go scout the Winter Palace now?

speaker: Basim
en: You do not have to get involved, Nehal. I know your feelings on this.

speaker: Nehal
en: It is utterly foolish. But it seems I cannot stop you. So I will come with, and nag you until you decide to abandon the idea of stealing a chest from the Caliph's. Winter. Palace.

speaker: Basim
en: When you say it like that, it only excites me further.

speaker: Nehal
en: Are we going or not?

speaker: Basim
en: Lead the way.

speaker: Nehal
en: This is a mad plan, Basim. Even if you were to succeed and they welcome you into their ranks, what then? Will you forget about us?

speaker: Basim
en: Of course not. Nehal, their intentions are our interests You, me and every street dweller who has been cast aside, living off scraps and dirty water. I can be an instrument that sees us out of that life. That sees that Jasib can use his talents to be a real craftsman. That sees that good men are not cast aside as my father was. And no children left wondering what tomorrow will bring.

speaker: Nehal
en: I hear what you are saying, Basim. But you paint a portrait of a world that cannot exist.

speaker: Basim
en: That is where we disagree.

speaker: Nehal
en: There it is. The Winter Palace. Come, this way.

speaker: Basim
en: Right behind you.

speaker: Nehal
en: Here. Let us wait for nightfall.

speaker: Nehal
en: Does where you stand not awaken fond memories?

speaker: Basim
en: Not so long ago we were counting our spoils up here under the cover of night, just like this.

speaker: Nehal
en: The stakes were lower then.

speaker: Basim
en: And so too was the prize.

speaker: Nehal
en: Well, before you claim your prize you will first have to reach it. And so far as I can see, that will take some creativity.

speaker: Basim
en: We could always try the front gate.

speaker: Nehal
en: You will have to let me know how that goes for you.

speaker: Basim
en: Where are you going?

speaker: Nehal
en: I've had a clever thought. If your mind is absent of one, you should perhaps follow mine.

speaker: Basim
en: Wait. (sigh)

speaker: Nehal
en: It is dark enough. Come.

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal.

speaker: Nehal
en: Fastening yourself to my tail, Basim? Very sensible.

speaker: Basim
en: I know how you hate to be alone.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: ...and then roasted, stuffed lamb. Oh, yes.

speaker: Nehal
en: I see some guards just that way.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Lentils with lime sauce, pomegranates and lemon. I can taste it now.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Shh! I heard something. A low roar.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Indeed! My stomach!

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Have you seen the guests? Such odd costumes.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Keep your mouth shut. You'll only invite trouble talking that.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Why dress that way, is all I'm asking. It's not festival time.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: They are here to meet the Caliph about the chest that arrived this morning. Which, need I remind you, is none of our concern.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: Are you not curious?

speaker: Soldier 4
en: Even if I am, it will not break my focus.

speaker: Nehal
en: Ah, good. This door may lead us inside.

speaker: Basim
en: Not without a key it won't.

speaker: Nehal
en: Hmm. Have a look around.

speaker: Nehal
en: Any luck finding the key?

speaker: Soldier 5
en: The Caliph appears unsettled. An unruly son is not helping matters.

speaker: Soldier 6
en: The young man is eager. It's his first time in the palace, is it not? Let him wander, I say. Cater to his needs. This meeting is supposed to be brief, after all.

speaker: Soldier 6
en: Here they are. Come.

speaker: Soldier 6
en: Through here. The Caliph awaits you.

speaker: Soldier 6
en: They have arrived, Mawlay (my lord).

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: Out. All of you. I am to meet with them alone.

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: Take him.

speaker: Nehal
en: Looks heavy. We'll never get it out of the palace.

speaker: Basim
en: Then I will just have to take what is inside.

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: Gentlemen. Welcome. Everything is in order.

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: I understand this means a great deal to you. Rest assured, it will be well protected here.

speaker: Masked Figure
en: We will accept nothing less. We will carry out our work and return to you when we are ready. Be prepared, Caliph.

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: Ah, might I see it once? The contents? If we are to guard this with our lives we should know

speaker: Masked Figure
en: You saw nothing of this. You say nothing. Do you understand?

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: Y-yes, of course. Perish the idea.

speaker: Basim
en: Now is our chance.

speaker: Nehal
en: Someone is coming.

speaker: Nehal
en: This way. Looks quiet.

speaker: Nehal
en: I never thought I'd set foot in here. Just look at these arches. You could chisel off a piece and sell it for a hoard of gold. You didn't happen to bring a pickaxe did you?

speaker: Basim
en: I will keep it in mind for the next time we break into a palace.

speaker: Basim
en: All right, Basim. Open. Snatch. Run.

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim, hurry!

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim!

speaker: Male Voice 1
en: dű-duàs hnomná arhzmr mnàæ gnsàsi (State your name for the record.)

speaker: Male Voice 2
en: hm més hr r n marhmid (Please, no—no more...)

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: Give me that!

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: No! La!

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: Do you have any idea what they will do to me?

speaker: Basim
en: Please, I—I am sorry.

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: This... This is your fault.

speaker: Basim
en: Stop! Please...!

speaker: Al-Mutawakkil
en: You thieving little rat!

speaker: Basim
en: No...

speaker: Nehal
en: Run!

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal, wait!

speaker: Soldier 7
en: Get that boy!

speaker: Soldier 8
en: Ring the bell! The Caliph is dead! Find that boy!

speaker: Soldier 9
en: Sealing the area!

speaker: Soldier 10
en: With me! He came this way.

speaker: Soldier 11
en: Burn! Cutting him off!

speaker: Soldier 12
en: No one will pass me!

speaker: Soldier 13
en: An intruder was spotted at the palace. Keep your eyes open for a young thief.

speaker: Soldier 14
en: Over there! I see him.

speaker: Soldier 15
en: The alarm bell rings! Stay alert! You there! Stop!

speaker: Basim
en: What... what have we done? Nehal... she just... What was she thinking? I need to find her. She would have gone back home.

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal?

speaker: Basim
en: No. Stop this. Please! What do you want from me?

speaker: Roshan
en: Calm! Calm, Basim.

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal?

speaker: Roshan
en: Not quite. Are you well?

speaker: Roshan
en: Good. Because I need you to tell me about... this.

speaker: Basim
en: I do not know what you mean.

speaker: Soldier
en: Search over there.

speaker: Roshan
en: Tell me what happened. Silence is not your ally here.

speaker: Basim
en: It is not silence. I cannot explain what I saw. That object. It did something to me. I was... somewhere else. Cold. And frightened. Before I knew it, the Caliph had his hands around my neck. I... it was an accident, I did not mean for... just wanted to help.

speaker: Roshan
en: We need to get you out of here. I have a boat at the western docks.

speaker: Basim
en: What? No, I-I cannot leave. I need to find Nehal.

speaker: Roshan
en: Stop and think, Basim. The Caliph's guard is searching for his murderer. A young thief of your description. They will not stop until they have found you. And when they do, it will not be a prison they throw you into. It will be a shallow grave. I am giving you a second chance. Take it.

speaker: Basim
en: Nehal... Dervis... they are all in danger!

speaker: Basim
en: The soldiers are hunting all who look like me.

speaker: Soldier
en: We are not to show mercy, men. Is that clear?

speaker: Basim
en: I will not be safe for certain if I do not lose these guards.

speaker: Nehal
en: Basim. Basim! Avert your eyes.

speaker: Nehal
en: There is nothing we could have done.

speaker: Basim
en: Nothing? If the Caliph were alive, this would not have happened!

speaker: Nehal
en: Watch where you point your blamey little finger, Basim. It was your idea to steal from the palace. All so that you could impress your cunning friends. I saved us.

speaker: Basim
en: You killed them! You did this!

speaker: Soldier
en: It came from over there.

speaker: Basim
en: I hope I never see you again.

speaker: Basim
en: All of them dead... when it was me they sought to punish. I... I... I cannot be here. I cannot.

speaker: Soldier
en: Scour the alleys for thieves. Round up every last one. Proceed.

speaker: Soldier 9
en: Stop. Is it him?

speaker: Soldier 10
en: I think so.

speaker: Soldier 9
en: Good enough.

speaker: Roshan
en: Move!

speaker: Basim
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Roshan
en: Don't think.

speaker: Basim
en: Truly, AlUla is a land of the rarest beauty.

speaker: Dervis
en: Basim, over here! I hope you are well-rested...

speaker: Basim
en: It was a fitful night. Sleep did not come easily.

speaker: Basim
en: The moment of truth. Ishaq ibn Khalid... Let us look for a grave bearing his name.

speaker: Dervis
en: If he is here, our quest is done... And if he is not, there is still hope.

speaker: Basim
en: Jareer ibn Sulaym... this is not my father's final resting place.

speaker: Basim
en: Do you recall the day my father was exiled?

speaker: Dervis
en: Your father was a good man, but also a proud one. When he was exiled, the burden of his shame was more than he could bear.

speaker: Basim
en: So ashamed that he abandoned me?

speaker: Basim
en: Rashid Al-Asadi... We must keep searching.

speaker: Basim
en: The day my father left me with you... That moment has stayed with me ever since.

speaker: Dervis
en: Of all the children who have come under my care... You were silent at first, but the pain in your eyes said enough.

speaker: Basim
en: You have been a father to so many of us orphans...Yet the horror that befell Jasib and the others...

speaker: Dervis
en: They are gone from this world, Basim, but not from our hearts.

speaker: Basim
en: I will examine the graves to the north. You, in the meantime, continue scouring the other burial grounds.

speaker: Basim
en: Mansoor Al-Kilabi... Not my father. A lifetime of hopes and fears, victories and defeats... reduced to a name etched on crumbling stone. It feels so... insubstantial.

speaker: Dervis
en: Our bodies are insubstantial. The soul is what matters. You can threaten a man, plunder his goods, torture his flesh, even take his life. But his soul is his own... no one can seize that.

speaker: Basim
en: There is no sign of him here.

speaker: Basim
en: My apologies, is Enkidu troubling you? This is not the way he usually acts.

speaker: Hind
en: He startled me, but I see now he means no disrespect to my late husband.

speaker: Basim
en: I am sorry for your loss. What is your name?

speaker: Hind
en: I am Hind.

speaker: Basim
en: And I am Basim... Tell me, Hind, how long have you been here?

speaker: Hind
en: I... I do not know. Time has no meaning anymore.

speaker: Basim
en: You must be exhausted. Allow me to escort you to your home.

speaker: Hind
en: You are very kind.

speaker: Dervis
en: I shall seek word of your father. If you need me, I'll be back at the tent.

speaker: Basim
en: Forgive me if I am being too forward, but I assume your husband's passing was recent?

speaker: Hind
en: He has been gone three days... though he had been ill for a long time. He often suffered chest pains this past year.

speaker: Basim
en: Do you have children?

speaker: Hind
en: Two boys, both still young. My husband has left enough wealth to care for us until the boys are old enough to make their own way.

speaker: Basim
en: Your sons are waiting for you at home?

speaker: Hind
en: They are staying with relatives... I am not the company they deserve right now.

speaker: Basim
en: Your grief carries no shame, Hind... I too tasted its bitterness when I was a child and lost the people I cherished most.

speaker: Hind
en: Your parents?

speaker: Basim
en: My mother died young, and my father... It is complicated.

speaker: Hind
en: I am sorry.

speaker: Basim
en: Still, I was fortunate to find another family... in a manner of speaking.

speaker: Hind
en: The heavier man at the cemetery?

speaker: Basim
en: Heavier man? Do not let him hear you say that.

speaker: Hind
en: My husband grew heavy later in life... You might ask your friend if he suffers from chest pains and heart flutters.

speaker: Basim
en: I doubt he would appreciate the thought. In his mind, he remains in his prime, though his body says otherwise.

speaker: Hind
en: Then he is a typical man.

speaker: Hind
en: We are nearly there. See, that is my home. And beside it, my husband's warehouse...

speaker: Hind
en: That... that mark. They are here.

speaker: Basim
en: Who?

speaker: Hind
en: They... they came for my husband's valuables.

speaker: Basim
en: Robbers, then?

speaker: Hind
en: In the warehouse, you will find a small wooden case. It holds my beloved husband's portrait. I beg you, retrieve it for me, but do not endanger your life for anything else.

speaker: Robber
en: Useless she-worm! Tears earn no mercy!

speaker: Robber
en: Leave me in peace!

speaker: Robber
en: Keep away from me!

speaker: Robber
en: Quiet, you miserable fool! Cease your wailing!

speaker: Robber
en: Wild brutes! Do not touch me!

speaker: Robber
en: Help! Someone help me!

speaker: Robber
en: Die, wench!

speaker: Basim
en: Are you hurt?

speaker: Servant
en: I am fine, thanks to you. I owe you my life. I will not forget it. Perhaps it is time I found another role in life... Something a bit safer.

speaker: Basim
en: Hind will be relieved when I return this to her.

speaker: Hind
en: Basim! Over here!

speaker: Hind
en: Basim, I am relieved you managed to get out of there.

speaker: Basim
en: I believe this is yours.

speaker: Hind
en: Thank you. Though it is nothing compared to what these criminals have stolen from many others all across AlUla.

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me more about them? "These criminals?"

speaker: Hind
en: There has always been lawlessness here, drawn by the caravan wealth. Yet recently, that lawlessness grows more united. Now they strike wherever they please. Sometimes the Caliph's men intervene, but it never ends well for them. For that reason, few dare to act now... the rest are too faint of heart.

speaker: Basim
en: You should not stay here. The robbers might come back.

speaker: Hind
en: You are right, they usually do not leave witnesses alive... Please, Basim, take me somewhere safe.

speaker: Basim
en: Where is safe?

speaker: Hind
en: Nimlot's house. I can send word for my children to join me there. I will show you the way.

speaker: Basim
en: And I will follow.

speaker: Basim
en: The symbol on the warehouse—the vulture—what does it mean?

speaker: Hind
en: The robbers always leave that mark. To cause fear... No one opposes them and lives. Until now... Who are you, Basim?

speaker: Basim
en: Sometimes I wish I knew.

speaker: Basim
en: You said the lawlessness has been unified...

speaker: Hind
en: His name is 'Abis.

speaker: Basim
en: Abis. An unfortunate name. "The one who frowns." He must have been quite the delightful child to earn such a title from his parents.

speaker: Hind
en: He grew up here, always a thorn in our side. But now, he becomes more savage than ever.

speaker: Hind
en: I am sure Nimlot will take me in...

speaker: Basim
en: Nimlot, who is he exactly?

speaker: Hind
en: A merchant, originally from Baghdad. Made his fortune in Misr (Egypt) and settled here in AlUla a few years back. He is a good man, steadfast and generous.

speaker: Hind
en: For what it is worth, Basim, you have reignited my hope. It is time we people of AlUla fought back against the criminals.

speaker: Basim
en: Yes, but be cautious. I would not have my example cost the lives of the innocent, especially yours.

speaker: Hind
en: Basim, a moment please!

speaker: Hind
en: Basim, you have already done so much for me, but I have one last favor to ask...

speaker: Basim
en: I am listening.

speaker: Hind
en: If you happen upon any more stolen items, please bring them to me. I will see that they are returned to their rightful owners.

speaker: Basim
en: Of course. I will do what I can.

speaker: Nimlot
en: Afterwards, once you are finished, I want you to

speaker: Nimlot
en: Hind?

speaker: Hind
en: Nimlot...

speaker: Nimlot
en: What has happened?

speaker: Hind
en: The robbers... They took nearly everything.

speaker: Nimlot
en: I will send some of my men to guard your home. Meanwhile, you are welcome under my roof.

speaker: Nimlot
en: See that she is cared for.

speaker: Hind
en: May God protect you.

speaker: Basim
en: And may God protect you.

speaker: Hind
en: And if you need me, you will find me here.

speaker: Nimlot
en: You... You are one of them. I am no threat... though I am aware of your kind. My apologies, but I am in a state of abject terror being in your presence.

speaker: Basim
en: I would have guessed mere nervousness. Yet, if it comforts you, know that appearances deceive. I did not come to AlUla seeking bloodshed, even if a touch of it found me. Now, tell me, how do you know of my people?

speaker: Nimlot
en: In Baghdad, at the Caravanserai... A soap mill owner... Though there were rumors he was something more. Something... darker. I was in the city on that day. I did not witness the deed, but saw the aftermath... a throat slit, carcass hanging from a balcony.

speaker: Basim
en: Al-Ghul...

speaker: Nimlot
en: That was not the name I heard whispered.

speaker: Basim
en: More of a... description. The man you speak of was Mas'ood Al-Ya'qoob... It was a righteous kill.

speaker: Nimlot
en: I must take your word for it. May I ask your role in today's ordeal?

speaker: Basim
en: I was present and chose to intervene.

speaker: Nimlot
en: You say you were "present"...?

speaker: Basim
en: My name is Basim. I came to AlUla in search of my father, Ishaq ibn Khalid. You know him?

speaker: Nimlot
en: The name, it is familiar, but... no.

speaker: Basim
en: It has been many years since I last saw him. I have recovered one of his possessions, likely stolen from him. If he fell prey to these same robbers, I must learn all I can about them. Swiftly.

speaker: Nimlot
en: The market. It is the heartbeat of AlUla... If you intend to seek out these men, begin there.

speaker: Nimlot
en: Basim? The men you seek... are dangerous, even for you... Nevertheless, I understand you may have no choice but to tread this path. I lost a loved one recently... and I... would stop at nothing to be reunited with them.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: The chief left in a hurry. I could almost smell the fear on him.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: Maybe that is why he wears so much of his wares, huh? Anyway, come on. Time for a break.

speaker: Basim
en: This does not look good for the perfume trader, but I need more proof.

speaker: Basim
en: Now I have all the proof I need to connect the perfume trader to the bandits. I should go before they catch my scent.

speaker: Basim
en: Done to perfection.

speaker: Basim
en: Your suspicions were on the nose. The ledger and marked coins connect the perfume trader to the bandits.

speaker: The Trade Delegate
en: Good work. And I appreciate you getting the job done in a timelier fashion on this occasion.

speaker: Basim
en: The Officers' Club. Now to find a way inside.

speaker: Soldier
en: It's not enough they get their own room, but they make us guard it.

speaker: Basim
en: Locked. This must be the Officers' room. I need the key.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: They trust me with the key to their special room. That's something, right?

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: Did you see that woman whose husband we took?

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: Do not speak his name, not even here! Of all of us, he scares me the most. You know what he's like. If he learns of my past and finds fault, where can I run? I do not have the luxuries of your ships, Nadir.

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: It is your voice I hear, but the words are those of the ' (Devil) himself.

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: Do not jest. I want no trouble when he returns.

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: Where is Dogan? He is late.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: My apologies, Generals. Dogan bin Arslan has been murdered, and we fear there is an intruder. We must get you to safety.

speaker: Al-Rukh
en: I knew something was wrong! Dogan is never late.

speaker: Basim
en: Those two are with the Order, and they serve a third they call Al-Mardikhwar. But now, I need to find a way out.

speaker: Basim
en: I am safe. I should return to Fuladh.

speaker: Ali
en: This is a great beginning!

speaker: Basim
en: Why do they fight? Their Warlord lies dead already.

speaker: Rebel
en: Allah fights with us!

speaker: Basim
en: That is it. Let us get out of here.

speaker: Ali
en: Follow me. Stay close!

speaker: Basim
en: Is this what you mean by freedom? Brawling our way out of a garrison?

speaker: Ali
en: Why? Do you lack the stomach for an honest fight?

speaker: Basim
en: No, I just prefer... an honest assassination. I hope you trained your men better than the Warlord trained his.

speaker: Ali
en: Can you not see for yourself? The fight is almost over already!

speaker: Basim
en: We made it! That was close.

speaker: Ali
en: Not close, inevitable.

speaker: Ali
en: More guards! You fight with a venom. Perhaps our cause appeals to you more than you admit?

speaker: Ali
en: That is the last of them!

speaker: Basim
en: Let us go out the same way we came in.

speaker: Ali
en: Oh no, my friend. We are leaving through the front gate. Keep up! We are close. The victory is ours!

speaker: Rebel
en: We are with you, Sahib az-Zanj (Chief of the Zanj)!

speaker: Ali
en: This is a good day! I will meet you at the Bureau.

speaker: Ali
en: Our fight begins! We will have freedom, or death! God is great!

speaker: Rebel
en: There is no God but God!

speaker: Ali
en: God is great!

speaker: Rebel
en: There is no God but God!

speaker: Ali
en: God is great!

speaker: Rebel
en: There is no God but God!

speaker: Basim
en: I should return to Fuladh at the Bureau.

speaker: Fuladh
en: If you mention the cat, it will come. And here he is.

speaker: Basim
en: Go softly, come softly, so the cat does not gore you.

speaker: Ali
en: You have honored your word. Wasif lies dead, and all who hear of it, hear of me.

speaker: Basim
en: I regret we could not save Beshi. He was a brave man.

speaker: Ali
en: Already they tell his story throughout Baghdad. He will free more by his death than he did in life. Freedom has a price. The only question is whether we will pay it. Beshi was proud to. I have much to do. I would wish peace upon you both, but... we know that is not in your future. Nor mine.

speaker: Fuladh
en: I fear Ali is right. Nothing will stop his rebellion now.

speaker: Basim
en: Maybe nothing should. The things he says...

speaker: Basim
en: At the Garrison, we saw Wasif arguing with Governor Muhammad ibn Tahir.

speaker: Fuladh
en: Muhammad? That is odd. I will keep eyes on him. Araka Lahiqan! (See you later!)

speaker: Artist
en: You, stranger! Over here!

speaker: Basim
en: Well met. How may I help you?

speaker: Artist
en: I have labored on this piece for many days.

speaker: Basim
en: You have done excellent work.

speaker: Artist
en: So it seems from where I stand. To be certain, I must see how it appears from above. Perhaps you could climb that rock formation and tell me how it looks from the summit? Or find any other way to view it from on high, whatever method you prefer.

speaker: Basim
en: It will be done.

speaker: Basim
en: From a bird's-eye vantage, it appears all the more grand.

speaker: Artist
en: Help me! These leopards are upon me!

speaker: Basim
en: You are safe now.

speaker: Artist
en: Thank you. I cherish my art, but I am glad I did not have to die for it.

speaker: Basim
en: As am I. From what I have seen, the world would be a poorer place without more of your work. But I will not always be here. Next time you venture into the wild, it would be wise to bring a companion to watch your back.

speaker: Artist
en: A sound counsel. I shall heed your advice.-->

speaker: Basim
en: You are the poet with the foolish tongue?

speaker: Satiric Poet
en: My sense of outrage got the better of me. Who knew words could come at such risk?

speaker: Basim
en: Few things are more dangerous than the wounded pride of a powerful man. Lead the way and I will shield you from his wrath.

speaker: Basim
en: The course is clear.

speaker: Satiric Poet
en: That's my nephew over there. I trust him to keep my presence secret, but I fear he might take it to his grave.

speaker: Basim
en: I will release him from that conflict.

speaker: The Nephew
en: Thank you! These mercenaries surely have been the end of me.

speaker: Basim
en: The danger has passed.

speaker: Satiric Poet
en: You see those Turk sell-swords? I believe they were sent to hunt me down.

speaker: Basim
en: They certainly do not look like students of poetry. I will deal with them.

speaker: Basim
en: It is safe now.

speaker: Satiric Poet
en: Some friends will meet me here. Baraka Allahu feek. (May God bless you.) I will write a poem in your honor.

speaker: Basim
en: Poetry is like music to my ears. All the more so when I am the subject.

speaker: Satiric Poet
en: Then you shall have your music, and your valor will be remembered long after we have both passed from this earthly existence.

speaker: Basim
en: So many dead, or disappeared. And each trail of blood leads back to you. Al-Bahamut. The last mask to be lifted. You set Wasif on the rebels, unleashed Al-Ghul, sold your son's crown to seize Alamut. And all for what? Some worthless token of a long-forgotten age? No matter. I will see you at the palace. And I will cut the Head from the Snake.

speaker: Basim
en: It seems Ali decided to attack the palace after all. His rebels could distract these guards.

speaker: Rebel
en: You! Hidden One. Do you think you can help us pass these gates? They're barred from the inside.

speaker: Basim
en: You appear primed for a fight, brothers. I will see what I can do.

speaker: Basim
en: I must be quick and quiet, Qabiha will be on her guard.

speaker: Basim
en: Chaos be my friend. Mask my steps.

speaker: Basim
en: Be free my friends...and eat well.

speaker: Basim
en: Finally. Now to find Qabiha... and save Alamut.

speaker: Soldier
en: They are breaking through! We need more men!

speaker: Basim
en: Ali's rebels are at the gate.

speaker: Basim
en: Well, well. If it's not a familiar face. We have to stop meeting like this.

speaker: Makira
en: I could not agree more.

speaker: Basim
en: Where is Qabiha?

speaker: Makira
en: If I knew, I would not tell you.

speaker: Basim
en: Do not play the fool, Makira.

speaker: Makira
en: Why not? It worked the last time.

speaker: Basim
en: Do you know what Qabiha is? What she really is?

speaker: Makira
en: More than anyone. I am more child to her than her own son, that fool who let his father die before his eyes. You have no idea who you are dealing with. But I do. And I say to you kindly, leave this place.

speaker: Basim
en: Makira will warn her mistress. Let us see where she leads.

speaker: Basim
en: The library. Qabiha must be within.

speaker: Makira
en: La'nat Allah Alaik! (God curse you!) Can you not leave me alone?

speaker: Basim
en: You? Gladly. But your mistress...

speaker: Makira
en: Do what you will, you will not find her! I have nothing more to say to you.

speaker: Basim
en: There must be a room beyond this one... but how to reach it?

speaker: Basim
en: What was it Arib recited? "Rage as the ocean, I'll sweeten your storms... scorch as the desert, I'll bathe in your heat..." Many volumes by Arib. Qabiha is an admirer... Blue, Black, White and Yellow tomes...

speaker: Basim
en: Which book would Qabiha choose to mark her path? She had Arib's book in her office...

speaker: Basim
en: Someone took great effort to hide this place.

speaker: Qabiha
en: Hidden One!

speaker: Qabiha
en: So many years spent searching... Combing ancient tomes and tombs... tracing forgotten histories. Snatching at rumor and at myth. When all I needed to do was wait...

speaker: Qabiha
en: ... for you... to come to me.

speaker: Qabiha
en: Our prodigal scion... has arrived. Yet he knows not what he is. Have you not wondered at your future? You who see more, who know more...

speaker: Qabiha
en: Even my son knew to ask what you were... when he saw your hand touch and wake the Ancient's Gift.

speaker: Basim
en: What am I?

speaker: Qabiha
en: Something more than man.

speaker: Basim
en: Enough riddles, speak plainly!

speaker: Basim
en: Why speak what can be shown? Come with me to Alamut. Beneath its Temple walls lies all the knowledge that you are heir to. Your so-called brothers would sooner die...

speaker: Qabiha
en: ... than see you claim it. But take heart, Basim. We will prepare the way. And set you free.

speaker: Basim
en: No!

speaker: Roshan
en: What poison have you lapped at her lips?

speaker: Basim
en: She said I was something more than man. What did she mean, Roshan? What lies beneath the Temple?

speaker: Roshan
en: That is forbidden ground. There is nothing there for you.

speaker: Basim
en: I told you of the nightmares, the jinni- You called it weakness. Told me to mend it. I tried and tried but you hid the way- You let me struggle alone!

speaker: Roshan
en: Not alone! You are not the first to walk the shadows broken, Basim. Stitch your shattered pieces into a whole. Pour your pain into the Brotherhood. Purge yourself of the poison she dripped and come home to us. No more than a man. But no less than our brother.

speaker: Roshan
en: Or is it too little for you?

speaker: Basim
en: What if it is?

speaker: Roshan
en: Follow the path she laid out for you. And I will kill you myself.

speaker: Basim
en: They say the Harem is home to hundreds, secluded and kept from sight of men. This place may be more secret than Alamut.

speaker: Basim
en: They say no man may enter the Harem unless he is a eunuch... or the Caliph himself. I am neither, so this could be interesting.

speaker: Abbas
en: Do not even think about it. Keep walking.

speaker: Basim.
en: That was friendly. I will have to find another way in.

speaker: Farah
en: Her influence wanes, her followers dwindle by the day!

speaker: Makira
en: Qabiha is a great woman, Farah.

speaker: Farah
en: Hm, she was, while Al-Mutawakkil lived. But her son did not succeed him, and her time has come and gone.

speaker: Nasrin
en: When her tide ebbs, will you be swept with it to the sea?

speaker: Makira
en: I do not like to get involved in politics, Nasrin.

speaker: Nasrin
en: Please. We know what you are.

speaker: Farah
en: Enough. The new Eunuchs will be arriving any minute. Meet them at the gate, Makira, and try not to make a mess of it. Come, Nasrin.

speaker: Basim
en: New servants mean new faces in the Harem... If I had a Eunuch's uniform, I could slip in among them.

speaker: Basim
en: That man seems happy to bask in the sun... Perhaps I should spare him the trouble of dressing for duty.

speaker: Eunuch
en: No, no, no! Give that back!

speaker: Basim
en: We will all be naked on , brother!

speaker: Basim
en: A eunuch's uniform, freshly tailored... Perfect.

speaker: Eunuch
en: How long is this going to take? I am running late!

speaker: Civilian 1
en: I promise, not much longer, sayyidi (sir).

speaker: Basim
en: Looks ready to me!

speaker: Basim
en: That looks like a good fit. Shame someone is already wearing it.

speaker: Basim
en: Let us just move you out of the way.

speaker: Basim
en: A bit tight across the chest... and gut.

speaker: Basim
en: Hopefully this will work.

speaker: Abbas
en: Tamahhal! (Slow down!) Do I know you?

speaker: Basim
en: I doubt you would, this is my first day. I would hate to be late!

speaker: Basim
en: Makira! As-salamu 'alaikum!

speaker: Abbas
en: You know him, Makira?

speaker: Makira
en: Um. I...

speaker: Basim
en: What? You have forgotten me already?

speaker: Makira
en: No, no, I... I'm sorry, it has been a long

speaker: Basim
en: That is all right, fair one. My face is quite forgettable. Unlike your own. Farah is expecting me. Between us, she terrifies me! Please do not make me late for her.

speaker: Makira
en: Let him in, 'Abbas.

speaker: Basim
en: Baraka Allah feek (May God bless you), sayyidati (my lady).

speaker: Basim
en: Sorry, that was Greek to me!

speaker: Civilian 3
en: These are not the notes, Aisha. You have to stop.

speaker: Elder
en: You! Tell me you have read .

speaker: Basim
en: I am sorry, sayyidati (my lady).

speaker: Elder
en: Does no one read anymore?

speaker: Child
en: Why do I need to learn algebra? I am never going to need it!

speaker: Makira
en: What are you doing?

speaker: Basim
en: Makira! I was just

speaker: Makira
en: ...breaking into Qabiha's office. You are no eunuch. Leave now or I'll tell Nasrin, I'll tell Farah!

speaker: Basim
en: Tell them what? That you let me in here? I cannot imagine they will be pleased about that. You are a qahramana (stewardess), no? You serve the concubines' every need. When is the last time someone asked what you needed? Someone who would not judge. Someone you forget was ever here. There must be something you need, Makira... or want.

speaker: Makira
en: There is something. Abbas at the gate... he... he has eyes for Farah, the Umm Walad. He doesn't look at me. But Farah uses a paint to make her eyes bigger... and if I could have some, I think he might...

speaker: Basim
en: Say no more, I am at your service. Where can I find this paint?

speaker: Makira
en: The storage room, but... no one is allowed in, apart from Nasrin. Farah trusts her with everything. Even her magic potion.

speaker: Basim
en: Farah has a magic potion?

speaker: Makira
en: She has Nasrin carry it, tells her when she wants a sip. It makes her breath foul. Still, I'd give anything to try it myself!

speaker: Basim
en: And so you shall. And in exchange, Makira? What will you give me?

speaker: Makira
en: The key to that office.

speaker: Basim
en: Eye paint and magic potion. Your wish is my command!

speaker: Basim
en: Eye paint and magic potion... seriously?

speaker: Basim
en: Bigger eyes might add to my disguise... No, focus, Basim. You need the key.

speaker: Basim
en: So what is this magic potion?... Ah. I see. Alcohol.

speaker: Basim
en: Here you are.

speaker: Makira
en: Oh, thank you! The others say I'm too young for paints and potions, but I'm not too young to know why they use such things.

speaker: Basim
en: Of course not. Now, the key.

speaker: Makira
en: They only know more than me because they've all read this book, "The Garden and its Mysteries". It's all about biology, the body, its secrets. It is quite infamous. Have you read it?

speaker: Basim
en: No.

speaker: Makira
en: Farah keeps it in the Caliph's quarters, they're on the roof, and strictly forbidden.

speaker: Basim
en: Makira, we had an agreement.

speaker: Makira
en: Please! If you could just get the book and bring it to my room. It's in the east corner, on the left...

speaker: Basim
en: Fine! But then, the key!

speaker: Basim
en: Paint, potion, now she has me fetching bawdy books. I meant to play a servant, not be one.

speaker: Farah
en: Abu 'Abdallah's ambition knows no bounds.

speaker: Civilian
en: But Farah, he cannot still believe he will take the throne?

speaker: Nasrin
en: Have you met his mother?

speaker: Farah
en: You. Qabiha might have been lax about lateness, but I am not so lenient as she.

speaker: Basim
en: I am sorry Farah, it will not happen again.

speaker: Nasrin
en: Farah? To you she is sayyidati, or Umm Al-Walad. Go about your duties.

speaker: Basim
en: Quarters fit for a Caliph.

speaker: Basim
en: "The Garden and its Mysteries." Not much spice to the title. I guess that was the idea.

speaker: Basim
en: There you are. Enjoy. Let us hope she does not come up with any more tasks. I think I have created a monster...

speaker: Basim
en: The book is in your room. Now

speaker: Makira
en: So? Are my eyes bigger?

speaker: Basim
en: Huge. Makira, I need the key!

speaker: Makira
en: This potion it... it gives you confidence! I feel like I could take on the world!

speaker: Basim
en: Yes, I am... familiar with this potion. We had a bargain, Makira. The key, now.

speaker: Makira
en: Wait, you have to return the potion to Nasrin! If Farah finds out it's gone, she'll be furious! Then the key is yours, I swear!

speaker: Basim
en: Fine. Drink some water while I am gone, will you please...

speaker: Basim
en: This is the last time, Basim. Put your foot down.

speaker: Basim
en: Back where you belong. The potion is put back, all is right in the world. Now I will get that key from Makira if I have to pry it from her hands.

speaker: Poet Concubine
en: Perfect timing! I need an honest opinion on my poem. I'm having trouble with the twenty-third stanza...

speaker: Basim
en: What is a stanza?

speaker: Poet Concubine
en: Never mind. Philistine.

speaker: Basim
en: It is done! I am done!

speaker: Makira
en: Thank you! Funny, I have a bit of a headache. What happens now?

speaker: Basim
en: You give me the key.

speaker: Makira
en: Oh, right! Erm...

speaker: Basim
en: You do not have it? You are afraid of Qabiha? What?

speaker: Makira
en: No, no. Her star is fallen, they all say it. It's just... I was having fun! Here it is.

speaker: Basim
en: Finally! Now, to find my answers.

speaker: Basim
en: I remember this perfume... I smelled it in the Bazaar. And perhaps in the Harem... but on who?

speaker: Basim
en: A hairpin... Ning's. When did Qabiha get it?

speaker: Basim
en: A signed book of Arib's poems: The Ocean, the Desert, the Cobra and the Dove.

speaker: Basim
en: A map of the Caliphate... and Alamut.

speaker: Basim
en: Yet for its grandeur, the room is all but empty. Things look to be missing... including Qabiha herself.

speaker: Abbas
en: What is this? What did you give her?

speaker: Nasrin
en: She always drank from it, she asked me to give it to her. It's harmless!

speaker: Abbas
en: You call this harmless, Nasrin?

speaker: Makira
en: You should go, now. Give me the key.

speaker: Basim
en: What happened to her?

speaker: Makira
en: Me. You really shouldn't have left me alone with that flask.

speaker: Abbas
en: I'll search the rooms. You, with me.

speaker: Nasrin
en: I did nothing! I did not hurt her!

speaker: Basim
en: What did you do?

speaker: Makira
en: Relax, no one is looking at us. They will be far too busy with the book they find in Nasrin's room.

speaker: Basim
en: Nasrin's room?

speaker: Makira
en: "The Garden and its Mysteries." Nothing bawdy, just a study of native herbs, their properties medicinal, poisonous..., cosmetic. Belladonna. Deadly nightshade. It does make the eyes look lovely, in small doses. Shame I had to waste it all on her. What? You saw them, Farah and Nasrin, dripping poison in everyone's ear.
