Spreading lies and rumors about my mistress.

speaker: Basim
en: Qabiha.

speaker: Makira
en: One dead, the other disgraced. No one will hear them now.

speaker: Basim
en: Ya si'la' (treacherous hag), what are you?

speaker: Makira
en: Loyal. In Qabiha's absence I defend her throne from those who would supplant her.

speaker: Basim
en: Her office is empty. She has abandoned you, Makira. You serve a faithless mistress.

speaker: Makira
en: She will return from the Palace when the danger has passed.

speaker: Basim
en: You really should not have told me that.

speaker: Makira
en: It makes no difference. You will never find her. Now, play nice, those are children present.

speaker: Makira
en: Nice uniform, by the way. Suits you.

speaker: Basim
en: I can do nothing for Farah... but if Qabiha is the Head of the Order, I could still spare those who have yet to suffer at her hands.

speaker: Basim
en: Done to perfection. It is done.

speaker: Basim
en: That is the mark. Lead on. Show me where I need to go.

speaker: Basim
en: There you are. Just as I thought.

speaker: The Slave Merchant
en: Finally, I am here. What? The auction has not yet begun?

speaker: Rival Slave Merchant
en: Your old friend, the trapper, is still preparing his wares in the garrison.

speaker: Basim
en: The slave trapper must be in the garrison. No doubt tending to his "cargo".

speaker: Basim
en: It is done. Time to leave.

speaker: Basim
en: Done to perfection.

speaker: Basim
en: There he is. Some freed prisoners might take care of him for me.

speaker: Basim
en: It is done.

speaker: Basim
en: Well executed.

speaker: Basim
en: Time to leave.

speaker: Basim
en: There might be more information I can find around here.

speaker: Basim
en: The Tax Collector does not work alone. Someone not from Baghdad controls the strings. There is a scent on the letter... Perfume. Rose, with ... iron? Hmm.

speaker: Basim
en: Orders to increase taxes. More coin tricking into their hands.

speaker: Basim
en: The blockade at the harbor is funded by the coin of the people. I am done here. Nothing else. Roshan and Rebekah will be waiting back at the Bureau.

speaker: Basim
en: Signs of a struggle... there was violence here. Though probably not deadly violence.

speaker: Basim
en: These marks on the ground suggest someone was dragged away. A kidnapping, perhaps? Most likely the delegate was taken somewhere nearby... I must find him before it is too late.

speaker: Basim
en: Here is the spot.

speaker: The Trade Delegate
en: About time. Promptness is clearly not your strong suit.

speaker: Basim
en: Are you injured?

speaker: The Trade Delegate
en: No, I always grimace when I'm having fun.

speaker: Basim
en: The danger has passed.

speaker: Basim
en: They were keeping you alive for a reason.

speaker: The Trade Delegate
en: It seems the perfume trader you killed was not the mastermind behind all this. Instead, they intended to bring me to the person he reported to, though for what reason I do not yet know.

speaker: Basim
en: Whatever the reason, that meeting would have ended badly for you.

speaker: The Trade Delegate
en: Which is why I'm grateful for your intervention, belated though it was. Now I must go. But I will contact you soon.

speaker: The Perfume Trader
en: You have secured the merchandise? Nothing has been tampered with?

speaker: Soldier
en: Everything is locked down tight.

speaker: The Perfume Trader
en: Keep your eyes open for anything suspicious!

speaker: Soldier
en: Calm yourself. We are professionals.

speaker: Basim
en: A bloody end to some bad happenings. Well executed.

speaker: Basim
en: Beshi sent me. I am here to help you to safety.

speaker: The Weapons Dealer
en: I do not know you. Am I just meant to take you at your word?

speaker: Basim
en: Do you have a choice?

speaker: The Weapons Dealer
en: Fine. I know a way out of the city. And remember, I have eyes in the back of my head in case you plan to stab me from behind.

speaker: Basim
en: Look, a threat to be met. Preferably by you.

speaker: Basim
en: The course is clear.

speaker: The Weapons Dealer
en: There's trouble ahead.

speaker: Basim
en: The course is clear.

speaker: The Weapons Dealer
en: Have you know the rebels long?

speaker: Basim
en: Long enough to believe in their cause.

speaker: The Weapons Dealer
en: Look, a threat to be met. Preferably by you.

speaker: Basim
en: The course is clear.

speaker: The Weapons Dealer
en: We are safe now. You have my thanks ... and my trust.

speaker: Basim
en: A fine finish.

speaker: Basim
en: This is the harbor. Now to find Admiral Nadir.

speaker: Basim
en: This is a detailed diagram of a strange-looking ship.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: The Admiral has a secret fear.

speaker: Soldier 2
en: I doubt we'll see the Admiral at the harbor today. He's busy working on more of his precious model ships.

speaker: Soldier 1
en: Do you know why he's afraid of fire? When he was boy, he tried to steal a sip from a bubbling pot of stew. His hair caught fire. They almost couldn't put it out.

speaker: Basim
en: A note directing all shipments to a location just south along the river Tigris.

speaker: Basim
en: This shipment is headed outside the city.

speaker: Soldier 3
en: It's just my luck to be sent to the biggest dung pile in all of Sharqiyah.

speaker: Soldier 4
en: This camp is the worst I've ever seen in all my years as a soldier. Rats live better.

speaker: Basim
en: Admiral Nadir is very concerned about keeping fire away from his prototype ship.

speaker: Soldier 5
en: The admiral is all talk. I've never heard bluster so much and do so little. Not even you.

speaker: Soldier 6
en: Shut up! If the Admiral doesn't beat you to stop your complaining, I will.

speaker: Soldier 7
en: The Admiral cares more for tis precious model ship than his own men, and look at it. I'm surprised it floats.

speaker: Basim
en: It would be a pity if that little ship caught fire.

speaker: Soldier
en: No, no no! Put it out! Hurry! He'll take our heads!

speaker: Basim
en: A letter from Al-Mardikhwar about missing shipments belonging to the Turkic mercenaries. The Admiral was stealing.

speaker: Basim
en: That is two down. I should return to Fuladh.

speaker: Merchant
en: Come! Please! I have urgent work for you!

speaker: Basim
en: How may I serve you?

speaker: Merchant
en: My son is to be .

speaker: Basim
en: Surely congratulations are in order?

speaker: Merchant
en: Alas, your goodwill may prove premature. I pledged the gift to the bride's father, a token of honor for our families. But earlier today, robbers fell upon us and seized the valuables, sharing them among their three chiefs.

speaker: Basim
en: You would have me recover your son's gift?

speaker: Merchant
en: Without it, the wedding contract is void. I would bring shame upon myself, and my son's joy would be shattered. The robbers' camp lies in the Southern Wilderness. If you can, do not draw attention to yourself. A subtle theft would serve us best.

speaker: Basim
en: I must try to relieve the three chiefs of their treasures with subtle hands.

speaker: Basim
en: I recovered the valuables, and no one is the wiser.

speaker: Merchant
en: That is wonderful news. You have my eternal gratitude. As a token of my thanks, and atop the agreed fee, allow me to offer you my eldest daughter's hand in marriage. She is a worthy woman. Though still mourning her first husband, her skill at the hearth is unmatched.

speaker: Basim
en: Shukran laka (Thank you, madame), but my vices are many. I would make for a poor husband and a worse son-in-law.

speaker: Merchant
en: As you wish. But do not be too hard on yourself! A few vices aside, you are clearly a man of quality.

speaker: Basim
en: My father has been taken. To find him, I must journey into the north of AlUla. But who leads the robbers now? With 'Abis dead... I wonder who this "real chief" may be?

speaker: Basim
en: I should remain alert to ambushes...

speaker: Basim
en: That smoke... I should investigate.

speaker: Trader 1
en: Please! Show pity! (screams)

speaker: Trader 2
en: Kill me, but spare my wife!

speaker: Trader 2
en: Have mercy on me!

speaker: Robber
en: We've got everything! Time to go! Move out!

speaker: Trader 1
en: I beg of you, stranger! I need your aid!

speaker: Trader 1
en: The robbers who attacked us stole everything, and we must now learn to live without.

speaker: Basim
en: Tell me, from where did these robbers come?

speaker: Trader 1
en: They suddenly appeared from the nearby canyon.

speaker: Basim
en: There is something here... I should follow these tracks. They might lead me to my prey...

speaker: Basim
en: This seems to be the right way...

speaker: Robber 2
en: You are surrounded, dog!

speaker: Basim
en: Oh? Yet you are the ones about to die!

speaker: Basim
en: This must be one of the robbers' hideouts. There could be useful information here to help me find my father.

speaker: Robber 3
en: Those wandering traders walked into this land carrying . And now they walk out empty-handed.

speaker: Robber 4
en: Not all of them will be walking out. Only the lucky few.

speaker: Basim
en: I should look at this more closely.

speaker: Basim
en: These symbols... It seems the robbers use them to communicate. I must investigate further.

speaker: Basim
en: This is helpful. I should check this area. It appears I have found one of the robbers' secret lairs. Perhaps there is a clue there that will lead me to my father.

speaker: Basim
en: Interesting... That explains much.

speaker: Basim
en: Soon enough I shall have my answers. Until then, I must remain focused.

speaker: Basim
en: If only I could understand what I did so grievously wrong. Or... perhaps... you deemed my very birth the error?

speaker: Basim
en: Father, why did you abandon me all those years past? Steady yourself, Basim. You are a man now, not a boy.

speaker: Basim
en: This looks like a hidden den of the robbers. Maybe I will find the information I need to locate my father.

speaker: Robber 1
en: Has he no shame? Stealing from his own brothers? There must be honor among thieves.

speaker: Robber 2
en: Rest easy. That dirty traitor dog is locked up tight while we decide his fate.

speaker: Robber 1
en: Who holds the key to his cage? Is it you?

speaker: Robber 2
en: No, I left it with Ahmad.

speaker: Renegade robber
en: Release me with the key and I will help you.

speaker: Basim
en: This traitor they spoke of may hold useful secrets. And this key might help loosen his tongue...

speaker: Renegade robber
en: You look like you're after some answers. Perhaps we can strike a bargain?

speaker: Basim
en: You will have your bargain if you answer my questions. But how do I know you will not alert the camp the moment I free you, just to regain favor with your old friends?

speaker: Renegade robber
en: Speak your questions, and we shall see.

speaker: Basim
en: That is not exactly reassuring.

speaker: Renegade robber
en: Do you want answers or not?

speaker: Basim
en: I seek an old man, recently taken from the oasis...

speaker: Renegade robber
en: Old man? Yes, I know the one, I helped capture him just the other day.

speaker: Basim
en: On whose orders? 'Abis is dead—mine was the last face he saw.

speaker: Renegade robber
en: Abis? He was never our true chief. He answered to Nimlot.

speaker: Basim
en: Nimlot? He commands your band of cutthroats?

speaker: Renegade robber
en: That's right. Though I've now parted from them, as you can see.

speaker: Basim
en: Do you know where the old man is held?

speaker: Renegade robber
en: It's hard to explain, but you will find it marked on this map. The place serves as Nimlot's base. All we steal goes there, then is sold off by a network of friendly merchants. To gain entry, you will need a whistle. You will find one upon that table. To pass as one of us, blow upon the whistle when you are standing close to the site. Now, hurry up and set me free.

speaker: Renegade robber
en: You are a rare man of honor. Much like myself.

speaker: Basim
en: I possess all that is needed to rescue my father. Only Nimlot stands in my way... So, Nimlot has been my enemy all along. How could I have been so naïve? But why take my father? Unless he hopes to use him as bait.

speaker: Tiferet
en: Open up, you stupid door!

speaker: Tiferet
en: What are you gawking at?

speaker: Basim
en: You sound like someone in need of help.

speaker: Tiferet
en: I will take it when I can.

speaker: Basim
en: Then I shall offer it. What is the problem?

speaker: Tiferet
en: This house belonged to my mother before she passed away. It holds an object of great value. A treasure you might say.

speaker: Basim
en: A treasure?

speaker: Tiferet
en: Hah! Suddenly he's all years.

speaker: Basim
en: Treasure intrigues me, but it does not rule my heart. Nor my ears.

speaker: Tiferet
en: Anyway, unless I find a way inside, the treasure is lost forever.

speaker: Basim
en: As a child I was quite the treasure hunter. Now is as good a time as any to renew that interest.

speaker: Tiferet
en: For a fee? So be it. After the job is complete.

speaker: Basim
en: Where exactly will I find this treasure?

speaker: Tiferet
en: My mother, a potter by trade, hid it inside a blue amphora.

speaker: Basim
en: Lusterware? That is a treasure in itself.

speaker: Tiferet
en: After her death, my grief was great, and I could not bring myself to enter the house and claim my birthright. Now I return only to find the place has sunk... Please, bring me what is mine.

speaker: Basim
en: Your birthright shall be restored.

speaker: Tiferet
en: Have you found the amphora yet?

speaker: Basim
en: Hopefully the damp has not damaged the treasure.

speaker: Basim
en: Here is the amphora... No way to open it other than to break it. Whatever it contains must be of great value.

speaker: Basim
en: So much for your mother's fine work.

speaker: Basim
en: And since when was a lump of copper considered a great treasure?

speaker: Tiferet
en: Your ignorance betrays you. With this copper I will make a hundred lusterware vases. Now, here is your fee. And a little extra for not running off with my treasure when you had the chance.

speaker: Tiferet
en: Ha, was it greed or clumsiness that led you to breaking the amphora?

speaker: Basim
en: If I had not broken it, you would have. There was no other way to open it. And besides, since when was a lump of copper considered to be a great treasure?

speaker: Tiferet
en: Your ignorance betrays you. With this copper I will make a hundred lusterware vases. Now, here is your fee. Minus a small forfeiture for breaking my mother's amphora. It held sentimental value, you know.

speaker: Dervis
en: Basim! Finally.

speaker: Basim
en: Have you missed me that much?

speaker: Dervis
en: I have something to show you.

speaker: Basim
en: Where did you find this?

speaker: Dervis
en: A merchant passed through, selling some items. Most stolen, I suspect. But this painting caught my eye. It reminded me of your brooch.

speaker: Basim
en: Samarra...

speaker: Dervis
en: Do you think your father painted it?

speaker: Basim
en: He and I loved this house deeply... Where did the Bedouin find it?

speaker: Dervis
en: He said he bought the painting in AlUla, from a notorious peddler of stolen goods.

speaker: Basim
en: AlUla? When I was a boy, my father read me stories of that ancient land and its mysterious monuments... He said we would go there together, when I was old enough to make the journey. I have not seen my father in many years. Not since the day he was exiled by the Khalifa. The day he left me behind.

speaker: Dervis
en: Sometimes the past chases us.

speaker: Basim
en: Dervis, what if my father is still alive? I must go to AlUla.

speaker: Dervis
en: You will likely be crossing a to visit a grave... Still, I understand your need to make the journey. I know the place quite well, having previously travelled there on matters of commerce...

speaker: Basim
en: You will accompany me, then?

speaker: Dervis
en: Whatever you face, Basim, I will not let you do so alone. Now, are you ready to uncover the truth about your father?

speaker: Basim
en: I am ready.

speaker: Basim
en: I am not sure what scares me more, finding my father's resting place or finding nothing at all.

speaker: Dervis
en: Remember, it is foolish to deny the past, yet also unwise to surrender to it. Better to face it, accept it... and move on.

speaker: Basim
en: First, we go to the cemetery. If my father's grave truly lies there, I need to see it with my own eyes.

speaker: Dervis
en: It has been a long journey, Basim. Let us take the time to rest. We can go in the morning.

speaker: Basim
en: You are right... Tomorrow shall yield its answers, whatever they may be.

speaker: Basim
en: Surely this is the market Nimlot spoke of.

speaker: Merchant
en: Please, behold the wares I have on offer. Take a look. I promise you will find my wares most inviting.

speaker: Basim
en: What a splendid market you have here. Treasures at every turn!

speaker: Merchant
en: We do our best, though it cannot compare to Baghdad.

speaker: Basim
en: I am glad of it. I came here to escape Baghdad, if only for a while.

speaker: Merchant
en: In that case, you will find AlUla offers much to discover. Still, we harbor our share of shadows...

speaker: Basim
en: Such as?

speaker: Merchant
en: Venture beyond that path with caution... They say it leads to the black heart of this market, where ugly desires find purchase.

speaker: Basim
en: His garb mirrors that of the robbers I met earlier. I must follow him.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps I should check his pockets for any clues...

speaker: Basim
en: It is a list of hidden spots where the robbers keep their weapons. There are many... even inside the Musa ibn Nusayr Fort.

speaker: Guard
en: Stop right there, dog!

speaker: Guard 2
en: Do not let him get away!

speaker: Basim
en: What is happening over there?

speaker: Robber
en: Off with you!

speaker: Basim
en: I cannot let them get to him first. My only chance to question him depends on it!

speaker: Basim
en: I was not swift enough. Enkidu, will you help me again, friend?

speaker: Merchant
en: This burnt-bean brew offends the tongue!

speaker: Coffee merchant
en: You know nothing of fine flavor!

speaker: Coffee merchant
en: Greetings! Would you care to sample the wine of the bean?

speaker: Basim
en: Wine of the bean? What manner of drink is this?

speaker: Coffee merchant
en: It is drawn from the of a that grows far to the south.

speaker: Basim
en: And what virtue does it hold?

speaker: Coffee merchant
en: It and kindles the body. One draught and weariness is driven off.

speaker: Basim
en: You speak with great confidence.

speaker: Coffee merchant
en: Perhaps you will permit a taste?

speaker: Basim
en: It is sharp upon the tongue.

speaker: Coffee merchant
en: Its true flavor unfolds with time.

speaker: Basim
en: Perhaps a touch of milk might temper its edge?

speaker: Coffee merchant
en: Preposterous! None in their right mind would taint the brew in such a manner.-->

speaker: Basim
en: Roshan and Fuladh will want to hear of these developments.

speaker: Fuladh
en: If I were in Ali's position I would do the same. An army is only as powerful as its weakest soldier.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: As-salamu 'alaikum (Peace be upon you), Basim!

speaker: Basim
en: Wa 'alaikum as-salam (And peace be upon you), Ahmad. How was your journey?

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: I am Abu Jafar.

speaker: Basim
en: Right. My apologies.

speaker: Basim
en: Is there a problem?.

speaker: Roshan
en: Not yet. But we've discovered Ali was brokering a deal with Nur to supply the rebels with resources in exchange for his help.

speaker: Fuladh
en: The Order is a thorn in his side, yes, but Ali has his sights set on the Caliphate. He will want us to honor this deal.

speaker: Roshan
en: What news do you bring?

speaker: Basim
en: Our target is Al-Ghul. He uses prisoners and laborers to dig around Baghdad. Ali and some of his men were captured and marked. With Beshi's help I freed them, but Ali had been taken elsewhere for questioning.

speaker: Basim
en: One of the rebels showed me his mark. If this list of captives is correct, Ali was sent to the Damascus Gate Prison.

speaker: Roshan
en: Where are these rebels now?

speaker: Basim
en: A watermill on the northern outskirts.

speaker: Roshan
en: I will meet with them. See what more I can learn about this deal. Find Ali.

speaker: Fuladh
en: The Damascus Gate Prison is the most well-guarded prison in Baghdad. This will prove to be no small challenge, I can tell you. I will scout ahead. Meet me near the prison's front gate.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: A moment of your time before you go, Basim? I have some useful thoughts to share.

speaker: Basim
en: You have my ears.

speaker: Abu Jafar Muhammad
en: First, I have fashioned a board with information brought to us by our spies around the city. Consult it at your leisure. Second, these lands are ripe with materials to improve your weapons. See the blacksmith Jawar nearby. He could help you. And lastly, I am your man for any tool enhancement. Bring me materials, and you will see what mastery I can provide.

speaker: Basim
en: Resourceful as always. My thanks, Abu Jafar.
